A commit log is a crash-recovery journal, not a replica — it can't substitute for having multiple copies of data across machines.
SSTables are precisely the immutable files meant to live on disk — saying they can only exist in memory has it backwards.

scenario: 一个 key 不在 memtable 中。磁盘上有很多 SSTable，逐个查会带来大量随机 I/O。
scenario_en: A key is not in the memtable. Many SSTables exist on disk, and checking each one would cause many random I/Os.
q: 读路径用 Bloom filter 的目的是什么？
q_en: Why use a Bloom filter in the read path?
options: 快速判断某个 SSTable 是否可能包含 key
保证每一次读到的 value 永远都是最新版本
把 value 自动解压成对象
替代数据库索引和缓存
options_en: Quickly tell whether an SSTable may contain the key
Guarantee the value read is always the newest version
Automatically decompress values into objects
Replace all indexes and caches
why: 这张卡考的是读放大控制。Bloom filter 用很小的内存换少量误判，把多数无关 SSTable 从磁盘读路径里剪掉。
why_en: This controls read amplification: a Bloom filter uses small memory and accepts some false positives to avoid many irrelevant SSTable checks.
tradeoff: 少读磁盘 vs 少量误判
whenOtherWins: 如果 SSTable 数量很少，直接查索引可能已经足够简单。

termDefinitions.meaning: 空间很省的概率集合结构；可能误报存在，但不会误报不存在。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Bloom filter is a space-efficient probabilistic set that may return false positives but not false negatives.

optionExplanations: 对，先问一句“这个文件里有没有可能有这个 key”，答案是否定的文件直接跳过，真正要打开逐一核对的候选就少了很多。
它答的是“可能在”还是“肯定不在”这道判断题，跟哪个版本才是最新写入完全是另一回事，读到的新鲜度不归它管。
解压 value 是序列化/反序列化的工作，跟“要不要打开这个文件去找 key”是完全不同的判断。
它省的只是磁盘查找这一步，数据库该有的完整索引能力、或者缓存层该扛的访问加速，都不是它能顶上的。
optionExplanations_en: Right — it first asks "could this key possibly be in this file," and any file that answers no gets skipped outright, leaving far fewer candidates that actually need opening and checking.
It only answers "maybe present" versus "definitely not" — which version is the newest write is an entirely separate question that freshness doesn't fall under its job.
Decompressing a value is a serialization concern, a completely different question from whether this file is even worth opening to look for the key.
All it saves is that one disk-lookup step — it's no substitute for a database's real indexing, nor for the access-speed job a caching layer is meant to carry.

q: KV 磁盘读路径的顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the order of the KV disk read path?
steps: 如果内存没有，查询 Bloom filter 找可能包含 key 的 SSTable
先查 memtable 或内存缓存
从候选 SSTable 读取数据
把找到的结果返回给客户端
why: 读路径先走最快的内存。只有 miss 后才用 Bloom filter 缩小磁盘候选集合。
why_en: The read path checks memory first, then uses Bloom filters to narrow the disk search.

q: 去中心化 KV 节点通常承担哪些职责？
q_en: What responsibilities do decentralized KV nodes usually carry?
options: 作为客户端请求的 coordinator
参与一致性哈希环的分片归属
保存和复制部分 key-value 数据
只做无状态 HTTP 静态文件服务
options_en: Act as a coordinator for client requests
Own key ranges on the consistent-hashing ring
Store and replicate some key-value data
Only serve stateless HTTP files
why: 去中心化设计里节点职责对称，避免单点。每个节点既能接请求，也参与路由、存储、复制和故障处理。
why_en: In a decentralized KV store, nodes share routing, storage, replication, coordination, and failure-handling duties to avoid single points.

termDefinitions.meaning: 接收客户端请求并协调目标副本读写的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A coordinator receives client requests and coordinates reads or writes across target replicas.

optionExplanations: 对，客户端请求可以打到任意节点，这个节点要临时充当 coordinator，找到真正负责这个 key 的副本集合。
对，去中心化节点同样要参与一致性哈希环，知道自己和其他节点各自负责环上哪一段。
对，每个节点本身也要保存并复制一部分 key-value 数据，不只是转发请求。
去中心化 KV 节点要同时承担路由、存储、复制等多种职责，只做无状态静态文件服务和这套对称职责模型完全不符。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a client request can land on any node, and that node temporarily acts as coordinator, locating the actual replica set responsible for the key.
Right — decentralized nodes also take part in the consistent-hash ring, knowing which segment they and their peers each own.
Right — every node also holds and replicates a portion of the key-value data itself, not just forwards requests.
A decentralized KV node juggles routing, storage, and replication all at once — being a stateless static-file server alone doesn't match that symmetric-duty model at all.
scenario: 一个无主的分布式 KV 集群要求任何节点都能直接接客户端请求，不允许存在专职 master。
scenario_en: A leaderless distributed KV cluster needs any node to serve client requests directly, with no dedicated master.

scenario: KV 有同样的 N=3 副本。你在比较 R=1/W=N 和 W=1/R=N。
scenario_en: A KV store has N=3 replicas. You are comparing R=1/W=N with W=1/R=N.
q: 这两个 quorum 配置的差别是什么？
q_en: How do these two quorum settings differ?
options: 前者优化读延迟，后者优化写延迟
前者无副本，后者有副本
前者只能 CP，后者只能 CA
前者只能用于缓存，后者只能用于数据库
options_en: The first optimizes read latency; the second optimizes write latency
The first has no replicas; the second has replicas
The first is only CP; the second is only CA
The first is only for caches; the second only for databases
why: R=1 读只等一个副本，所以读快；W=1 写只等一个副本，所以写快。两者都是把等待成本挪到另一条路径上。
why_en: R=1 makes reads fast, while W=1 makes writes fast; each shifts waiting cost to the other path.
tradeoff: 读等待 vs 写等待
whenOtherWins: 如果读写比例接近，还要同时考虑 W+R>N 和尾延迟。
optionExplanations: 对，R=1 让读只等一个副本所以读快，W=1 让写只等一个副本所以写快，两种配置都是把等待成本挪到了另一条路径上。
两种配置的副本数量是一样的，差别只在于读写各自要等多少个副本确认，跟“有没有副本”无关。
R 和 W 的取值只是调节等待成本和一致性概率，不会决定系统只能做 CP 还是只能做 CA，这个判断过头了。
这两种 quorum 配置都是通用的一致性调节手段，缓存和数据库都能用，不存在只能用于某一种场景的限制。
optionExplanations_en: Right — R=1 makes reads wait on just one replica so reads are fast, and W=1 makes writes wait on just one replica so writes are fast; each configuration shifts the waiting cost onto the other path.
Both configurations have the same replica count — the difference is only how many replicas reads and writes each wait for, unrelated to whether replicas exist.
R and W values just tune waiting cost and the odds of freshness — they don't lock the system into being only CP or only CA; that's overreaching.
Both quorum configurations are general consistency knobs usable by either caches or databases — there's no restriction limiting either one to a single use case.

scenario: 某个热门 key 被很多节点先后写入，向量时钟里的 [server, counter] 项越来越多。系统设置长度阈值，超过就删最旧的项。
scenario_en: A hot key is written by many servers, so its vector clock accumulates many [server, counter] entries. The system caps length and drops oldest entries.
q: 截断向量时钟的风险是什么？
q_en: What is the risk of truncating vector clocks?
options: 可能无法准确判断祖先关系，合并变低效
value 会立刻丢失
所有副本都会因此彻底停止接收读请求
哈希环会重新排序
options_en: It may lose causal information and make reconciliation less accurate
The value is immediately lost
All replicas stop serving reads because of it
The hash ring is reordered
why: 删掉旧计数会丢因果线索。系统可能把能自动覆盖的版本当成冲突，增加读修复和客户端合并成本。
why_en: Dropping old counters loses causality, so the system may treat clean descendants as conflicts and require extra reconciliation.
optionExplanations: 对，删掉最旧的 [server, counter] 项等于丢掉了那部分因果线索，系统可能没法准确判断谁是谁的祖先，合并逻辑会因此变得低效或出错。
截断向量时钟不涉及删除 value 本身，丢失的是判断版本关系的元数据，不是数据内容。
截断向量时钟是版本元数据层面的问题，不会导致所有副本停止接收读请求这么剧烈的后果。
截断向量时钟跟哈希环上节点的排列顺序完全是两个不相关的机制，不会引发环重新排序。
optionExplanations_en: Right — dropping the oldest [server, counter] entries throws away that piece of causal history, so the system may no longer be able to tell ancestry accurately, and merging becomes less efficient or outright wrong.
Truncating the vector clock doesn't delete the value itself — what's lost is the metadata for judging version relationships, not the data content.
Truncating vector clocks is a versioning-metadata issue — it doesn't cause anything as drastic as every replica refusing reads.
Truncating vector clocks and the ordering of nodes on the hash ring are two entirely unrelated mechanisms — it doesn't trigger the ring reordering.

scenario: KV 服务全国用户，一个数据中心可能因灾害完全离线。业务要求核心数据仍可从其他地区访问。
scenario_en: The KV service serves national users, and one data center may go fully offline; core data must remain accessible elsewhere.
q: 机房级故障的核心设计是什么？
q_en: What is the core design for data-center-level failure?
options: 跨多个数据中心复制数据
把所有副本放进最大机房
只备份配置，不备份数据
只依赖客户端重试
options_en: Replicate data across multiple data centers
Put all replicas in the largest data center
Back up only configuration, not data
Rely only on client retries
why: 机房级故障要让数据提前存在于其他机房。客户端重试只换入口，不会凭空生成丢失的副本。
why_en: Surviving a data-center outage requires data to already exist in another site; retries alone cannot recreate missing replicas.
tradeoff: 容灾冗余 vs 跨机房复制成本
whenOtherWins: 如果只是开发环境或可重建缓存，单机房部署可以省成本。
optionExplanations: 数据要提前存在于其他机房，这个机房出问题时其他地方才有完整数据可读，这是唯一能真正扛住机房级故障的路径。
把所有副本都放进同一个最大机房，那个机房一旦整体离线，副本再多也一起没了，没有解决跨机房容灾的问题。
只备份配置不备份数据，意味着机房故障后配置能恢复，但真正的业务数据仍然是丢的。
客户端重试只是换一个入口重新尝试，如果数据本来就没有存在于其他机房，重试再多次也读不到。
optionExplanations_en: Data needs to already exist in other datacenters ahead of time, so when one goes down, the others still have a complete copy to serve — the only path that actually survives a facility-level failure.

Putting every replica in the single biggest datacenter means that when that one facility goes entirely offline, all the replicas go down with it — it doesn't address cross-datacenter disaster recovery at all.
Backing up only configuration and not data means config can be restored after an outage, but the actual business data is still gone.
Client retries just try a different entry point — if the data was never replicated elsewhere to begin with, no number of retries will find it.

scenario: KV 存储 session、配置、购物车等不同对象。存储层只需要按 key 读写，不需要理解 value 里的字段。
scenario_en: A KV store holds sessions, configs, and carts. The storage layer only needs get/put by key and does not inspect fields inside values.
q: value 应该被存储层如何对待？
q_en: How should the storage layer treat the value?
options: 当作不透明字节或对象保存
拆成关系表并做 JOIN
要求所有 value 都是 SQL 行
只允许整数 value
options_en: Store it as opaque bytes or an opaque object
Normalize it into relational tables and JOIN
Require every value to be a SQL row
Allow only integer values
why: KV 的简单性来自 key 到 opaque value 的查找。存储层不理解字段，换来接口简单和通用性，但也失去复杂查询能力。
why_en: KV stores stay simple by treating values as opaque payloads, gaining generality while giving up rich querying.
tradeoff: 简单通用接口 vs 复杂查询能力
whenOtherWins: 如果必须按 value 内部字段过滤、聚合、JOIN，关系型或文档数据库更合适。

termDefinitions.meaning: 存储系统不解析内部结构的 value，只负责保存和返回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An opaque value is stored and returned without the storage system interpreting its internal structure.

optionExplanations: 把 value 当成不透明字节或对象存起来，存储层不用理解里面的字段，接口就能保持简单和通用，session、配置、购物车都能用同一套 get/put。
拆成关系表并做 JOIN 意味着存储层要理解字段结构，这已经是关系数据库的思路，违背了 KV 只按 key 查值的简单性。
要求所有 value 都是 SQL 行，会强行给不同形态的对象套上同一种结构，跟 KV 存任意对象的初衷相反。
只允许整数 value 完全没法承载 session、配置这类天然是复杂结构的数据，限制过头了。
optionExplanations_en: Treating the value as an opaque blob or object means the storage layer never needs to understand its internal fields, keeping the interface simple enough that sessions, config, and carts can all share the same get/put.

Splitting into relational tables and doing JOINs requires the storage layer to understand field structure — that's already relational-database thinking, working against KV's simplicity of just looking up by key.
Forcing every value to be a SQL row forces oddly-shaped objects into one rigid structure, working against the whole point of a KV store holding arbitrary objects.
Allowing only integer values can't hold naturally complex data like sessions or configs at all — far too restrictive.

scenario: 一个 KV 追求高写入吞吐。写入先追加日志、进内存表，之后批量刷成不可变有序文件；读取需要从多个文件里找 key。
scenario_en: A KV store targets high write throughput. Writes append to a log, enter an in-memory table, then flush into immutable sorted files; reads must find keys across files.
q: 这类 LSM 风格路径的核心取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the core tradeoff of this LSM-style path?
options: 写入顺序化更快，但读取和后台整理更复杂
读取路径永远只需要查询一个文件就够了
写入必须随机改磁盘页
不需要崩溃恢复
options_en: Sequential writes are faster, but reads and background maintenance are more complex
The read path always checks exactly one file
Writes must randomly update disk pages
Crash recovery is unnecessary
why: 顺序追加和内存缓冲让写路径快。代价是读路径要靠 Bloom filter、索引和 compaction 控制多文件查找。
why_en: Sequential append and memory buffering speed writes, while reads need Bloom filters, indexes, and compaction to control file fanout.
tradeoff: 写吞吐 vs 读放大
whenOtherWins: 如果读极多且写少，B-tree 类原地更新索引可能更容易控制读延迟。

termDefinitions.meaning: 写优化存储结构，把写入批量落成不可变有序文件，再后台合并。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSM tree is a write-optimized storage structure that flushes writes into immutable sorted files and compacts them later.

termDefinitions.meaning: 后台合并 SSTable、清理旧版本或删除标记的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Compaction is the background process of merging SSTables and removing obsolete versions or tombstones.

optionExplanations: 顺序追加加内存缓冲让写路径几乎不用随机改磁盘，代价转移到了读这一侧——要靠多个文件查找和后台整理来兜底。
一次读要跨多个不可变文件查找同一个 key 的历史版本，说“永远只查一个文件”不符合这类结构的实际读路径。
这条路径的核心正是把随机写变成顺序追加，说写入必须随机改磁盘页正好说反了。
崩溃恢复要靠先写的那份日志重放，不是可以省略的步骤，说不需要崩溃恢复不符合这套设计。
optionExplanations_en: Sequential appends plus an in-memory buffer keep the write path almost entirely free of random disk writes — the cost shifts onto the read side, which has to search multiple files and rely on background cleanup.
A single read has to search across multiple immutable files for a key's history, so claiming it "always queries just one file" doesn't match how this kind of path actually reads.
The whole point of this path is turning random writes into sequential appends — saying writes must randomly modify disk pages has it exactly backwards.
Crash recovery depends on replaying that log written first — it isn't a step this design can skip, so saying it needs no crash recovery doesn't fit.

scenario: KV 集群按 key 分片。某个业务想把所有用户都写到 key 前缀 user:，只有后缀不同。
scenario_en: A KV cluster shards by key. One service writes all users under the prefix user:, with only suffixes differing.
q: 分区键设计最怕什么？
q_en: What is the main partition-key risk?
options: 低基数或偏斜 key 会制造热分区
key 取得越短就一定会分布得越均匀
所有前缀都会自动分散
副本数会修复所有写热点
options_en: Low-cardinality or skewed keys create hot partitions
Shorter keys are always more balanced
All prefixes automatically spread
Replication fixes every write hotspot
why: 分片看的是哈希输入的有效差异。低基数或业务偏斜会让流量集中到少数分区。
why_en: Sharding depends on useful key variability; low-cardinality or skewed keys concentrate traffic on a few partitions.
tradeoff: 查询局部性 vs 写入分散
whenOtherWins: 如果查询总是按某个前缀批量读取，保留前缀局部性可能更重要，但要配合拆热点。

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个分片收到远高于平均水平的请求或数据量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot partition receives much more traffic or data than average.

optionExplanations: 哈希看的是输入本身有没有足够差异，如果几乎所有 key 都共享同一个前缀、只有后缀不同，流量还是会集中到少数几个分区。
key 短不代表哈希输入的有效差异就大，长度和分布均匀度是两回事，说“越短就一定越均匀”没有依据。
前缀相同、只有后缀不同的这批 key 恰恰不会自动分散，这正是低基数或偏斜 key 制造热分区的原因。
副本数量解决的是容错和读写扩展问题，跟分片本身是否均匀是两个独立的维度，不会自动修复写热点。
optionExplanations_en: Sharding depends on how much real difference exists in the input; if nearly every key shares the same prefix and differs only in the suffix, traffic still concentrates onto a handful of partitions.
A shorter key doesn't mean more effective variance for hashing — length and distribution evenness are separate things, so "shorter is always more even" has no basis.
Keys sharing the same prefix with only the suffix varying are exactly what fails to spread out automatically — that's the cause of low-cardinality or skewed keys creating hot partitions.
Replica count addresses fault tolerance and read/write scaling, a separate dimension from whether sharding itself is balanced — it doesn't automatically fix a write hot spot.

scenario: 客户端把 put(key,value) 发给任意一个 KV 节点。该节点不一定是 key 的副本之一。
scenario_en: A client sends put(key,value) to any KV node, which may not be one of the key’s replicas.
q: coordinator 节点负责什么？
q_en: What does the coordinator node do?
options: 根据 key 找副本集合，并收集足够读写响应
在本地永久保存所有 key 的主副本数据
只做 DNS 解析
替客户端合并 UI 页面
options_en: Find the replica set for the key and collect enough read/write responses
Permanently store the primary copy of every key locally
Only perform DNS resolution
Merge UI pages for the client
why: coordinator 是请求代理。它按分片规则找目标副本，再按 R 或 W 等待足够响应。
why_en: The coordinator proxies the request: it finds target replicas and waits for enough responses according to R or W.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 KV 集群里接收客户端请求并协调副本读写的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A coordinator receives client requests and coordinates replica reads and writes in a KV cluster.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把域名解析成网络地址的系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS maps domain names to network addresses.

optionExplanations: 对，coordinator 按分片规则算出这个 key 该由哪几个副本负责，再等到 R 或 W 要求的副本数量都回应了，才把结果返回给客户端。
coordinator 只是临时转发请求的代理角色，不是某个 key 的固定主副本，也不会永久持有所有 key 的主副本。
coordinator 要理解分片规则、转发请求、收集响应，这些都不是 DNS 解析能完成的工作。
coordinator 处理的是存储层的读写请求，跟客户端 UI 页面怎么合并展示完全不是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the coordinator computes which replicas own this key according to the sharding rule, then waits until the number required by R or W have responded before returning a result to the client.
The coordinator is just a temporary relay for the request, not a fixed primary for any given key, and it doesn't permanently hold the primary copy of every key.
A coordinator has to understand sharding rules, forward requests, and collect responses — none of which DNS resolution does.
A coordinator handles storage-layer read/write requests, an entirely different concern from how a client merges and displays a UI page.

scenario: KV 支持按请求选择一致性级别。一个读取可以只等一个副本，也可以等多数副本。
scenario_en: A KV store supports per-request consistency levels. A read can wait for one replica or for a majority.
q: 一致性级别调节的核心是什么？
q_en: What does a consistency level mainly tune?
options: 延迟、可用性和读到新值的概率
取决于 value 内容的压缩率高低
key 的字符长度
客户端 UI 样式
options_en: Latency, availability, and chance of seeing fresh data
It depends on the value compression ratio
Key string length
Client UI style
why: 等的副本越多，越可能读到新值，但尾延迟和故障失败率也会上升。它是每次读写的取舍旋钮。
why_en: Waiting for more replicas improves freshness odds but raises tail latency and failure exposure, making consistency a per-operation knob.
tradeoff: 低延迟/高可用 vs 新鲜度
whenOtherWins: 强不变量操作可以单独用更高一致性，普通浏览读用较低一致性。

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次读写需要等待多少副本响应的策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A consistency level is the policy for how many replicas an operation waits for.

optionExplanations: 对，等的副本越多，越可能读到最新写入，但延迟和因为个别副本慢或故障而失败的概率也会跟着上升，这正是每次读写要权衡的旋钮。
一致性级别调节的是等待几个副本确认，跟 value 本身要不要压缩是两个不相关的存储细节。
key 的字符长度是设计 key 时该考虑的问题，跟每次请求选多高的一致性级别没有关系。
一致性级别是存储和复制层面的设置，客户端 UI 长什么样是展示层的问题，两者不在一个维度上。
optionExplanations_en: Right — waiting on more replicas raises the odds of catching the latest write, but it also raises tail latency and the chance of failure from one slow or down replica — exactly the tradeoff dial on every read and write.
Consistency level tunes how many replicas to wait for — an unrelated storage detail from whether the value itself gets compressed.
Key character length is a concern when designing the key itself, unrelated to how high a consistency level a given request chooses.
Consistency level is a storage/replication setting; client UI styling is a presentation-layer concern — the two aren't on the same axis at all.

scenario: 一次 quorum 读从 3 个副本拿到两个不同版本。coordinator 能判断其中一个副本落后。
scenario_en: A quorum read from three replicas returns two different versions, and the coordinator can tell one replica is stale.
q: read repair 应该做什么？
q_en: What should read repair do?
options: 返回正确值的同时，把落后副本异步更新
直接删除所有副本
让客户端每次都永远同时看到两个版本
停止整个集群等待人工处理
options_en: Return the correct value while asynchronously updating stale replicas
Delete all replicas
Make the client always see both versions
Stop the cluster for manual handling
why: read repair 把读请求顺手变成修复机会。它能缩短副本不一致窗口，但会给读路径增加后台写压力。
why_en: Read repair turns reads into repair opportunities, reducing divergence at the cost of extra background writes.
tradeoff: 收敛速度 vs 读路径额外写入
whenOtherWins: 如果读延迟极敏感，可以把修复放到独立 anti-entropy 后台任务。

termDefinitions.meaning: 读到副本不一致时，系统顺手把落后副本更新到较新版本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read repair updates stale replicas when a read detects inconsistent versions.

optionExplanations: 对，趁着这次读顺手把落后副本更新到最新版本，能缩短副本之间不一致的时间窗口，代价是给这次读多加了一次后台写。
直接删除所有副本会把这个 key 的数据全部丢掉，跟“修复不一致”这个目标完全相反。
让客户端永远看到两个版本回避了修复这件事，只是把选择哪个版本的负担无限期地丢给用户。
为了一个 key 的版本分歧就停下整个集群等人工处理，代价远远超过问题本身，不是合理的响应方式。
optionExplanations_en: Right — piggybacking an update to the lagging replica onto this read shortens the window of inconsistency between replicas, at the cost of an extra background write on this read.
Deleting all the replicas outright throws away this key's data entirely — the opposite of the goal of fixing an inconsistency.
Letting the client always see both versions dodges the repair altogether, just handing the burden of choosing indefinitely to the user.
Halting the entire cluster for manual intervention over one key's version divergence is wildly disproportionate to the actual problem.

scenario: 写请求必须等 W=2。当前只有一个副本可达，其他副本网络超时。业务要求不能确认可能丢失的写。
scenario_en: A write requires W=2. Only one replica is reachable and the others time out. The business must not acknowledge writes that may be lost.
q: 严格 quorum 应该怎么做？
q_en: What should strict quorum do?
options: 拒绝或超时这次写入
先确认成功，以后再说
只写客户端本地缓存
把 W 自动降到 1 且不记录
options_en: Reject or time out this write
Acknowledge success and handle it later
Write only to the client cache
Silently lower W to 1
why: 严格 quorum 的承诺是达到 W 才成功。达不到就不能假装成功，否则故障后可能丢已确认写。
why_en: Strict quorum only succeeds after W acknowledgments; otherwise acknowledging would risk losing a confirmed write.
tradeoff: 确认安全 vs 故障期可用性
whenOtherWins: 如果业务更看重可用性，可以选择 sloppy quorum，但要接受临时不一致。
optionExplanations: 严格 quorum 的承诺就是凑够 W 个确认才能算成功，凑不齐的时候只能拒绝或超时，不能假装写成功了。
先确认成功、以后再说，等于对客户端撒了一个可能兑现不了的承诺，一旦真的丢失就成了已确认写却丢失的严重故障。
只写客户端本地缓存并不会让其他副本真正拿到这份数据，业务要求的持久确认根本没有达成。
把 W 自动降到 1 且不记录，等于悄悄放弃了严格 quorum 的承诺，跟“不能确认可能丢失的写”这个要求正相反。
optionExplanations_en: Strict quorum's whole promise is that success only counts once W acknowledgments come in; falling short means rejecting or timing out, not pretending it succeeded.
Confirming success now and sorting it out later makes a promise to the client that might not hold — if the write is actually lost, that becomes a confirmed-but-lost write, a serious failure.
Writing only to the client's local cache never actually gets the data onto the other replicas — the durable acknowledgment the business requires never happens.
Silently dropping W to 1 with no record quietly abandons the strict-quorum promise — the opposite of the requirement not to confirm a possibly-lost write.

scenario: KV 为了可用性启用 sloppy quorum。原副本 s2 不可达，健康节点 s3 代收写入。
scenario_en: The KV store enables sloppy quorum. Original replica s2 is unreachable, and healthy node s3 temporarily accepts writes for it.
q: sloppy quorum 的隐藏风险是什么？
q_en: What hidden risk comes with sloppy quorum?
options: 代收数据在回交前可能让读取看到旧值或缺值
所有写都会立刻强一致
不再需要 hinted handoff
副本数量会永久翻倍
options_en: Before handoff, reads may see stale or missing values
All writes become immediately strongly consistent
Hinted handoff is no longer needed
Replica count doubles permanently
why: sloppy quorum 把可用性放在前面。代收节点还没把数据交回原副本时，不同读路径可能看到不同状态。
why_en: Sloppy quorum favors availability, so before handoff completes different read paths may observe different states.
tradeoff: 故障期接收写入 vs 临时分歧
whenOtherWins: 严格金融写入不适合这种临时代收，应宁可失败也不确认。
optionExplanations: 读到代收节点还是读到原副本，结果会不一样；要靠 read repair 或调高 R 才收敛。
这套机制存在的目的正是故障期间别把写路径卡死，代价换来的是暂时不敢保证所有节点看到同一个答案。
hinted handoff 正是这里依赖的关键步骤，用来把代收数据交还原副本，说不再需要它是理解反了。
代收只是把数据临时放在健康节点上，不会让副本总数量发生变化，更不会永久翻倍。
optionExplanations_en: A read that lands on the hinted node sees a different answer than one that lands on the original replica; read repair or a higher R is what makes them converge.
The whole point of this mechanism is not letting the write path stall during an outage — the tradeoff is not being able to promise every node agrees on the same answer for a while.
Hinted handoff is the very step this mechanism depends on to return buffered writes to the original replica, so calling it unnecessary gets it backwards.
Standing in for a replica just temporarily holds data on a healthy node — it doesn't change the total replica count, let alone permanently double it.

q: hinted handoff 的完整状态链是什么？
q_en: What is the full state chain of hinted handoff?
steps: 原副本不可达，coordinator 选择健康节点代收
代收节点保存数据和目标副本的 hint
原副本恢复后，代收节点把变更交回
目标副本应用变更后，hint 可以清理
why: 这条链要讲清中间状态：数据暂时不在原副本上，而是在代收节点带着 hint 等恢复。代价是可能重复交付，写入要幂等。
why_en: Hinted handoff stores temporary writes with a hint, hands them back on recovery, and needs idempotent handling because delivery can repeat.

termDefinitions.meaning: 代收节点保存的元数据，说明这份写入最终应交给哪个原副本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hint is metadata saying which original replica should receive the temporarily stored write.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一操作重复执行多次，最终效果仍等同执行一次。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotent means repeating an operation has the same final effect as doing it once.

scenario: 某些 key 很冷，几个月没有被读到。只靠 read repair，冷 key 的副本分歧可能长期存在。
scenario_en: Some keys are cold and may not be read for months. If the system only uses read repair, divergence on cold keys can last a long time.
q: 冷数据副本收敛靠什么？
q_en: How should cold-data replicas converge?
options: 后台 anti-entropy 周期性比较和修复
只等到用户读到每个 key 的时候才顺带修复它
把冷 key 全部删除
让客户端每次读都全量扫描所有副本
options_en: Background anti-entropy periodically compares and repairs
Repair opportunistically only when a user reads each key
Delete all cold keys
Make clients full-scan every replica on every read
why: read repair 依赖读流量，冷 key 可能永远不触发。anti-entropy 在后台主动比较副本，让冷数据也能收敛。
why_en: Read repair depends on reads, so background anti-entropy is needed to converge cold data too.
tradeoff: 后台修复成本 vs 冷数据长期分歧
whenOtherWins: 如果数据很热，read repair 已经能快速修复大部分分歧。

termDefinitions.meaning: 副本之间后台比较并同步差异，减少长期不一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Anti-entropy is background comparison and synchronization between replicas to reduce long-lived divergence.

optionExplanations: 只靠读流量触发的修复对冷 key 不起作用，得有一个后台任务周期性主动比较副本、找出并修复分歧，冷数据才不会被永远遗忘。
等待用户读到每个 key 才能触发修复，正是冷 key 几个月没人读、分歧长期存在的根本原因，不是解法。
把冷 key 全部删除会造成真实数据丢失，用删除来回避一致性问题代价太大，不是合理做法。
让客户端每次全量扫描去发现分歧，成本极高而且分散在每个客户端上不可控，不是系统该承担一致性的方式。
optionExplanations_en: Repair that only triggers on read traffic never reaches a cold key — a background job that periodically compares replicas on its own is what keeps even cold data from being forgotten forever.
Waiting for a user to eventually read each key is exactly why a cold key that hasn't been touched in months keeps its divergence for so long — that's the problem, not the fix.
Deleting all the cold keys causes real data loss — using deletion to dodge a consistency problem is far too costly to be reasonable.
Having every client do a full scan to discover divergence is extremely expensive and scattered across uncontrolled clients — not how a system should own its own consistency.

scenario: 10 亿个 key 被切成 100 万个 Merkle bucket。你要估算每个 bucket 的平均 key 数，用来判断修复粒度。
scenario_en: One billion keys are split into one million Merkle buckets. Estimate average keys per bucket to judge repair granularity.
q: 这个 bucket 粒度意味着什么？
q_en: What does this bucket granularity imply?
options: 平均约 1000 key/bucket，修复可定位到较小范围
平均约 1 key/bucket，树会太浅
平均约 100 万 key/bucket，粒度太粗无法减少传输
bucket 数和 key 数无关
options_en: About 1000 keys per bucket, so repair can target smaller ranges
About 1 key per bucket, making the tree too shallow
About 1 million keys per bucket, so transfer is not reduced
Bucket count is unrelated to key count
why: 公式是 1,000,000,000 / 1,000,000 = 1000 key/bucket。这个数决定一次哈希差异定位后，最多要同步多粗的一段数据。
why_en: One billion divided by one million is about 1000 keys per bucket, which sets the repair granularity after a hash mismatch.
optionExplanations: 10 亿除以 100 万正好是 1000，意味着一次哈希差异定位后，最多只需要同步大约 1000 个 key 这么小的一段，不用搬动全部 10 亿。
如果平均只有 1 个 key/bucket，10 亿个 key 就要对应 10 亿个 bucket，跟题目给的 100 万个 bucket 数字对不上。
如果平均是 100 万 key/bucket，总 key 数就要到万亿级别，远超题目给出的 10 亿，这个换算是错的。
bucket 数量和 key 总数正是通过除法直接关联在一起的，说两者无关忽略了这道题本身在问的换算关系。
optionExplanations_en: 10 billion divided by 1 million comes out to exactly 1000, meaning after one hash-diff localization, at most about 1000 keys' worth of data needs syncing, not the full 10 billion.
If it averaged 1 key per bucket, 10 billion keys would need 10 billion buckets, which doesn't match the 1 million buckets given in the problem.
If it averaged 1 million keys per bucket, the total key count would have to be in the trillions, far more than the 10 billion given — this conversion is wrong.
Bucket count and total key count are directly linked by this division — saying they're unrelated ignores the exact conversion this question is asking about.

scenario: 客户端读到两个 sibling 购物车版本：一个加了牙刷，一个加了毛巾。系统无法自动判断哪个应该覆盖。
scenario_en: A client reads two sibling cart versions: one added a toothbrush and one added a towel. The system cannot know which one should overwrite the other.
q: 购物车冲突更适合怎么合并？
q_en: How should shopping-cart conflicts be merged?
options: 由业务按商品集合合并，再写回新版本
随机保留其中一个版本
总是按服务器 ID 的大小来覆盖合并
删除整个购物车
options_en: Let business logic merge item sets and write a new version
Randomly keep one version
Overwrite by the larger server ID
Delete the whole cart
why: 购物车的合并语义通常是保留两个添加动作。存储层只检测冲突，业务层知道怎么合并。
why_en: For carts, the business often wants to preserve both additions; storage detects the conflict, while application logic merges it.
tradeoff: 保留用户意图 vs 客户端合并复杂度
whenOtherWins: 如果字段是“最后一次设置用户名”，last-write-wins 可能更简单。
optionExplanations: 业务清楚“加了牙刷”和“加了毛巾”这两个动作应该都保留，由业务按商品集合把两个版本的内容合并成一份，再写回新版本。
随机保留其中一个版本意味着用户添加的另一件商品会凭空消失，用户明明加过却找不到了。
按服务器 ID 大小覆盖是一种跟业务意图无关的技术规则，同样会让其中一次真实的添加操作被悄悄丢弃。
删除整个购物车是最激进的做法，两个用户添加的商品会全部丢失，代价远超冲突本身。
optionExplanations_en: The business knows both "added a toothbrush" and "added a towel" should be kept, so merging the two versions' item sets into one and writing back a new version preserves both actions.
Randomly keeping one version means whichever item the user added in the other one simply vanishes, even though they genuinely added it.
Overwriting by comparing server IDs is a technical rule with no connection to business intent, and it would just as quietly drop one of the two real additions.
Deleting the whole cart is the most drastic option — both users' added items are lost entirely, a cost far greater than the conflict itself.

scenario: KV 检测到同一 key 的并发写。你在比较 last-write-wins 和 vector clock + merge。
scenario_en: A KV store detects concurrent writes to the same key. You compare last-write-wins with vector clock plus merge.
q: 两种冲突策略的核心取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the core tradeoff between the two conflict policies?
options: LWW 简单但可能丢更新；向量时钟保留冲突但要合并
LWW 一定强一致；向量时钟不能复制
LWW 只能用在读路径；向量时钟只能用在写路径
两者都不需要版本信息
options_en: LWW is simple but may lose updates; vector clocks preserve conflicts but need merging
LWW is always strongly consistent; vector clocks cannot replicate
LWW is only for reads; vector clocks only for writes
Neither needs version information
why: LWW 把冲突压成一个值，操作简单但可能丢掉并发意图。向量时钟暴露 sibling，复杂但更少误删。
why_en: Last-write-wins collapses conflicts simply but can lose intent, while vector clocks expose siblings for safer merging.
tradeoff: 简单自动收敛 vs 保留并发更新
whenOtherWins: 对可覆盖字段、日志指标这类数据，LWW 的简单性可能足够。

termDefinitions.meaning: 按时间或版本选择最后一个写入作为胜者的冲突策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Last-write-wins chooses the latest write by timestamp or version as the winner.

optionExplanations: 对，LWW 只需要挑一个值留下，操作简单，但可能悄悄丢掉另一个并发写入的意图；向量时钟会把冲突暴露出来，需要额外一步合并，但更少误删。
LWW 保留最后一次写入不等于强一致，它照样会丢并发更新；向量时钟本身完全可以正常复制，这两个判断都不成立。
LWW 和向量时钟都是在写入时判断版本关系、在读取时暴露结果，不存在只能用于读或只能用于写的限制。
这两种策略恰恰都依赖版本信息才能工作——LWW 靠时间戳判断谁最后写，向量时钟靠因果计数判断并发，说都不需要版本信息是错的。
optionExplanations_en: Right — LWW just keeps one value, simple to operate, but can silently drop another concurrent write's intent; vector clocks surface the conflict instead, needing an extra merge step but losing less.
Keeping the last write doesn't make LWW strongly consistent — it still loses concurrent updates; and vector clocks replicate perfectly normally — neither claim holds.
Both LWW and vector clocks make their version judgment at write time and surface the result at read time — neither is restricted to only reads or only writes.

Both strategies actually depend on version information to work — LWW uses a timestamp to decide who wrote last, vector clocks use causal counters to detect concurrency — saying neither needs version info is wrong.

scenario: 开发者想先写 memtable，再异步写 commit log，以降低写延迟。机器可能随时崩溃。
scenario_en: A developer wants to write the memtable first and append the commit log asynchronously to reduce latency. The machine may crash at any time.
q: 这个顺序有什么危险？
q_en: What is dangerous about this ordering?
options: 确认后但日志前崩溃，会丢已确认写
读路径会自动更快且无代价
SSTable 会变成可变文件
副本数会减少到 1
options_en: A crash after acknowledgement but before logging can lose confirmed writes
Reads become faster with no cost
SSTables become mutable files
Replica count drops to one
why: commit log 是崩溃恢复的底线。先确认再落日志，会让客户端以为成功但恢复时找不到这次写。
why_en: The commit log is the recovery floor; acknowledging before logging can lose a write the client believes succeeded.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不可变、按 key 排序的磁盘键值文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SSTable is an immutable sorted on-disk key-value file.

optionExplanations: 对，客户端已经收到写成功的确认，但这次写其实还没落进日志，机器一崩溃，恢复时重放日志根本找不到这次写，等于承诺了一个没兑现的确认。
读路径变快是有代价的，代价就是牺牲了崩溃时的持久性保证，不存在“无代价”这种说法。
这个顺序问题出在崩溃恢复的可靠性上，跟 SSTable 是不是可变文件没有关系。
这里讨论的是写确认和日志顺序的风险，不会因为这个顺序问题就让副本数量减少。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the client already got a success acknowledgment, but the write hasn't actually hit the log yet, so a crash right there means replay during recovery can never find it — a confirmation that was never actually kept.
A faster read path doesn't come free — the cost here is giving up the durability guarantee during a crash; there's no such thing as "no cost" here.
This ordering problem is about crash-recovery reliability, unrelated to whether SSTables are mutable or immutable files.
This is about the risk from write-acknowledgment-versus-log ordering — it doesn't cause the replica count to shrink.

scenario: memtable 一直吸收写入。它占用内存越来越大，崩溃恢复需要重放的 commit log 也越来越长。
scenario_en: A memtable keeps absorbing writes. Its memory footprint grows, and crash recovery would need to replay more commit-log data.
q: 什么时候该 flush memtable？
q_en: When should the memtable be flushed?
options: 达到内存或时间阈值时刷成 SSTable
每读一次都刷盘
永远不刷，靠 commit log 查询
只在数据库删除时刷盘
options_en: Flush to an SSTable at memory or time thresholds
Flush on every read
Never flush; query the commit log
Flush only when deleting the database
why: flush 把内存状态固化成磁盘 SSTable，并允许旧日志段回收。阈值太大恢复慢，太小会制造太多小文件。
why_en: Flushing persists memory state into SSTables and allows log cleanup; too large slows recovery, too small creates many files.
tradeoff: 恢复时间/内存 vs SSTable 数量
whenOtherWins: 极低写入量系统可以用更简单的定时刷盘策略。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把内存缓冲中的数据批量写成磁盘文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Flush means writing buffered in-memory data out to disk files.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不可变、按 key 排序的磁盘键值文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SSTable is an immutable sorted on-disk key-value file.

optionExplanations: 达到内存占用或时间阈值时把 memtable 刷成 SSTable，既能释放内存，也能让旧的 commit log 段被回收，控制恢复时要重放的日志长度。
每读一次都刷盘会让读路径背上巨大的额外 I/O 开销，读操作不该触发这种代价高昂的动作。
永远不刷、只靠 commit log 查询，意味着每次查找都要重放全部历史日志，查询会越来越慢，也失去了 SSTable 该有的读优化。
只在数据库删除时才刷盘意味着 memtable 会无限增长，内存和恢复时间都会失控，跟控制这两者的目标相反。
optionExplanations_en: Flushing the memtable into an SSTable once it hits a memory or time threshold frees up memory and lets old commit log segments be reclaimed, keeping the replay time on recovery in check.
Flushing to disk on every single read saddles the read path with huge extra I/O overhead — reads shouldn't trigger something this expensive.
Never flushing and querying only through the commit log means every lookup has to replay the entire history, getting slower over time and losing all the read optimization SSTables provide.
Flushing only when the database is deleted lets the memtable grow without bound, letting both memory and recovery time spiral — the opposite of controlling either.

scenario: LSM 存储不断 flush 新 SSTable。删除会写 tombstone，旧值和删除标记可能分散在多个文件里。
scenario_en: An LSM store keeps flushing new SSTables. Deletes write tombstones, and old values plus delete markers may sit in many files.
q: compaction 主要解决什么？
q_en: What does compaction mainly solve?
options: 合并文件并清旧版本
把 commit log 压缩成图片
把副本同步到同一机房
让 Bloom filter 不再误判
options_en: Merge files and clear old versions
Compress commit logs into images
Sync replicas into one data center
Make Bloom filters never false-positive
why: SSTable 越多，读一个 key 要查的候选越多。compaction 用后台 I/O 换更少文件、更少旧版本和更稳的读延迟。
why_en: More SSTables increase read fanout, so compaction spends background I/O to reduce files, obsolete versions, and read latency.
tradeoff: 后台 I/O/写放大 vs 读放大
whenOtherWins: 写入极少、SSTable 数量很小的时候，可以降低 compaction 频率。

termDefinitions.meaning: 写优化存储结构，把写入批量落成不可变有序文件，再后台合并。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSM tree is a write-optimized structure that flushes writes into immutable sorted files and compacts them later.

termDefinitions.meaning: 删除操作写下的删除标记，用来在合并前压住旧值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tombstone is a delete marker that suppresses older values until compaction removes them.

optionExplanations: 对，compaction 把分散在多个文件里的同一 key 的旧版本和删除标记合并清理掉，减少一次读要翻查的候选文件数。
commit log 是用来做崩溃恢复的日志文件，把它压缩成图片既不现实也完全脱离了 compaction 要解决的问题。
把副本同步到同一机房是数据放置策略，跟“清理同一存储引擎内部分散的旧版本文件”完全是两回事。
compaction 处理的是文件和版本的整理，不会改变 Bloom filter 本身的误判率，这是另一个独立的机制。
optionExplanations_en: Right — compaction merges away old versions and delete markers of the same key scattered across multiple files, cutting down how many candidate files a single read has to check.
A commit log is the journal for crash recovery — compressing it into an image is neither realistic nor anywhere near what compaction is actually solving.
Syncing replicas into the same datacenter is a data-placement policy, an entirely different concern from cleaning up scattered old version files within one storage engine.
Compaction cleans up files and versions — it doesn't change the Bloom filter's own false-positive rate, which is a separate mechanism.

scenario: Bloom filter 判断某个 SSTable 可能包含 key，但实际查文件后没有找到。
scenario_en: A Bloom filter says an SSTable may contain a key, but the file lookup does not find it.
q: Bloom filter 误判会造成什么？
q_en: What does a Bloom-filter false positive cause?
options: 多做一次无用磁盘查找，但不会漏掉真实 key
会直接把一个错误的 value 返回给客户端
永久删除这个 key
破坏 quorum 公式
options_en: An extra useless disk lookup, but no missed real key
Return a wrong value directly to the client
The key is permanently deleted
The quorum formula is broken
why: Bloom filter 可以误报“可能在”，不能误报“肯定不在”。所以它影响性能，不应该影响正确性。
why_en: Bloom filters can false-positive but not false-negative, so they may waste I/O without hiding an existing key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 结构说“可能存在”，但真实数据里不存在。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false positive means the structure says an item may exist when it actually does not.

tradeoff: 少量无用 I/O vs 不漏真实 key
whenOtherWins: 如果磁盘 I/O 已经很便宜、内存很紧，可以把 Bloom filter 做小一点，接受更多误判。
optionExplanations: 代价就停在“白开了一次没找到东西的文件”这一步，多花的是一点点磁盘 I/O 时间，不会牵连到最终交给客户端的结果对不对。
这道题真正要分清的是两种错法：漏报会让存在的数据凭空消失，误报只是多看一眼——这里发生的属于后者，无害得多。
跟数据本身要不要被删除毫无关系，它只是一个用来跳过无关文件的过滤器，不参与任何删除决策。
多付出的成本只是磁盘读取次数，跟 quorum 公式里读写副本数量的计算完全不在一个层面。
optionExplanations_en: The cost stops at "opened a file for nothing" — a bit of wasted disk I/O time, with no bearing on whether the final answer handed to the client is right.
The real distinction here is between two kinds of wrong: a false negative makes real data vanish, a false positive just costs one extra look — this is the harmless latter kind.
It has nothing to do with whether the data itself should be deleted — it's purely a filter for skipping irrelevant files, playing no part in any deletion decision.
The only extra cost is a few more disk reads — a completely different layer from the read/write replica counts in the quorum formula.

scenario: 一次读从多个 SSTable 找到同一个 key 的多个版本，另有一个 tombstone。系统需要返回对客户端正确的状态。
scenario_en: A read finds multiple versions of the same key across SSTables, plus a tombstone. The system must return the correct state.
q: 读路径如何选择结果？
q_en: How should the read path choose the result?
options: 按版本或时间戳合并，tombstone 可覆盖旧值
随机返回第一个 SSTable 里读到的那个值
永远忽略 tombstone
把所有版本直接拼成字符串
options_en: Merge by version or timestamp, letting tombstones suppress older values
Randomly return whatever the first SSTable holds
Always ignore tombstones
Concatenate all versions into a string
why: LSM 读路径要理解同一 key 的多版本。最新写或删除标记决定可见结果，旧值等 compaction 清掉。
why_en: An LSM read must reconcile multiple versions of a key; the latest write or delete marker determines the visible result.
tradeoff: 写入顺序化 vs 读时合并复杂度
whenOtherWins: 如果存储引擎原地更新，读时多版本合并压力会小一些。

termDefinitions.meaning: 写优化存储结构，把写入批量落成不可变有序文件，再后台合并。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSM tree is a write-optimized structure that flushes writes into immutable sorted files and compacts them later.

optionExplanations: 最新的写入或删除标记决定这个 key 该展示成什么状态，比它更旧的版本会在之后的 compaction 里被清掉，读路径按版本或时间戳合并出这一个正确结果。
随机返回第一个文件里的值完全忽略了版本先后，很可能把一个早就被覆盖或删除的旧值当成正确答案返回。
tombstone 就是用来标记这个 key 已经被删除的，永远忽略它会让已经删除的数据看起来仍然存在。
把所有版本直接拼成字符串完全不是这个 key 该有的真实状态，读者拿到的会是一堆无意义的拼接内容。
optionExplanations_en: The most recent write or delete marker decides what state this key should show as; anything older than that gets cleaned up in a later compaction, and the read path merges by version or timestamp to produce that one correct result.
Randomly returning whatever's in the first file ignores version order entirely and could easily hand back a value that was already overwritten or deleted long ago.
A tombstone exists precisely to mark that this key has been deleted — ignoring it forever would make deleted data look like it's still there.
Concatenating every version into one string isn't this key's real state at all — the caller would just get a meaningless jumble.

scenario: 社交资料 KV 在网络分区时仍要允许用户更新简介。短时间看到旧简介可以接受，稍后同步即可。
scenario_en: A social-profile KV store should let users update bios during network partitions. Seeing an old bio briefly is acceptable if it syncs later.
q: 这个业务更像 AP 还是 CP？
q_en: Is this business closer to AP or CP?
options: AP，继续服务并接受短暂旧值
CP，所有分区期间写入都报错
CA，完全不考虑分区
单机内存表，无需复制
options_en: AP, continue serving and accept temporary staleness
CP, reject all writes during partitions
CA, ignore partitions entirely
Single-node memory table with no replication
why: 简介不是强金融不变量，用户体验更怕不可用。AP 让写入先成功，之后靠同步和冲突策略收敛。
why_en: A profile bio is not a hard financial invariant, so AP behavior favors user availability and repairs later.
tradeoff: 用户可用性 vs 立即一致
whenOtherWins: 如果字段代表法定身份或余额，CP 会更稳。
optionExplanations: 社交简介不是强金融不变量，用户更怕分区期间连改个简介都不让改，AP 让写入先成功，后续再靠同步和冲突策略把内容收敛一致。
分区期间所有写入都报错，意味着用户遇到网络分区就完全不能更新简介，跟“仍要允许用户更新”的要求正相反。
CA 假装分区不会发生，这在真实的多机网络环境里本身就是不成立的前提。
社交资料要跨多个用户共享和访问，只用单机内存表没有任何复制和容灾能力，不适合这种规模的服务。
optionExplanations_en: A social profile isn't a strict financial invariant, and users mind being blocked from updating it during a partition far more than seeing a stale one — AP lets the write succeed first and lets sync plus conflict resolution converge it later.
Erroring out on every write during a partition means the user can't update their bio at all while it lasts — the opposite of the requirement to keep allowing updates.
CA pretends partitions never happen, which isn't a valid assumption in any real multi-machine networked environment.
A social profile needs to be shared and accessed across many users — a single in-memory table with no replication offers no disaster tolerance at this scale.

scenario: KV 的 key 可能是很长的 JSON 查询条件，也可能是短的哈希摘要。系统每次 get/put 都要传输和比较 key。
scenario_en: KV keys may be long JSON query strings or short hash digests. Every get/put transmits and compares the key.
q: 为什么短 key 通常更好？
q_en: Why are shorter keys usually better?
options: 减少网络、内存和索引比较开销
让 value 自动变小
保证不会有冲突
让 CAP 选择消失
options_en: They reduce network, memory, and index-comparison overhead
They automatically shrink values
They guarantee no collisions
They remove CAP tradeoffs
why: key 会出现在请求、索引、缓存和日志里。短 key 不改变语义，但能降低每次操作的固定成本。
why_en: Keys appear in requests, indexes, caches, and logs, so shorter keys reduce per-operation overhead without changing semantics.
tradeoff: 可读性 vs 操作开销
whenOtherWins: 排障或人工操作很重要时，可读 key 也有价值，可以用前缀加短 ID 折中。

termDefinitions.meaning: Consistency、Availability、Partition Tolerance 三者在网络分区时不能同时满分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP says consistency, availability, and partition tolerance cannot all be fully satisfied during a network partition.

optionExplanations: key 会反复出现在每次请求、索引、缓存和日志里，更短的 key 能直接降低这些地方的网络传输、内存占用和比较开销。
key 的长度只影响 key 本身的开销，不会让存进去的 value 自动变小，这两者互相独立。
key 短不能保证不会有冲突，冲突是由哈希算法和分片规则决定的，跟 key 长度没有必然联系。
key 长度是操作开销层面的问题，跟 CAP 定理要不要在一致性和可用性之间取舍完全是两个维度。
optionExplanations_en: A key shows up repeatedly in every request, index, cache, and log entry, so a shorter one directly lowers the network, memory, and comparison overhead in all of those places.
Key length only affects the key's own overhead — it doesn't shrink the value being stored, the two are independent.
A short key doesn't guarantee no collisions — collisions come from the hash algorithm and sharding rule, not necessarily from key length.
Key length is an operational-overhead concern, an entirely different dimension from whether CAP forces a tradeoff between consistency and availability.

scenario: KV 设计假设单个 key-value 小于 10KB。现在产品想把 50MB 文件直接作为 value 写入。
scenario_en: The KV design assumes each key-value pair is under 10KB. Product now wants to write 50MB files directly as values.
q: 大 value 会改变什么设计？
q_en: How do large values change the design?
options: 应考虑对象存储保存大文件，KV 只存引用
直接塞进 memtable，没有任何影响
把 W 和 R 都设为 0
关闭副本避免网络传输
options_en: Use object storage for large files and keep only references in KV
Put them into the memtable with no impact
Set both W and R to 0
Disable replication to avoid network transfer
why: 大 value 会放大复制、日志、compaction 和读写延迟。KV 更适合存小对象或元数据，大文件交给对象存储。
why_en: Large values amplify replication, logging, compaction, and latency, so KV should store metadata or references while object storage holds files.
tradeoff: 简单 get/put vs 大对象传输成本
whenOtherWins: 如果系统专门是 blob store，就应围绕分块、校验和对象存储路径设计。

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向大对象或文件的存储服务，通常用对象 key 读写整块数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Object storage stores large blobs or files addressed by object keys.

termDefinitions.meaning: 后台合并 SSTable、清理旧版本或删除标记的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Compaction is the background process of merging SSTables and removing obsolete versions or tombstones.

optionExplanations: 50MB 的大文件更适合放进对象存储，KV 里只留一个指向它的引用，这样复制、日志和 compaction 都不用直接搬这么大的数据。
直接塞进 memtable 会让内存占用、复制流量和日志写入都被这一个大文件严重放大，说没有任何影响明显不成立。
把 W 和 R 都设为 0 等于放弃了这次写入的一致性确认，跟“该怎么处理大文件”这个问题完全不相关。
关闭副本确实能避免这次网络传输，但代价是这份数据失去了容错能力，一台机器故障就直接丢失。
optionExplanations_en: A 50MB file fits object storage much better, with the KV store only holding a reference to it, so replication, logging, and compaction never have to move that much data directly.
Stuffing it straight into the memtable inflates memory usage, replication traffic, and log writes all at once because of this one large file — saying it has no impact clearly doesn't hold.
Setting both W and R to 0 abandons consistency confirmation for this write entirely — unrelated to the actual question of how to handle a large file.
Turning off replication does avoid this one network transfer, but it costs the data all fault tolerance — one machine failure and it's simply gone.

scenario: KV 集群没有固定 master。每个节点都能接请求、维护成员信息、转发到副本并保存部分数据。
scenario_en: A KV cluster has no fixed master. Every node can accept requests, maintain membership, forward to replicas, and store part of the data.
q: 去中心化架构的好处是什么？
q_en: What is the benefit of this decentralized architecture?
options: 减少单点故障，并让节点增删更自动
让所有请求必须经过一个 leader
取消副本和故障检测
让一致性永远最强
options_en: Reduce single points of failure and make membership changes more automatic
Force all requests through one leader
Remove replication and failure detection
Make consistency always strongest
why: 节点职责对称时，某个协调节点挂了不等于集群停摆。代价是成员状态、冲突和修复逻辑更复杂。
why_en: Symmetric node roles avoid one coordinator becoming a cluster-wide stop point, at the cost of more membership and repair complexity.
tradeoff: 无单点 vs 协议复杂度
whenOtherWins: 强事务数据库可能选择 leader 或共识组来换更清晰的一致性语义。
optionExplanations: 节点职责对称意味着任何一个协调节点挂掉都不会让整个集群停摆，节点增删也不需要围着某个中心节点重新配置。
要求所有请求必须经过一个 leader，正是去中心化架构想要避免的单点瓶颈，跟它的设计目标正相反。
去中心化架构照样需要副本和故障检测来保证数据可靠，取消它们会让系统直接失去容错能力。
去中心化换来的是无单点，不是免费获得更强一致性；协调节点之间的冲突处理反而会让一致性语义更复杂。
optionExplanations_en: Symmetric node duties mean any single coordinating node dying doesn't stall the whole cluster, and adding or removing nodes doesn't require reconfiguring around one central node.
Requiring every request to pass through one leader is exactly the single-point bottleneck a decentralized architecture is trying to avoid — the opposite of its design goal.
A decentralized architecture still needs replicas and failure detection to keep data reliable — removing them would strip out fault tolerance entirely.
Decentralization buys you no single point of failure, not free stronger consistency — resolving conflicts across coordinating nodes actually makes consistency semantics harder.

q: Cassandra 风格 KV 写路径的正确顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the correct order of a Cassandra-style KV write path?
steps: 追加 commit log 保证崩溃可恢复
写入 memtable 作为内存有序缓冲
达到阈值后 flush 成不可变 SSTable
后台 compaction 合并 SSTable 并清理旧版本
why: 这条链把持久性、低延迟写入、磁盘落盘和后台整理分开。漏掉任何一步，都讲不清 LSM 的取舍。
why_en: The chain separates durability, fast in-memory writes, disk flushing, and background cleanup, which is the LSM tradeoff.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种去中心化宽列数据库，常用 LSM 风格存储路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is a decentralized wide-column database that commonly uses an LSM-style storage path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写优化存储结构，把写入批量落成不可变有序文件，再后台合并。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSM tree is a write-optimized structure that flushes writes into immutable sorted files and compacts them later.

scenario: KV 使用 Cassandra 风格的 LSM 写路径：commit log、memtable、SSTable 和后台 compaction 分工不同。
scenario_en: The KV store uses a Cassandra-style LSM write path with commit log, memtable, SSTable, and background compaction.

q: 分布式 KV 需要分别处理哪些故障？
q_en: Which failures should a distributed KV store handle separately?
options: 单节点临时不可达
副本永久丢失或长期落后
整个数据中心不可用
用户把 value 写成字符串
options_en: A single node temporarily unreachable
A replica permanently lost or far behind
A whole data center unavailable
A user writes a string value
why: 临时故障靠 handoff，永久分歧靠 anti-entropy，机房故障靠跨 DC 副本。普通字符串 value 不是故障类型。
why_en: Temporary failure uses handoff, permanent divergence uses anti-entropy, and data-center outage requires cross-site replicas.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据中心，是一组可能共享电力、网络或地理风险的基础设施。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A data center is an infrastructure site that may share power, network, or geographic risks.

optionExplanations: 对，单节点临时不可达属于短暂性故障，通常靠代收和回交这类机制来兜底，不需要动用更重的手段。
对，副本永久丢失或长期落后已经不是短暂故障，得靠后台主动比较和修复来处理，跟临时不可达是不同类型的问题。
对，整个数据中心不可用是最大范围的故障，只能靠提前存在于其他机房的副本来承接，跟单机故障的应对方式完全不同。
用户把 value 写成字符串是正常的业务写入行为，不是系统需要专门处理的故障类型，不该和真正的故障混在一起。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a single node being briefly unreachable is a transient fault, usually covered by standing-in-and-handing-back mechanisms without needing anything heavier.
Right — a replica being permanently lost or badly lagging is no longer transient, and needs active background comparison and repair, a different problem from a brief outage.

Right — an entire datacenter going down is the largest-scale failure, only survivable through replicas that already exist elsewhere ahead of time, handled completely differently from a single-machine fault.
A user writing a value as a string is normal business write behavior, not a failure type the system needs special handling for — it shouldn't be lumped in with real faults.
scenario: 一个跨三机房、每个 key 三副本的 KV 存储，要给不同类型的故障各配一套恢复手段。
scenario_en: A KV store spanning three data centers with three replicas per key needs a separate recovery path for each class of failure.

scenario: 客户端收到写成功后，立刻断电重启一个副本。系统不能丢这次已确认写。
scenario_en: A client receives write success, then one replica loses power and restarts. The system must not lose that acknowledged write.
q: 单节点内最关键的持久化机制是什么？
q_en: What is the key per-node durability mechanism?
options: 写前日志或 commit log
只放 memtable
只靠客户端重试
只依赖节点之间的 gossip 心跳来做恢复
options_en: A write-ahead log or commit log
Only the memtable
Only client retries
Rely only on gossip heartbeats between nodes
why: 副本级持久性要先落本地日志。gossip 只能发现节点状态，不能恢复内存里丢失的数据。
why_en: Replica durability needs a local log first; gossip detects liveness but cannot recover lost in-memory writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写数据页或内存表前先追加的恢复日志。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A write-ahead log is appended before data pages or memory tables so writes can be recovered.

tradeoff: 本地持久性 vs 只做存活检测
whenOtherWins: 如果只是临时缓存节点，数据源可重建，本地 commit log 可以弱化。
optionExplanations: 先把写入落到本地日志，断电重启后重放这份日志就能把已确认的写恢复回来，这是副本级持久性能扛住断电的根本手段。
只放 memtable 意味着数据只存在内存里，一断电这些数据就彻底没了，完全撑不住“已确认写不能丢”的要求。
只靠客户端重试解决不了服务端已经确认成功、但数据其实还没落盘就断电的问题，客户端根本不知道要重试。
gossip 心跳只能用来发现节点是否存活，不负责恢复某台机器内存里已经丢失的数据内容。
optionExplanations_en: Writing to a local log first means replaying it after a power loss and restart can restore the confirmed writes — the fundamental mechanism that lets per-replica durability survive a crash.
Keeping data only in the memtable means it exists purely in memory, so a power loss wipes it out entirely — nowhere near enough to satisfy "a confirmed write can't be lost."
Relying only on client retries can't fix a case where the server already confirmed success but the data never actually hit disk before power loss — the client has no idea a retry is even needed.
Gossip heartbeats only detect whether a node is alive — they aren't responsible for recovering data that was lost from one machine's memory.

scenario: 用户刚修改个人资料，马上刷新页面却可能被路由到旧副本。产品希望这个用户至少读到自己的新写入。
scenario_en: A user updates their profile and immediately refreshes, but may be routed to a stale replica. Product wants the user to at least read their own write.
q: 如何支持 read-your-writes？
q_en: How can read-your-writes be supported?
options: 会话路由或更高 R
永远 R=1 随机读
删除所有旧副本
关闭写入确认
options_en: Session routing or higher R
Always random-read with R=1
Delete all old replicas
Disable write acknowledgments
why: 最终一致不等于用户必须读到旧值。会话粘性、版本 token 或更高 R 都能保护“读到自己的写”。
why_en: Eventual consistency can still provide read-your-writes through session routing, version tokens, or stronger read consistency.
tradeoff: 用户体验一致性 vs 读延迟/路由状态
whenOtherWins: 纯匿名浏览数据不需要这个保证，随机读低延迟更重要。

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端完成写入后，自己的后续读取能看到这次写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read-your-writes means a client can see its own completed write in later reads.

optionExplanations: 把这个用户的后续请求粘在写入发生的那个副本上，或者干脆提高读要等待的副本数，都能让他大概率读到自己刚写的修改。
永远 R=1 随机读，意味着这个用户完全可能被路由到还没同步到最新修改的副本，读不到自己刚做的修改。
删除所有旧副本会造成真实的数据丢失，而且解决不了“读到自己最新写入”这个路由问题。
关闭写入确认只会让你更不确定这次修改到底有没有真的生效，跟保证用户读到自己写入完全是相反方向。
optionExplanations_en: Pinning this user's subsequent requests to the replica their write landed on, or simply raising how many replicas a read waits for, both make it likely they'll see their own just-made change.
Always reading with R=1 at random means this user could easily land on a replica that hasn't caught up yet, missing the change they just made.
Deleting all the old replicas causes real data loss and doesn't even solve the routing problem of reading back one's own latest write.
Turning off write acknowledgment only makes it less certain the change actually took effect — the opposite direction from guaranteeing a user sees their own write.

scenario: 同一个 KV 平台同时服务购物车、余额缓存和推荐特征。不同业务对新鲜度和可用性要求不同。
scenario_en: One KV platform serves carts, balance cache, and recommendation features. Different workloads have different freshness and availability needs.
q: 为什么要提供 tunable consistency？
q_en: Why offer tunable consistency?
options: 让每类请求按业务风险选择 R/W 或一致性级别
强制让所有类型的业务都走同一个固定一致性级别
让 key 不再需要分片
让冲突永远不会出现
options_en: Let each request choose R/W or consistency level by business risk
Force every workload onto the same fixed consistency level
Remove the need for sharding
Make conflicts impossible
why: 一个固定一致性策略很难同时满足所有业务。可调一致性让高风险操作多等副本，低风险读走低延迟。
why_en: One fixed policy rarely fits every workload, so tunable consistency lets risky operations wait for more replicas and low-risk reads stay fast.
tradeoff: 统一简单性 vs 按业务调优
whenOtherWins: 单一业务、单一 SLO 的小系统可以固定一种一致性级别，减少使用错误。

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务对外承诺或内部追踪的目标水平，比如延迟或可用性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLO is a target level for a service, such as latency or availability.

optionExplanations: 购物车、余额缓存、推荐特征对新鲜度和可用性的要求各不相同，让每类请求按自己的业务风险去选 R/W 或一致性级别，才能同时照顾到它们。
强制所有业务用同一个延迟目标，意味着低风险的推荐读取也要背上余额那种强确认的等待成本，完全没必要。
一致性级别是复制层面的调节手段，跟 key 该不该分片是两个不同的设计维度，调它不会让分片变得不必要。
可调一致性只是在延迟、可用性和新鲜度之间给出更灵活的权衡旋钮，冲突这件事本身还是会照常发生，只是处理方式可以不同。
optionExplanations_en: Carts, cached balances, and recommendation features each need different levels of freshness and availability, so letting each type of request pick its own R/W or consistency level based on its business risk serves all of them at once.
Forcing every business onto the same latency target means even low-risk recommendation reads would carry the same heavy acknowledgment wait as a balance check — completely unnecessary.
Consistency level is a replication-layer knob, a different design dimension from whether a key needs sharding at all — tuning it doesn't make sharding unnecessary.
Tunable consistency just gives a more flexible dial between latency, availability, and freshness — conflicts still happen just the same, only how they're handled can differ.

scenario: 你要设计订单 ID。要求：全局唯一、纯数字、64-bit 内、按时间大致递增、峰值超过 10,000 IDs/s。
scenario_en: You are designing order IDs that must be globally unique, numeric, fit in 64 bits, roughly time-ordered, and exceed 10,000 IDs per second.
q: 为什么单库 auto_increment 不够？
q_en: Why is a single database auto_increment not enough?
options: 它会把生成能力和可用性绑到单点数据库
它生成的 ID 不是数字
它不能保证本机递增
它生成的 ID 一定会超过 128-bit 的长度
options_en: It ties generation capacity and availability to one database point
It does not generate numeric IDs
It cannot increment locally
Its IDs are always larger than 128 bits
why: 单库自增简单，但吞吐和故障域都集中。分布式系统需要多节点独立生成，还不能互相撞号。
why_en: Single-database auto-increment is simple, but it centralizes throughput and failure risk instead of letting many nodes generate safely.
tradeoff: 集中简单性 vs 分布式可用性
whenOtherWins: 小型单体应用只需要一台数据库时，自增主键仍然最简单。

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库自动递增生成主键值的功能。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Auto-increment is a database feature that automatically assigns increasing primary-key values.

optionExplanations: 对，发号能力和这台数据库是否在线绑在了一起，数据库一挂或扛不住 10,000/s 的峰值，全公司的订单号就一起停摆。
auto_increment 生成的整数本身就是数字，这个选项对它输出格式的判断是错的。
单库自增在同一台机器上天然递增，问题不出在本机是否递增，而是多台机器之间没法协调。
32/64-bit 的自增整数不会自己跑到 128-bit，这个担心没有依据。
optionExplanations_en: Right — generation capacity and availability both get tied to whether this one database is up; if it dies or can't take the 10,000/s peak, every order ID across the company stalls with it.
auto_increment produces plain integers, which already are numbers — this option's claim about its output format is wrong.
A single database's auto-increment is inherently sequential on that one machine — the issue isn't whether it's sequential locally, it's that multiple machines can't coordinate with each other.
A 32- or 64-bit auto-increment integer never grows past 128 bits, so that worry has no basis.

scenario: ID 要 64-bit、纯数字、按时间排序。你在比较 UUID、ticket server、multi-master 自增、Snowflake。
scenario_en: IDs must be 64-bit, numeric, and time-ordered. You compare UUIDs, a ticket server, multi-master auto-increment, and Snowflake.
q: 哪个方案最贴合这些约束？
q_en: Which approach best fits these constraints?
options: Snowflake 风格按 bit 分段生成
UUID v4 随机生成
用单个 ticket server 集中自增来发号
多主库按步长自增
options_en: Snowflake-style bit-partitioned IDs
Random UUID v4
Central auto-increment from a single ticket server
Multi-master increment by step
why: Snowflake 把时间、机房、机器和序列号放进 64-bit，能多节点生成且大致按时间递增。其他方案至少会卡在长度、排序、单点或拓扑变化上。
why_en: Snowflake packs time, location, machine, and sequence into 64 bits, giving distributed generation with rough time ordering.
tradeoff: 约束贴合度 vs 依赖时钟和配置
whenOtherWins: 如果只要求全局唯一、不要求 64-bit 或排序，UUID 会更省协调。

termDefinitions.meaning: 128-bit 的通用唯一标识符，通常可由节点独立生成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A UUID is a 128-bit universally unique identifier that can usually be generated independently.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把时间戳、节点标识和序列号编码到整数 ID 的分布式 ID 思路。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Snowflake is a distributed ID scheme that encodes timestamp, node identity, and sequence into one integer.

optionExplanations: 把时间、机房、机器和序列号一起塞进 64 bit，既能多节点各自生成，又能大致按时间排序，正好一次性满足题目列出的所有约束。
UUID v4 是 128-bit 随机值，跟“64-bit 数字、按时间排序”这两条硬约束直接冲突。
单 ticket server 虽然能自增排序，但所有发号请求都要打这一台机器，规模一大就成了单点瓶颈。
多主库按步长自增能避免冲突，但节点数一变步长规则就要跟着改，运维和迁移成本会持续增加。
optionExplanations_en: Packing time, datacenter, machine, and a sequence number all into 64 bits lets multiple nodes generate independently while still staying roughly time-ordered — it satisfies every constraint listed here in one shot.
UUID v4 is a 128-bit random value, directly at odds with the two hard requirements of a 64-bit number that's time-sortable.
A single ticket server can self-increment and stay sorted, but every request for a new ID has to hit that one machine, which becomes a bottleneck at scale.
Multi-primary step increments avoid collisions, but the step rule has to change every time the node count does, adding ongoing operational and migration cost.

scenario: Web 服务器各自本地生成 UUID，几乎不需要协调。现在产品要求 ID 必须放进 64-bit 整数列，并按创建时间排序。
scenario_en: Web servers generate UUIDs locally with almost no coordination. Product now requires IDs to fit a 64-bit integer column and sort by creation time.
q: UUID 在这个场景的主要问题是什么？
q_en: What is the main issue with UUIDs here?
options: 通常太长，而且不天然按时间递增
必须依赖单点数据库
每秒只能生成一个
不能在 Web 服务器生成
options_en: They are usually too long and not naturally time-increasing
They require a single database point
They can generate only one per second
They cannot be generated on web servers
why: UUID 的优势是低协调和低碰撞概率。这里硬约束是 64-bit 数字和时间排序，所以优势不够抵消格式不匹配。
why_en: UUIDs are great for low coordination, but they do not fit a 64-bit numeric, time-ordered requirement.
tradeoff: 无协调唯一性 vs ID 格式要求
whenOtherWins: 日志追踪、对象外部引用这类不要求短整数排序的场景，UUID 很合适。
optionExplanations: 对，UUID 通常是 128-bit 且没有内建的时间语义，跟“必须塞进 64-bit 整数列、还要按创建时间排序”这两条硬要求直接对不上。
本地生成 UUID 恰恰是它的强项，不需要依赖单点数据库协调，这一点在这个场景里并不是问题所在。
UUID 每次生成都是独立事件，本地随时能连续生成很多个，不存在每秒只能生成一个的限制。
题目描述的正是 Web 服务器各自本地生成 UUID 的场景，说它不能在 Web 服务器生成与前提矛盾。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a UUID is typically 128 bits with no built-in time semantics, directly clashing with the two hard requirements of fitting a 64-bit integer column and sorting by creation time.
Generating UUIDs locally without a central database is exactly its strength — that isn't the problem in this scenario.
Each UUID generation is an independent local event; there's no limit to generating many in a row, so "only one per second" doesn't apply.
The scenario itself describes web servers generating UUIDs locally, so claiming they can't be generated there contradicts the premise.

scenario: 团队考虑用一个 ticket server 统一发号。实现简单，ID 递增，但所有服务都要请求它。
scenario_en: The team considers a ticket server that hands out IDs centrally. It is simple and increasing, but every service must call it.
q: ticket server 的最大风险是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest risk of a ticket server?
options: 单点故障和吞吐瓶颈
ID 一定不是数字
ID 一定不能递增
无法和数据库一起使用
options_en: Single point of failure and throughput bottleneck
IDs are never numeric
IDs can never increase
It cannot be used with databases
why: 集中发号容易理解，但发号服务挂了，下游都拿不到新 ID。做多 ticket server 又会引入同步和分段分配问题。
why_en: A central ticket server is easy to reason about, but if it fails every dependent service stops getting new IDs.
tradeoff: 实现简单 vs 高可用
whenOtherWins: 中小规模内部系统、发号量低且可接受主备切换时，ticket server 可以很实用。

termDefinitions.meaning: 集中生成并分发唯一 ID 的服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ticket server is a centralized service that generates and hands out unique IDs.

optionExplanations: 对，所有服务都要请求同一台机器领号，这台机器一旦挂掉，下游写入全部卡住，吞吐也天然被这一台机器的处理能力封顶。
它完全可以配置成只发数字号，说 ID 一定不是数字不成立。
ticket server 常见的实现恰恰就是靠一张自增表来发号，天生就是递增的，说它一定不能递增说反了。
它底层本来就是一张数据库自增表，和数据库一起用完全没有问题。
optionExplanations_en: Right — every service has to request a ticket from the same machine, so that one machine dying stalls every downstream write, and throughput is naturally capped by whatever that single machine can handle.
It can be configured to hand out purely numeric IDs, so claiming the IDs cannot be numbers does not hold.
A typical ticket server implementation is literally a self-incrementing database table, so it's inherently sequential — saying it can never increment has this backwards.
It is backed by an auto-increment table in the first place, so using it together with a database is a non-issue.

scenario: 两个数据库主节点各自自增。为了避免冲突，一个发奇数，一个发偶数；之后要新增第三个主节点。
scenario_en: Two database masters generate IDs independently, one odd and one even. Later, a third master must be added.
q: 多主步长自增的扩展问题是什么？
q_en: What scaling issue does multi-master step increment have?
options: 节点数变化会改变步长和号段规则，迁移很麻烦
它根本就没有办法生成连续的数字 ID 序列
它完全不依赖数据库
它天然按全局时间排序
options_en: Changing node count changes step and allocation rules, making migration hard
It cannot generate a contiguous numeric ID sequence at all
It does not rely on databases at all
It is naturally globally time-ordered
why: 按 k 个主节点设置步长时，k 变了规则也变。跨机房和节点增删都会让配置、排序和冲突处理复杂化。
why_en: When the step depends on the number of masters, adding or removing masters changes the allocation rules and complicates migration.
tradeoff: 局部生成 vs 拓扑变更成本
whenOtherWins: 固定两个主库、规模稳定、只要避免冲突不要求时间排序时，这个方案可以凑合。
optionExplanations: 对，奇偶步长是按当前的节点数量设计的，一旦节点数从两个变成三个，原来的步长和号段划分规则整个要重新设计，迁移过程还要避免和历史号段冲突。
奇偶步长发出来的仍然是普通整数，说它不能生成数字 ID 不成立。
它恰恰是完全依赖数据库自增机制实现的，说它完全不依赖数据库正好说反了。
不同主节点是各自独立按自己的节奏自增的，之间没有统一的全局时钟协调，不能保证严格按全局时间排序。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the odd/even step is designed around today's node count, so going from two primaries to three means redesigning the whole step and segment rule, with migration having to avoid colliding with old segments.
Odd/even stepping still produces ordinary integers — claiming it can't generate numeric IDs doesn't hold.
This scheme is built entirely on database auto-increment — saying it doesn't depend on a database has it exactly backwards.
Each primary increments independently at its own pace with no shared global clock coordinating them, so it can't guarantee strict global time ordering.

q: Snowflake 64-bit ID 通常由哪些部分组成？
q_en: What fields usually make up a Snowflake-style 64-bit ID?
text: 一个 Snowflake 风格 ID 常见布局是：{{sign bit}}、{{timestamp}}、datacenter ID、machine ID、sequence number。
text_en: A Snowflake-style ID commonly contains a {{sign bit}}, {{timestamp}}, datacenter ID, machine ID, and sequence number.
why: 这些字段把“什么时候生成”和“哪台机器生成”编码进同一个整数。序列号处理同一毫秒内的多次生成。
why_en: These fields encode when and where the ID was generated, with the sequence handling multiple IDs in the same millisecond.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一机器同一时间粒度内递增的小计数，用来避免撞号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sequence number is a small counter within the same time bucket on one machine to avoid collisions.

scenario: Snowflake 布局给 datacenter ID 5 bits，machine ID 5 bits。每个 bit 字段能表示 2^bits 个值。
scenario_en: A Snowflake layout gives 5 bits to datacenter ID and 5 bits to machine ID. A bit field represents 2^bits values.
q: 这两个字段带来什么容量上限？
q_en: What capacity limit do these two fields imply?
options: 32 个机房，每个机房 32 台机器
5 个机房，每个机房 5 台机器
10 个机房，共 10 台机器
64 个机房，每个机房 64 台机器
options_en: 32 data centers and 32 machines per data center
5 data centers and 5 machines per data center
10 data centers and 10 machines total
64 data centers and 64 machines per data center
why: 公式是 2^5=32。这个数字用于规划发号节点上限；超过后要重新分配 bit，或引入 worker 组、号段服务等方案。
why_en: Five bits gives 2^5 or 32 values, which bounds how many data centers and machines the ID layout can encode.

termDefinitions.meaning: 二进制位，只能表示 0 或 1；n 个 bit 能表示 2^n 种状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bit is a binary digit, and n bits can represent 2^n states.

optionExplanations: 5 bit 能表达的数值范围正好是 2 的 5 次方，两个 5-bit 字段分别限定了机房数量和每机房机器数量的独立上限。
5 个机房、每机房 5 台，这个数字对应的是 5-bit 而不是这里给定的字段位宽，跟题目给的字段设定不符。
10 这个数字既不是 2 的整数次幂，也没有对应到 5-bit 字段的表达范围，不符合这里的位宽换算。
64 对应的是 6-bit 字段能表达的范围，比题目给定的 5-bit 多了一位，直接超出了这两个字段实际能装下的容量。
optionExplanations_en: The range a 5-bit field can express is exactly 2 to the 5th power, and the two separate 5-bit fields each cap datacenter count and per-datacenter machine count independently.
5 datacenters with 5 machines each corresponds to a 3-bit field, not the 5-bit width actually given here — it doesn't match the stated field size.
10 is neither a power of two nor does it map to what a 5-bit field can express — it doesn't fit this bit-width conversion.
64 is what a 6-bit field expresses, one bit wider than the 5 bits given here — it directly exceeds what these two fields can actually hold.

scenario: Snowflake 序列号字段是 12 bits，并且每台机器每毫秒重置一次。
scenario_en: The Snowflake sequence field is 12 bits and resets every millisecond on each machine.
q: 12-bit sequence 的吞吐含义是什么？
q_en: What throughput does a 12-bit sequence imply?
options: 单机每毫秒最多 4096 个 ID
整个系统每天 4096 个 ID
单机每秒最多 12 个 ID
只能支持 4096 台机器
options_en: Up to 4096 IDs per machine per millisecond
4096 IDs per day for the whole system
Up to 12 IDs per second per machine
Only 4096 machines are supported
why: 公式是 2^12=4096。它是单机器、单毫秒内的序列空间；超过就要等下一毫秒或扩大序列字段。
why_en: Twelve bits gives 4096 sequence values per machine per millisecond; beyond that you wait or allocate more bits.
optionExplanations: 2 的 12 次方正好是这个数字，而且它是限定在“同一台机器、同一毫秒”这个窗口内的序列空间，不是全天或全系统的总量。
4096 是单机单毫秒的序列空间，不是整个系统按天累计的总量，把它套到“系统每天”的量级上换算错了。
12 bit 表达的数值范围远超过 12，说单机每秒只能发 12 个，跟这个字段实际能表达的范围差了好几个数量级。
12 bit 是序列号字段的位宽，跟能支持多少台机器毫无关系，那是 machine ID 字段该管的事。
optionExplanations_en: 2 to the 12th power comes out to exactly this number, and it's the sequence space bounded within "one machine, one millisecond" — not a system-wide or daily total.
4096 is the sequence space for one machine in one millisecond, not a daily system-wide total — applying it to a "per day" scale is the wrong conversion.
A 12-bit field expresses a range far larger than 12 — claiming a machine can only issue 12 per second is off by several orders of magnitude from what this field can actually hold.
The 12-bit width belongs to the sequence field and has nothing to do with how many machines are supported — that's the machine ID field's job.

scenario: Snowflake 用 41-bit 毫秒时间戳，相对自定义 epoch 计时。你要评估这套 ID 布局能用多久。
scenario_en: Snowflake uses a 41-bit millisecond timestamp relative to a custom epoch, and you need to estimate how long the layout lasts.
q: 41-bit 时间戳的设计影响是什么？
q_en: What design impact does a 41-bit timestamp have?
options: 约 69 年寿命，决定 epoch 和迁移计划
机器数会自动扩到 69 台
整个集群每秒总共最多只能生成 69 个 ID
可以忽略时钟回拨问题
options_en: About 69 years of lifetime, driving epoch and migration planning
The machine count automatically expands to 69
The whole cluster can generate at most 69 IDs per second
Clock rollback can be ignored
why: 公式是 (2^41-1) ms /1000/3600/24/365，约 69 年。这个数不是背诵点，它决定 epoch 选多近，以及未来何时需要迁移 ID 格式。
why_en: A 41-bit millisecond timestamp lasts about 69 years, so it drives epoch choice and long-term ID migration planning.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统约定的起始时间点，时间戳字段记录相对它经过了多久。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An epoch is the chosen start time from which timestamp values count elapsed time.

optionExplanations: 按公式换算出的这个年数，直接决定了 epoch 该定在哪一年、以及未来大概什么时候需要考虑迁移 ID 格式或扩位。
这个数字来自时间戳字段能表达多久，跟系统实际部署了多少台机器完全是两回事。
这个数字是时间戳字段的总寿命，不是发号的速率或吞吐，不能拿来当作每秒能生成多少 ID 的依据。
这个数字恰恰揭示的是时钟相关问题必须认真处理的时间窗口有多长，不能因为寿命长就忽略时钟回拨风险。
optionExplanations_en: The year figure this formula gives directly decides where to set the epoch, and roughly when the system will eventually need to consider migrating or widening the ID format.
This number comes from how long the timestamp field can express, an entirely different question from how many machines are actually deployed.
This number is the timestamp field's total lifespan, not a generation rate — it can't be used as a basis for how many IDs get issued per second.
This number actually shows just how long a window clock-related issues need to be taken seriously over — a long lifespan is no reason to ignore clock rollback risk.

scenario: 产品要求新生成的 ID 大致按创建时间排序，方便数据库按 ID 范围扫描近期数据。
scenario_en: Product wants newly generated IDs to roughly sort by creation time so the database can range-scan recent records by ID.
q: Snowflake 中哪个字段主要提供时间排序？
q_en: Which Snowflake field mainly provides time ordering?
options: 高位 timestamp 字段
低位 sequence number
sign bit
machine ID 的最后一位
options_en: The high-order timestamp field
The low-order sequence number
The sign bit
The last bit of machine ID
why: 时间戳放在高位，时间越晚，高位数值越大。低位机器和序列字段只负责同一时间附近的区分。
why_en: Putting the timestamp in high-order bits makes later times sort larger, while lower fields disambiguate nearby IDs.
tradeoff: 时间可排序 vs 时钟依赖
whenOtherWins: 如果只需要随机唯一且不按时间查，随机 UUID 不依赖机器时钟排序。
optionExplanations: 把时间戳放在最高位意味着时间越晚生成的 ID，这部分数值就越大，整个 ID 的大小关系主要由这一段决定。
低位的序列号只负责区分同一毫秒内发出的多个 ID，数值大小不携带跨毫秒的时间先后信息。
sign bit 只是为了保证 ID 在有符号整数里保持非负，不承担任何排序职责。
machine ID 只用来区分不同发号机器，它的最后一位跟这个 ID 是什么时候生成的没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: Putting the timestamp in the high bits means IDs generated later have a larger value in that segment, and that segment is what mainly drives the overall ordering of the ID.
The low-order sequence number only distinguishes multiple IDs issued within the same millisecond — its magnitude carries no information about ordering across different milliseconds.
The sign bit exists only to keep the ID non-negative as a signed integer — it carries no ordering responsibility at all.
Machine ID only distinguishes which machine issued the ID — its last bit has nothing to do with when that ID was generated.

scenario: 发号机器的系统时钟向后回拨。它可能再次使用过去的 timestamp 和相同 sequence。
scenario_en: An ID generator machine clock moves backward, so it may reuse an old timestamp with the same sequence values.
q: 时钟回拨会带来什么风险？
q_en: What risk does clock rollback create?
options: 可能生成重复 ID 或破坏时间排序
只会让 ID 更短
会自动扩展 machine ID
会让数据库读更快
options_en: It can create duplicate IDs or break time ordering
It only makes IDs shorter
It automatically expands the machine ID
It makes database reads faster
why: Snowflake 的唯一性依赖 timestamp、机器 ID、序列号组合不重复。时钟倒退会重用时间桶，所以要等待、拒绝发号或切换保护策略。
why_en: Snowflake uniqueness relies on not reusing the same timestamp-machine-sequence tuple, so clock rollback must be guarded.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常见的网络时间同步协议，用来让机器时钟尽量一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NTP is a common protocol for synchronizing machine clocks across a network.

optionExplanations: 对，时钟一旦回拨，机器可能再次落在一个刚刚用过的时间桶里，如果序列号也凑巧重叠，就会撞出两个一样的 ID，先后顺序也会因此错乱。
时钟回拨改变的是生成 ID 用的时间段落，跟 ID 本身占多少位、有多长完全没有关系。
machine ID 是配置好的固定字段，不会因为本机时钟往回走就自动扩展位数。
时钟回拨是发号服务这一层的问题，跟数据库读取速度快慢没有任何因果关系。
optionExplanations_en: Right — once the clock rolls back, the machine can land in a time bucket it already used, and if the sequence number happens to overlap too, two identical IDs collide and the ordering breaks.
Clock rollback changes which time segment gets used for generation — it has nothing to do with how many bits or how long the ID itself is.
Machine ID is a fixed configured field — it doesn't automatically widen just because the local clock moved backward.
Clock rollback is an issue at the ID-generation layer, with no causal connection to how fast the database can read.

scenario: 两台发号进程被错误配置成同一个 datacenter ID 和 machine ID，并且它们在同一毫秒内发号。
scenario_en: Two generator processes are misconfigured with the same datacenter ID and machine ID and generate IDs in the same millisecond.
q: 机器 ID 配置错误会导致什么？
q_en: What can wrong machine-ID assignment cause?
options: 不同机器可能生成相同 ID
ID 会自动转成 UUID
系统吞吐提升一倍
timestamp 字段失效为 0
options_en: Different machines may generate the same ID
IDs automatically become UUIDs
System throughput doubles
The timestamp field becomes zero
why: 机器 ID 是分布式唯一性的隔离字段。两个进程共享同一身份时，timestamp 和 sequence 撞上的概率就变成真实风险。
why_en: Machine ID separates generators; if two processes share it, matching timestamp and sequence values can collide.
optionExplanations: 对，机器身份本来是用来把不同机器的号段隔开的，两台机器共用同一个身份，在同一毫秒发号时，timestamp+machine+sequence 这组合就可能完全撞上。
机器 ID 配置错误只是让唯一性隔离失效，不会让发号器输出的格式从数字自动变成 UUID。
两台机器共享同一身份是配置错误，不是扩容手段，不会带来吞吐翻倍的效果，反而增加了撞号风险。
timestamp 字段照常按本机时钟正常取值，不会因为机器身份配置错误就失效变成 0。
optionExplanations_en: Right — machine identity exists to keep different machines' ID segments apart; two machines sharing the same identity and issuing in the same millisecond can produce the exact same timestamp+machine+sequence combination.
A misconfigured machine ID only breaks the uniqueness isolation — it doesn't change the generator's output format from numbers into UUIDs.
Two machines sharing one identity is a misconfiguration, not a scaling technique — it doesn't double throughput, it just raises collision risk.
The timestamp field still reads normally off the local clock — a misconfigured machine ID doesn't zero it out.

q: 调整 Snowflake bit 分配时，哪些取舍成立？
q_en: When tuning Snowflake bit allocation, which tradeoffs are valid?
options: 更多 timestamp bits 能延长可用年限
更多 sequence bits 能提高单机同毫秒吞吐
更多 machine bits 能支持更多发号节点
更多 sign bits 会自动提升一致性
options_en: More timestamp bits extend the usable lifetime
More sequence bits raise per-machine per-millisecond throughput
More machine bits support more generator nodes
More sign bits automatically improve consistency
why: 64-bit 总预算固定，给一个字段更多 bit，就要从别的字段拿。调参要看寿命、节点数、单机峰值哪个更紧。
why_en: The 64-bit budget is fixed, so bit allocation trades lifetime, generator count, and per-machine burst capacity.
optionExplanations: 对，时间戳字段变宽，能表达的毫秒数变多，系统在溢出前能用的年限也就相应变长。
对，序列号字段变宽，同一台机器在同一毫秒内能发的号就更多，抗的住更高的瞬时峰值。
对，机器 ID 字段变宽，能容纳的独立发号节点数量就更多，扩容上限也随之提高。
sign bit 只有一位，作用是保证 ID 非负，跟系统的一致性保证没有任何关系，加多少 sign bit 都不会提升一致性。
optionExplanations_en: Right — widening the timestamp field lets it express more milliseconds, extending how many years the system can run before overflow.
Right — widening the sequence field lets one machine issue more IDs within the same millisecond, absorbing a higher instantaneous peak.
Right — widening the machine field lets more independent generating nodes exist at once, raising the scale-out ceiling.
The sign bit is a single bit whose only job is keeping the ID non-negative — it has nothing to do with consistency guarantees, no matter how many sign bits were added.
scenario: 64-bit ID 总预算固定，业务要求服务至少跑 50 年、且单机每毫秒能发上千个 ID。
scenario_en: The 64-bit ID budget is fixed, and the service must run for 50+ years while issuing thousands of IDs per millisecond per node.

q: Snowflake 为什么能多节点生成可排序 ID？
q_en: Why can Snowflake generate sortable IDs on many nodes?
steps: timestamp 放在高位，让晚生成的 ID 通常更大
datacenter 和 machine 字段隔离不同发号节点
sequence 字段处理同一机器同一毫秒内的多次生成
所有字段拼成一个 64-bit 数字返回
why: 这条链把排序、分布式唯一性和同毫秒并发分开说。面试里不要只说“用 Snowflake”四个字。
why_en: The reasoning separates time ordering, generator identity, and same-millisecond concurrency instead of just naming Snowflake.

scenario: ID 生成器是下单、发帖、写日志的前置依赖。服务不可用时，业务写入都会被卡住。
scenario_en: The ID generator is a prerequisite for orders, posts, and logs; when it is unavailable, business writes are blocked.
q: ID 生成器的高可用重点是什么？
q_en: What is the high-availability focus for an ID generator?
options: 让多个独立节点本地发号，并严格分配唯一机器身份
只部署一个最大规格机器
让客户端自己随机猜 ID
每一次发号都要先跑一遍完整的跨机房强同步事务
options_en: Let multiple independent nodes generate locally with unique machine identities
Deploy one largest possible machine
Let clients randomly guess IDs
Run a full cross-region strong-sync transaction for every ID
why: 发号服务不能成为写路径单点。多节点本地发号能抗单机故障，但机器身份和时钟保护必须管严。
why_en: The generator must not be a write-path single point, so local multi-node generation needs strict identity and clock safeguards.
tradeoff: 本地高可用 vs 配置纪律
whenOtherWins: 低吞吐内部后台任务可以用单主号段服务，简单性更重要。
optionExplanations: 让多个节点各自在本地就能发号，任何一台挂了不会拖垮别的节点，但前提是必须严格分配、不能重复的机器身份，否则会撞号。
只部署一台最大规格的机器仍然是单点，这台机器一旦故障，下单、发帖等业务写入会全部被卡住。
让客户端自己随机猜 ID 完全没有唯一性保证，撞号概率会随规模增长变得不可接受。
每次发号都做跨机房同步事务，会把本该很快的发号操作拖慢成跨网络的强一致写入，代价太高。
optionExplanations_en: Letting multiple nodes each generate locally means one going down doesn't take the others with it — but only if machine identities are strictly and uniquely assigned, or collisions follow.
Deploying just one maximally-sized machine is still a single point of failure — if it goes down, every downstream write like orders or posts gets stuck.
Letting the client randomly guess an ID gives no uniqueness guarantee at all, and collision odds become unacceptable as scale grows.
