why: 队列深度直接说明生产快于消费。扩 worker 增加消费能力，或限流入口避免延迟继续扩大。
why_en: Queue depth shows producers are outpacing consumers, so scale workers or throttle incoming sends.
whenOtherWins: 如果积压来自第三方限流，盲目扩 worker 无效，要改退避和发送速率。

termDefinitions.meaning: 队列中还没被处理的任务积压。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Backlog is the number of queued jobs waiting to be processed.

optionExplanations: 先看 backlog 是在持续增长还是抖一下就回落，前者要加消费能力，后者只是峰值。
模板字符数长短跟队列为什么积压没有直接因果关系，改短文案解决不了消费跟不上生产的问题。
用户头像缓存命中率是完全不相关的另一个系统的指标，跟通知队列积压没有关联。
数据库表名长度纯粹是命名规范，跟队列积压、通知延迟这些问题毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: First check whether the backlog keeps growing or just spikes and drains — the former needs more consumers, the latter is only a burst.
Template character count has no causal link to why the queue is backing up — shortening the copy doesn't fix consumption falling behind production.
User avatar cache hit rate belongs to an entirely unrelated system, with no connection to the notification queue backing up.
Database table name length is purely a naming convention, with nothing to do with queue backlog or notification delay.

scenario: 通知 API 只给内部服务或可信客户端用；如果被滥用，会变成垃圾通知入口。
scenario_en: The notification API is for internal services or trusted clients; abuse would turn it into a spam gateway.
q: API 层先做什么安全控制？
q_en: What security control belongs at the API layer?
options: 认证调用方并保护密钥
把 appSecret 下发给所有用户
只依赖消息模板
关闭所有日志
options_en: Authenticate callers and protect secrets.
Ship appSecret to every user.
Rely only on templates.
Disable all logs.
why: 通知入口必须先确认调用方身份，不然任何人都能触发发送。密钥泄漏后要能轮换，并配合限流。
why_en: Authenticate notification callers because an unauthenticated send API becomes a spam endpoint.
whenOtherWins: 如果所有调用都在私有网络内，也仍要用服务身份或 mTLS 做内层保护。

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端或服务接入 API 的凭据对，secret 必须保密。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An appKey/appSecret pair authenticates API callers, and the secret must stay private.

termDefinitions.meaning: Mutual TLS，客户端和服务端都用证书互相认证。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: mTLS is Mutual TLS, where client and server authenticate each other with certificates.

optionExplanations: 先确认调用方到底是谁、再妥善保护好用来鉴权的密钥，是防止这个入口被滥用成垃圾通知源头的第一道关卡。
把 appSecret 下发给所有用户，等于让任何人都能拿着这个密钥冒充可信调用方，入口的鉴权形同虚设。
只依赖消息模板管的是内容格式，完全挡不住一个未经身份验证的调用方触发发送。
关闭所有日志不但没有增加任何安全防护，反而让真出问题时连排查和追溯的线索都没有了。
optionExplanations_en: Confirming who the caller actually is and properly protecting the credentials used to authenticate is the first line of defense against this endpoint becoming a source of spam notifications.
Handing out the appSecret to every user lets anyone impersonate a trusted caller with that key, making authentication at this entry point meaningless.
Relying only on message templates addresses content format — it does nothing to stop an unauthenticated caller from triggering a send in the first place.
Turning off all logging adds no security protection at all, and it strips away every trail needed to investigate when something actually does go wrong.

scenario: 产品团队想知道通知是否真的带来打开、点击和后续转化，而不仅是发出去了。
scenario_en: The product team wants to know opens, clicks, and downstream conversion, not just whether messages were sent.
q: 要接入哪类组件？
q_en: What component should be integrated?
options: 事件追踪/analytics 管线
接入一个专门的 DNS resolver 组件
URL frontier
关系图数据库
options_en: An event-tracking or analytics pipeline.
A DNS resolver component
A URL frontier.
A social graph database.
why: 发送成功只说明供应商接收了请求，不能说明用户互动。埋点能反哺模板、限频和投放策略。
why_en: Delivery success does not measure user engagement, so tracking opens and clicks feeds future notification strategy.
whenOtherWins: 如果是强事务告警，首要指标是送达和失败告警，互动分析可以后置。

termDefinitions.meaning: 收集和分析事件数据，用于理解用户行为和系统效果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Analytics collects and analyzes event data to understand behavior and outcomes.

tradeoff: 投递成功信号 vs 用户互动信号
optionExplanations: 接一条事件追踪或 analytics 管线，才能真正看到用户有没有打开、点击、以及后续是否转化，而不只是知道消息发出去了。
DNS resolver 负责域名解析，跟通知有没有带来用户打开、点击这些互动行为完全不是一回事。
URL frontier 是爬虫系统里管理待抓 URL 的组件，跟通知系统要追踪的用户互动毫无关系。
关系图数据库擅长表达实体间的关系，不是专门用来采集和分析打开、点击这类事件流的组件。
optionExplanations_en: Wiring up an event-tracking or analytics pipeline is what actually shows whether users opened, clicked, and later converted — not just that a message went out.
A DNS resolver handles domain resolution, entirely unrelated to whether a notification drove any open or click behavior.
A URL frontier is the pending-URL component in a crawler system, unrelated to the user engagement a notification system needs to track.
A graph database is good at modeling relationships between entities — it isn't a purpose-built component for collecting and analyzing an open/click event stream.

scenario: worker 调第三方发送失败；系统既不能丢通知，也不能无限静默重试。
scenario_en: A worker fails to send through a provider; the system must not lose the notification or retry silently forever.
q: 失败后的可靠处理顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the reliable failure-handling sequence?
steps: 若重试耗尽，告警开发者或切备用供应商
worker 调 provider 失败
按退避策略重新入队等待下一次 worker 拉取
读取持久 notification log 重建任务
成功则标记完成并记录结果，否则进入重试判断
why: 先有持久记录，失败才有东西可重试；重试要有退避和上限。否则不是打爆供应商，就是故障没人知道。
why_en: Durable intent enables retry, and bounded backoff keeps failures visible instead of hammering the provider.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Log[Notification log] --> W[Worker]
  W --> P[Provider]
  P -->|fail| R[Retry with backoff]
  R --> W
  R -->|exhausted| A[Alert or failover]
  P -->|ok| Done[Mark sent]

termDefinitions.meaning: 重试间隔逐步拉长，避免故障时持续打满下游。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Backoff gradually increases retry delay to avoid overwhelming a failing dependency.

scenario: 通知希望尽快到达，但大促高峰时允许几十秒级延迟，不能为了低延迟丢数据。
scenario_en: Notifications should arrive quickly, but during campaign peaks a delay of tens of seconds is acceptable; data loss is not.
q: 这更像什么系统语义？
q_en: What delivery semantics does this imply?
options: soft real-time，用队列缓冲峰值
hard real-time，必须固定毫秒送达
离线批处理，第二天统一发
纯客户端轮询
options_en: Soft real-time with queues absorbing peaks.
Hard real-time with fixed millisecond delivery.
Offline batch, sent the next day.
Pure client polling.
why: 需求说尽快但可延迟，所以队列换来削峰和可靠性。硬实时会增加复杂度和成本，这里不值得。
why_en: This is soft real-time: queueing can trade small delay for reliability and burst absorption.
tradeoff: 低延迟 vs 削峰可靠性
whenOtherWins: 如果是电话呼叫控制或交易撮合，硬实时约束才可能主导设计。

termDefinitions.meaning: 软实时表示越快越好，但小延迟可接受。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Soft real-time means faster is better, but small delays are acceptable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 硬实时表示错过时间界限就是系统失败。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hard real-time means missing the deadline is a system failure.

optionExplanations: 要求是尽快到达但高峰期能接受几十秒延迟、绝不能为了低延迟丢数据，这正是软实时的定义——用队列先缓冲峰值，用可靠性换一点可以接受的延迟。
硬实时要求固定毫秒级必达，会显著增加系统复杂度和成本，跟这里“允许几十秒延迟”的实际需求不匹配，是过度设计。
离线批处理要到第二天才统一发送，跟“尽快到达”这个基本诉求完全对不上。
纯客户端轮询意味着用户设备要不停主动去问有没有新通知，既费电又没法保证消息不丢。
optionExplanations_en: Wanting delivery as fast as possible while tolerating tens of seconds of delay at peak, and never trading reliability away for lower latency, is exactly the definition of soft real-time — a queue buffers the peak, trading a bit of acceptable delay for reliability.
Hard real-time demanding guaranteed millisecond delivery adds significant complexity and cost, mismatched with the actual requirement here of tolerating tens of seconds of delay — overkill.
Offline batch processing that sends everything the next day is completely at odds with the basic requirement of arriving as soon as possible.
Pure client polling means the device has to keep actively asking whether there's anything new, which drains battery and still can't guarantee nothing gets missed.

scenario: notification server 位于业务服务和队列之间，是发送入口而不是最终投递方。
scenario_en: The notification server sits between business services and queues; it is the send entry point, not the final delivery provider.
q: 它通常负责哪些事？
q_en: What does it usually handle?
options: 认证和基础参数校验
读取用户/设备/模板元数据
把事件写入对应消息队列
直接替代 APNS/FCM 的全球网络
options_en: Authentication and basic validation.
Fetching user, device, and template metadata.
Writing events to the right message queue.
Replacing the global APNS/FCM networks.
why: 入口层适合做轻量校验、补齐元数据和入队。真正跨运营商或平台的投递仍由第三方网络完成。
why_en: The entry layer validates, enriches, and enqueues; platform delivery still belongs to external push, SMS, or email providers.

termDefinitions.meaning: Apple Push Notification Service，iOS 推送网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: APNS is Apple's iOS push notification network.

termDefinitions.meaning: Firebase Cloud Messaging，常见 Android 推送网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FCM is a common Android push notification network.

optionExplanations: 对，认证调用方和校验基础参数是入口层该做的轻量检查，把不合规的请求先挡在外面。
对，读取用户、设备和模板这些元数据，把业务意图补全成一条规范的发送事件。
对，把补全好的事件写进对应的消息队列，交给后面的 worker 去处理，这正是入口层该完成的动作。
跨运营商、跨平台的真实投递依赖的是 APNS/FCM 这类外部网络的全球基础设施，notification server 自己没有能力也不该替代它们。
optionExplanations_en: Right — authenticating the caller and validating basic parameters is exactly the lightweight check an entry layer should do, keeping malformed requests out.
Right — reading user, device, and template metadata rounds business intent out into a properly formed send event.
Right — writing that completed event into the appropriate message queue for downstream workers to handle is exactly what the entry layer is meant to do.
Actual cross-carrier, cross-platform delivery depends on external networks like APNS/FCM's global infrastructure — a notification server has neither the ability nor the reason to replace that.

scenario: 用户不在 App 前台，但你希望新消息或提醒主动出现在锁屏上。
scenario_en: The user is not actively using the app, but you want new messages or alerts to appear on the lock screen.
q: 通知系统为什么偏 push？
q_en: Why does the notification system favor push?
options: 客户端轮询更省电
服务端经平台主动触达设备，不靠客户端频繁拉取
所有通知都必须等到用户主动打开 App 才显示
push 不需要用户授权
options_en: Client polling saves more battery.
The server reaches devices through platform services without frequent client pulls.
Every notification must wait until the user opens the app
Push requires no user permission.
why: 移动端频繁 pull 会浪费电量和网络，push 把唤醒交给平台。代价是依赖 APNS/FCM 等外部服务和用户授权。
why_en: Push avoids constant client polling by using platform delivery services, at the cost of provider dependency and permissions.
tradeoff: 主动触达 vs 外部平台依赖
whenOtherWins: 如果只是站内消息列表，用户打开页面时 pull 最新数据就够。

termDefinitions.meaning: 平台主动把通知投递到设备的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A push notification is delivered proactively to a device by a platform service.

optionExplanations: 客户端频繁轮询恰恰更费电，跟省电这个说法正好相反，也正是要用 push 来避免的做法。
设备不在前台时，把唤醒这件事交给平台自己的网络主动推送，客户端不需要频繁主动去问有没有新消息，省电也省网络。
强制所有通知都等用户打开 App 才能看到，完全违背了“主动出现在锁屏上”这个诉求。
push 依然需要用户主动授权通知权限，说不需要授权不符合实际情况。
optionExplanations_en: Frequent client polling is actually what drains battery — the opposite of what's claimed, and exactly the behavior push is meant to avoid.

When the device isn't in the foreground, letting the platform's own network handle waking it means the client doesn't have to keep actively asking whether there's anything new — saving both battery and network.
Forcing every notification to wait until the user opens the app directly contradicts the goal of proactively showing up on the lock screen.
Push still requires the user to actively grant notification permission — claiming no permission is needed doesn't match reality.

scenario: 同一条促销消息要发给 iOS 和 Android 用户；两个平台的推送网关不同。
scenario_en: The same campaign must reach iOS and Android users, but the platforms use different push gateways.
q: 通道适配层要区分什么？
q_en: What should the channel adapter distinguish?
options: APNS 给 iOS，FCM 常给 Android
把 APNS 用于 SMS，把 FCM 用于 email
两者都只负责模板存储
两者都能绕过设备 token
options_en: APNS for iOS, FCM commonly for Android.
APNS for SMS and FCM for email
Both only store templates.
Both bypass device tokens.
why: 不同平台网关、凭据和 payload 格式不同，所以 adapter 要按平台封装。业务服务不该直接散落这些差异。
why_en: APNS and FCM differ in gateway, credentials, and payload shape, so hide them behind platform adapters.
whenOtherWins: 如果只支持一个平台，先做单 adapter 可以更快上线。

termDefinitions.meaning: Apple Push Notification Service，Apple 设备的推送服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: APNS is Apple Push Notification Service for Apple devices.

termDefinitions.meaning: Firebase Cloud Messaging，Google/Firebase 提供的推送服务，常用于 Android。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FCM is Firebase Cloud Messaging, commonly used for Android push.

tradeoff: 平台差异封装 vs adapter 维护成本
optionExplanations: 苹果和安卓两个平台走的是不同的推送网关、不同的凭据体系、不同的 payload 格式，通道适配层要按平台各自封装这些差异。
把两个平台的推送网关和短信、邮件这两个完全不同的通道混在一起对应，完全说错了这几种通道各自服务的对象。
这两个网关的核心职责是把消息真正推送到设备上，不是负责存储模板，说它们只负责模板存储不准确。
设备 token 是推送定位到具体设备的关键标识，两个网关都需要依赖它，不存在绕过设备 token 的说法。
optionExplanations_en: iOS and Android go through different push gateways with different credential systems and different payload formats, so the channel adapter layer has to wrap each platform's differences separately.
Mixing up these two device-push gateways with SMS and email — a completely different pair of channels — misstates what each of these actually serves.
Both gateways' core job is actually pushing the message to the device, not storing templates — claiming they're only for template storage isn't accurate.
A device token is the key identifier that lets a push land on a specific device — both gateways depend on it, so there's no such thing as bypassing device tokens.

scenario: SMS 和 email 都能自己搭服务，但交付率、退信处理和运营商接入都很麻烦。
scenario_en: SMS and email can be self-hosted, but deliverability, bounces, and carrier integration are hard.
q: 为什么常用第三方 gateway？
q_en: Why use third-party gateways?
options: 它们提供投递网络、交付率工具和分析能力
它们可以让用户从此彻底无法退订消息
它们可以替代所有业务数据库
它们保证没有任何费用
options_en: They provide delivery networks, deliverability tooling, and analytics.
They make opting out impossible for users
They can replace all business databases.
They guarantee zero cost.
why: SMS/email 的难点在外部网络和送达质量，商业 gateway 通常更成熟。代价是成本、限流和供应商锁定。
why_en: SMS and email delivery quality depends on external networks, where commercial gateways are usually stronger.
tradeoff: 交付能力 vs 成本和锁定
whenOtherWins: 如果是内部低量邮件，自己维护 SMTP 也可能够用。

termDefinitions.meaning: 连接内部系统和外部投递网络的服务入口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A gateway connects an internal system to an external delivery network.

termDefinitions.meaning: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol，邮件服务器之间传送邮件的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SMTP is the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol used between mail servers.

optionExplanations: 交付率优化、退信处理、运营商接入这些都是专门的技术和运维投入，成熟的第三方 gateway 已经把这些沉淀成了现成能力，不用自己从头搭。
第三方 gateway 本身不会阻止用户退订，退订是业务层需要自己实现和遵守的机制。
第三方 gateway 提供的是投递能力，不会替代承载业务核心数据的数据库，这两者职责完全不同。
使用第三方 gateway 通常按量或按功能计费，说它们保证完全没有任何费用不符合实际情况。
optionExplanations_en: Delivery rate optimization, bounce handling, and carrier integration all take specialized engineering and operations investment, which a mature third-party gateway has already built out as ready-made capability instead of building from scratch.
A third-party gateway itself doesn't stop users from opting out — opt-out is a mechanism the business layer needs to implement and honor on its own.
What a third-party gateway provides is delivery capability — it doesn't replace the database that holds core business data; the two serve entirely different roles.
Using a third-party gateway is typically billed by volume or feature — claiming they guarantee zero cost at all doesn't match reality.

scenario: 业务服务不会直接调用每个第三方；它们先调用内部 notification API。
scenario_en: Business services do not call every provider directly; they call an internal notification API first.
q: notification server 入口最少要做什么？
q_en: What must the notification server entry point do?
options: 认证调用方、校验目标、取模板/设置并入队
直接保证用户已打开通知
替用户安装 App
替 APNS 保存整整五年的投递历史记录
options_en: Authenticate callers, validate targets, fetch templates/settings, and enqueue.
Guarantee the user has opened the notification.
Install the app for the user.
Store five years of APNS delivery history
why: 入口层负责把业务意图变成规范的发送事件，不能把脏数据直接丢给 worker。真正投递由后面的 worker 和 provider 完成。
why_en: The entry layer turns business intent into a valid send event before workers and providers handle delivery.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次待发送通知的结构化事件，包含用户、通道、模板和变量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A send event is a structured notification intent with user, channel, template, and variables.

optionExplanations: 先确认调用方身份、校验发送目标合不合法、拿到对应的模板和用户设置，再把这些拼成一个规范事件入队，是入口层最起码要完成的工作。
入口层只负责把发送事件送进队列，它没有能力也不负责保证用户真的已经打开了这条通知。
替用户安装 App 完全超出了通知服务的职责范围，这不是它该做的事。
保存历史数据是供应商或专门的存储系统的职责，notification server 入口层不该越俎代庖替 APNS 存这些。
optionExplanations_en: Confirming the caller's identity, validating the send target, fetching the right template and user settings, then assembling all of that into a proper event to enqueue is the bare minimum the entry layer needs to do.
The entry layer is only responsible for putting the send event into the queue — it has neither the ability nor the responsibility to guarantee the user actually opened the notification.
Installing the app on the user's behalf is completely outside a notification service's scope — that's not its job at all.
Retaining historical records is the provider's or a dedicated storage system's responsibility — the notification server's entry layer shouldn't be overstepping to store that on APNS's behalf.

scenario: 大促开始十分钟内涌入几百万通知；第三方通道有每秒发送上限。
scenario_en: A campaign creates millions of notifications in ten minutes, while the provider has a per-second send limit.
q: 队列在这里主要解决什么？
q_en: What does the queue mainly solve here?
options: 削峰缓冲，让 worker 按下游能力消化
让第三方没有限流
让每一条通知都退化成同步阻塞的下游请求
删除用户设置检查
options_en: Buffer bursts so workers consume at downstream capacity.
Make providers have no rate limits.
Turn every notification into a synchronous blocking downstream call
Remove user settings checks.
why: 队列把入口峰值变成可控消费速率，避免 API 线程等待供应商。代价是用户收到通知可能晚一点。
why_en: Queues convert producer bursts into controlled consumer throughput, trading latency for stability.
tradeoff: 峰值吸收 vs 端到端延迟
whenOtherWins: 如果通知必须毫秒级响应，队列延迟预算要更严格，甚至走专用高优先级通道。

termDefinitions.meaning: 限制单位时间内可发送或调用的数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rate limit caps how many sends or calls can happen per time window.

optionExplanations: 队列先把瞬间涌入的几百万条消息缓冲住，再让 worker 按第三方通道实际能承受的速率一点点消化，避免直接冲垮下游限速。
第三方通道自身的限流是它自己设定的规则，队列没有能力也不负责让第三方取消这个限制。
把所有通知变成同步请求恰恰是队列想要避免的模式，同步意味着每条消息都要卡住等下游响应，完全没法应对峰值。
删除用户设置检查跟能不能扛住流量峰值毫无关系，反而会让不该发的通知也被发出去。
optionExplanations_en: The queue first buffers the instant flood of millions of messages, then lets workers drain it at whatever rate the third-party channel can actually sustain, instead of slamming straight into its downstream rate limit.
A third-party channel's own rate limit is a rule it sets itself — a queue has neither the ability nor the job of getting the provider to lift that limit.

Turning every notification into a synchronous request is exactly what a queue is meant to avoid — synchronous means every message blocks waiting on a downstream response, which can't absorb a burst at all.
Removing the user-settings check has nothing to do with surviving a traffic spike — it would just let notifications that shouldn't be sent go out anyway.

scenario: 一个服务要给 500 万用户发送同一活动提醒，但每个用户的语言和退订设置不同。
scenario_en: A service must send the same campaign to 5 million users, but each user has different language and opt-out settings.
q: fanout 该在哪里展开？
q_en: Where should fanout be expanded?
options: 在后台批处理/队列中分批展开，并逐个检查设置
让调用方同步循环 500 万次
把一个事件直接丢给 APNS 让它猜用户
只给第一个用户发送
options_en: Expand in batches through background jobs/queues and check settings per user.
Make the caller synchronously loop 5 million times.
Send one event to APNS and let it guess users.
Send only to the first user.
why: 大 fanout 会很慢，要异步分批处理；每个用户仍要套模板、查设置和选通道。
why_en: Large fanout should be batched asynchronously while still applying per-user settings and templates.
tradeoff: 批量吞吐 vs 个性化检查
whenOtherWins: 如果只是给一个用户发交易通知，不需要 campaign fanout。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个发送意图展开成许多接收者任务的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fanout expands one send intent into many recipient-specific tasks.

optionExplanations: 把 500 万用户的发送拆成一批批在后台异步处理，每个用户仍然要单独套上自己的语言模板、检查自己的退订设置，批处理和逐个个性化检查并不冲突。
让调用方同步循环 500 万次，会让发起这次调用的线程被阻塞极长时间，根本不现实。
把一个笼统的事件直接丢给 APNS 自己猜该发给谁，APNS 只负责真正的设备推送，不负责理解你的用户列表和个性化逻辑。
只给第一个用户发送等于放弃了其余 499 万多个用户，完全没有完成这次活动提醒的目标。
optionExplanations_en: Splitting the 500 million sends into batches processed asynchronously in the background still lets each user get their own language template and their own opt-out check — batching and per-user personalization aren't in conflict.
Having the caller loop synchronously 500 million times would block the calling thread for an unrealistically long time.

Handing one generic event straight to APNS and letting it guess who to send to misunderstands its role — APNS only handles the actual device push, not understanding your user list or personalization logic.
Sending to only the first user abandons the other 4.99 million-plus users entirely, completely failing the goal of this campaign reminder.

scenario: 用户卸载重装 App 或更换手机后，旧 device token 可能失效。
scenario_en: After a user reinstalls the app or changes phones, old device tokens may become invalid.
q: token 生命周期怎么处理？
q_en: How should token lifecycle be handled?
options: 更新新 token，清理旧 token
永远保留一个用户名下所有的旧 token
只把 token 写进模板
用户退订时删除邮箱
options_en: Update new tokens and prune old ones.
Keep every old token forever
Put tokens only inside templates.
Delete email addresses when users opt out.
why: device token 是会变化的路由地址，服务端要更新和淘汰。否则会浪费发送额度，还可能漏发新设备。
why_en: Device tokens are mutable routing identifiers, so update and prune them over time.
whenOtherWins: 如果是 email 地址变更，也要类似做验证和更新，但机制不同。

termDefinitions.meaning: 推送平台给某个设备安装分配的投递标识。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A device token is the delivery identifier assigned by a push platform to an app installation.

optionExplanations: 卸载重装或换机会让旧 token 失效，服务端要及时更新成新 token、清理掉不再有效的旧记录，才能保证 push 真的送到当前设备上。
永远保留所有旧 token 会让系统不断往已经失效的设备发送，白白浪费发送额度，还可能让新设备漏收通知。
把 token 写进模板混淆了内容格式和设备路由信息，模板本该跟具体某台设备的 token 无关。
用户退订通知和邮箱地址是否还存在是两件不同的事，退订不该直接触发删除邮箱这个联系方式本身。
optionExplanations_en: A reinstall or new phone invalidates the old token, so the server needs to promptly update to the new one and clean up the stale record, or push won't actually reach the current device.
Keeping every old token forever means the system keeps wasting send quota on devices that no longer exist, and can miss delivering to the new device entirely.
Writing the token into the template conflates content format with device routing information — a template shouldn't be tied to any specific device's token at all.
Opting out of notifications and whether an email address still exists are two different things — opting out shouldn't directly trigger deleting that contact detail itself.

scenario: 业务方想区分“我们提交给供应商了”和“供应商确认送达/失败了”。
scenario_en: The business wants to distinguish submitted-to-provider from provider-confirmed delivered or failed.
q: 需要接哪类反馈？
q_en: What feedback should be integrated?
options: 接 provider delivery receipt
DNS TTL 刷新
接一个 URL Seen 专用的 Bloom filter
聊天 heartbeat
options_en: Consume provider delivery receipts.
DNS TTL refresh.
URL Seen Bloom filter
Chat heartbeat.
why: 提交成功不等于用户收到，receipt 能更新发送状态和失败原因。代价是回调也要鉴权、去重和重试。
why_en: Provider receipts distinguish accepted requests from delivery outcomes and failure reasons.
whenOtherWins: 如果通道不提供 receipt，只能用提交状态和抽样监控近似。

termDefinitions.meaning: 第三方回传的投递结果事件，例如已送达、失败或退信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A delivery receipt is a provider event reporting delivered, failed, or bounced status.

tradeoff: 供应商反馈闭环 vs 额外异步状态处理
optionExplanations: 接入供应商的投递回执，才能真正区分“我们提交给供应商了”和“供应商确认送达或失败了”这两个不同阶段的状态。
DNS TTL 刷新管的是域名解析缓存的有效期，跟通知有没有真正送达完全不是一回事。
URL Seen 的 Bloom filter 是爬虫系统里用来判断 URL 是否见过的结构，跟通知投递状态毫无关系。
聊天心跳检测的是连接是否存活，跟供应商是否确认送达这条通知是两个不同系统里的不同概念。
optionExplanations_en: Wiring up the provider's delivery receipt is what actually distinguishes "we submitted it to the provider" from "the provider confirmed delivery or failure" as two separate states.
DNS TTL refresh governs how long a domain resolution cache stays valid — entirely unrelated to whether a notification was actually delivered.
URL Seen's Bloom filter is a structure a crawler uses to check whether a URL has been seen before — unrelated to notification delivery status.
Chat heartbeats detect whether a connection is still alive — a different concept in a different system from whether a provider confirmed this notification's delivery.

scenario: email provider 返回 429；继续全速重试会让失败更久。
scenario_en: The email provider returns HTTP 429; retrying at full speed will prolong the failure.
q: worker 应该怎么退避？
q_en: How should workers back off?
options: 按 provider 和通道做指数退避，并保留最大重试次数
立刻无限重试同一请求
把所有 email 改成 SMS
直接把 notification log 这张表整个删掉
options_en: Use provider/channel-level exponential backoff with a retry cap.
Retry the same request forever immediately.
Convert every email to SMS.
Drop the notification log table entirely
why: 429 表示下游限流，退避要降低对该 provider 的压力。最大次数和死信队列能让故障可见。
why_en: A 429 means the downstream is throttling, so exponential backoff and retry caps keep pressure controlled.
whenOtherWins: 如果是永久错误如无效邮箱，应该直接标失败，不进入多轮重试。

termDefinitions.meaning: Too Many Requests，表示调用方超过限流。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests means the caller exceeded a rate limit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保存多次处理失败任务的队列，便于排查或人工处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dead-letter queue stores jobs that failed repeatedly for later inspection.

optionExplanations: 429 说明下游正在限流，按供应商和通道分别做指数退避、并设一个最大重试次数，才能既给对方喘息空间，又不让失败无限拖下去。
立刻无限重试同一个已经返回 429 的请求，只会给已经在限流的供应商施加更大压力，让失败持续更久。
把所有 email 直接改成 SMS 没有解决 email 供应商限流这个根本问题，只是换了个通道回避问题。
删除 notification log 不但没有缓解限流，反而丢掉了本该用来排查这次限流事件的记录。
optionExplanations_en: A 429 means the downstream is rate-limiting, so applying exponential backoff per provider and channel with a capped retry count gives it room to recover without letting the failure drag on indefinitely.
Immediately retrying the same request that already got a 429, at full speed, just piles more pressure onto a provider that's already rate-limiting — prolonging the failure.
Switching every email to SMS doesn't address the root cause of the email provider rate-limiting — it just dodges the problem by changing channels.
Deleting the notification log doesn't relieve the rate limit at all — it just throws away the very record needed to investigate this incident.

scenario: 通知系统已经能发送，但运营需要知道延迟、失败、重复和用户互动。
scenario_en: The notification system can send messages, but operations need latency, failure, duplicate, and engagement visibility.
q: 观测面板至少看什么？
q_en: What should the dashboard include?
options: 看队列、延迟、错误、重复、互动
网页 PageRank
聊天在线绿点数作为唯一指标
DNS cache 命中率作为所有通道指标
options_en: Track queues, latency, errors, duplicates, engagement.
Web PageRank.
Chat online-dot count as the only metric.
DNS cache hit rate for every channel.
why: 这些指标覆盖系统健康和产品效果：发得快不快、失败在哪、是否扰民、有没有互动。
why_en: These metrics cover both system health and product outcome: speed, failures, duplicates, and engagement.

termDefinitions.meaning: 收到通知后打开或查看的人数比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Open rate is the fraction of recipients who open or view a notification.

termDefinitions.meaning: 收到通知后点击链接或按钮的人数比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Click rate is the fraction of recipients who click a notification link or action.

optionExplanations: 队列、延迟、错误、重复和用户互动这几项合在一起，才能同时回答“发得快不快”“坏在哪”“有没有扰民”和“有没有真正被打开”这几个运营真正关心的问题。
网页 PageRank 是搜索引擎排序用的信号，跟通知系统的运营健康完全不相关。
只用一个聊天在线绿点数当唯一指标，看不到延迟、失败和重复这些通知系统自己的核心问题。
DNS cache 命中率反映的是域名解析效率，不能代表所有通道的整体运营状况。
optionExplanations_en: Queue depth, latency, errors, duplicates, and engagement together answer what operations actually cares about: is it sending fast, where's it failing, is it annoying users, and is anyone actually opening it.
Web PageRank is a search-ranking signal, entirely unrelated to a notification system's operational health.
Using just one chat-presence indicator as the sole metric shows nothing about the notification system's own core issues like latency, failure, and duplicates.
DNS cache hit rate reflects domain resolution efficiency — it can't stand in for the overall operational state across every channel.

scenario: 发送前每条通知都要查用户是否对该 channel opt-in；高峰时设置表压力很大。
scenario_en: Before each send, the system checks whether the user opted into that channel; the settings table is under heavy peak load.
q: settings 读取怎么优化？
q_en: How should settings reads be optimized?
options: 缓存用户通知设置，并用短 TTL 或变更失效
完全跳过退订检查
把用户设置硬编码写死在每一个 worker 里
每次都全表扫描
options_en: Cache notification settings with short TTL or change invalidation.
Skip opt-out checks entirely.
Hard-code user settings inside the worker
Scan the full table every time.
why: 设置读多写少，缓存能保护数据库；但退订要尽快生效，所以 TTL 不能太长。
why_en: Settings are read-heavy, so cache them, but keep TTL or invalidation tight for opt-out correctness.
tradeoff: 数据库压力 vs 退订生效速度
whenOtherWins: 如果法规要求退订立即生效，发送前读主库或强失效更稳。

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据变化后让旧缓存失效的动作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Invalidation marks stale cached data unusable after the source changes.

optionExplanations: 把用户的通知设置缓存起来，用较短的 TTL 或者在设置变更时主动失效，既能挡住高峰期对设置表的读压力，又不会让退订生效拖太久。
完全跳过退订检查会让已经明确退订的用户继续收到通知，直接违背了用户的选择。
把设置硬编码在 worker 里，用户改了设置后 worker 却毫不知情，会一直按旧设置错误地发送。
每次都全表扫描在高峰期会给数据库带来巨大压力，正是缓存想要避免的情况。
optionExplanations_en: Caching user notification settings with a short TTL or invalidating on change protects the settings table from peak-time read pressure while still keeping opt-out from taking too long to kick in.
Skipping the opt-out check entirely means users who explicitly opted out keep getting notifications, directly violating their choice.
Hardcoding settings into the worker leaves it completely unaware when a user changes their setting, continuing to send under the stale old setting indefinitely.
A full table scan on every send puts massive pressure on the database exactly at peak time — precisely what caching is meant to avoid.

scenario: 一个营销模板上线后发现链接错误；同时队列里还有旧模板生成的待发送任务。
scenario_en: A campaign template ships with a bad link, while queued jobs generated from the old template still exist.
q: 模板系统要支持什么？
q_en: What should the template system support?
options: 模板版本和回滚，任务记录使用的版本
只保存一个可以被随时覆盖掉的模板
让 worker 随机选模板
不记录变量
options_en: Template versions and rollback, with jobs recording the version used.
Keep only one overwritable template
Let workers pick templates randomly.
Do not record variables.
why: 版本能解释某条通知按哪个内容发出，也能停止坏版本继续扩散。代价是模板管理更像发布流程。
why_en: Versioning makes template sends auditable and lets you roll back bad content.
whenOtherWins: 小型内部提醒可以先用简单模板，但生产营销系统需要版本和审核。

termDefinitions.meaning: 发现新版本有问题后切回旧版本的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Rollback means reverting to a previous version after a bad release.

optionExplanations: 给模板加版本号并支持回滚，同时让每条任务记录自己用的是哪个版本，出问题时既能解释某条通知为什么长这样，也能立刻停掉坏版本继续扩散。
只保存一个可覆盖的模板，一旦发现内容错误再去改，队列里还没处理完的旧任务全都会带着这个错误版本继续发出去。
让 worker 随机选模板完全没有意义，通知内容会变得不可预测，也没法保证发的是正确版本。
不记录变量会让每条通知具体填了什么内容都无从查起，出问题时根本没法复盘。
optionExplanations_en: Versioning templates with rollback support, and having each task record which version it used, lets a bad version be explained after the fact and stopped from spreading further right away.
Keeping only one overwritable template means fixing a content error doesn't stop tasks already queued under the old version from still going out with the mistake.
Having the worker pick a template at random makes no sense — notification content becomes unpredictable with no guarantee the correct version was used.
Not recording variables leaves no way to trace back what content a given notification actually contained, making post-incident review impossible.

scenario: 安全验证码、支付提醒和促销广告共用系统；高峰时不能让广告压住验证码。
scenario_en: Security codes, payment alerts, and promotional ads share the system; ads must not delay codes during peaks.
q: 队列还需要什么维度？
q_en: What extra queue dimension is needed?
options: 按优先级或业务类型隔离队列/配额
所有消息完全同优先级
只按模板名字排序
只按用户 ID 的奇偶来拆分队列
options_en: Separate queues or quotas by priority or business type.
Treat every message as exactly the same priority.
Sort only by template name.
Split only by odd/even user ID
why: 不同通知价值不同，高优先级通道要有保留吞吐。代价是调度要防止低优先级永久饥饿。
why_en: Different notification classes need reserved capacity so low-value campaigns cannot block critical sends.
tradeoff: 关键通知延迟 vs 低优先级公平
whenOtherWins: 如果系统只发送一种同等重要的通知，单优先级队列更简单。

termDefinitions.meaning: 给某类流量保留或限制的资源份额。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quota is a reserved or capped share of capacity for a traffic class.

optionExplanations: 按业务重要性给队列或配额分出优先级，能保证高峰期验证码和支付提醒不会被大量促销广告挤占资源，先保住最关键的那部分吞吐。
让所有消息完全同优先级，广告量一大就会跟验证码抢同样的处理资源，关键通知的延迟会跟着广告一起变差。
只按模板名字排序跟消息本身的业务重要性毫无关系，起不到保护关键通知的作用。
只按用户 ID 奇偶拆分只是把负载分成两半，不区分消息类型，验证码照样可能和广告混在同一半里被拖慢。
optionExplanations_en: Splitting queues or quotas by priority or business type guarantees OTPs and payment reminders aren't squeezed out by a flood of promo ads at peak, protecting the throughput that matters most.
Treating every message at the same priority means a surge of ads competes for the same processing capacity as OTPs, dragging critical-notification latency down along with the ads.
Sorting only by template name has nothing to do with a message's actual business importance and does nothing to protect critical notifications.
Splitting only by odd/even user ID just halves the load without distinguishing message type — an OTP could still land in the same half as ads and get delayed.

scenario: worker 请求供应商超时，不知道供应商是否已经发送；重试可能造成用户收到两条。
scenario_en: A worker times out calling a provider and does not know whether the provider already sent; retry may duplicate the notification.
q: 如何让 provider 调用更安全？
q_en: How can provider calls be safer?
options: 复用 event_id 作幂等 key
每次重试都重新生成一个新的业务 ID
关闭所有重试
只改通知文案
options_en: Reuse event_id as an idempotency key.
Generate a brand-new business ID on every retry
Disable all retries.
Only change the notification copy.
why: 如果供应商支持幂等 key，同一事件重试会被识别成同一次发送。否则只能靠本地去重和业务容忍重复。
why_en: If the provider supports idempotency keys, retries for the same event can map to one provider-side send.
whenOtherWins: 如果供应商不支持幂等 key，要在本地记录尝试状态并降低重复影响。

termDefinitions.meaning: 发送请求携带的唯一 key，用于让下游识别重复请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotency key lets a downstream service recognize duplicate requests.

optionExplanations: 复用同一个事件自带的 ID 作为幂等 key 传给供应商，供应商如果支持，就能把这次超时后的重试识别成同一次发送，而不是新发一条。
每次重试都生成一个新的业务 ID，供应商会把每次重试都当成一次全新的请求处理，用户完全可能收到多条重复消息。
关闭所有重试意味着一次超时就直接放弃了这次发送，跟“防止重复”这个诉求无关，还引入了新的丢失风险。
只改通知文案是内容层面的调整，跟超时重试可能造成的重复发送这个根因完全不搭边。
optionExplanations_en: Reusing the same event's ID as the idempotency key sent to the provider lets it, if supported, recognize this timeout-triggered retry as the same send rather than a new one.
Generating a fresh business ID on every retry makes the provider treat each retry as an entirely new request, so the user can easily end up receiving multiple duplicate messages.
Turning off all retries means one timeout just gives up on the send entirely — unrelated to preventing duplicates, and it introduces a new risk of losing the notification altogether.
Changing only the notification copy is a content-layer tweak, completely unrelated to the root cause of timeout retries potentially causing duplicate sends.

scenario: 调用方传入非法手机号、空邮箱或过大的 push payload；如果直接入队会浪费 worker。
scenario_en: Callers pass an invalid phone number, empty email, or oversized push payload; enqueuing it wastes workers.
q: 入口校验要挡什么？
q_en: What should entry validation block?
options: 挡格式、缺字段、超限和越权
所有合法请求
provider 的内部网络抖动
用户是否点击
options_en: Block bad format, missing fields, oversize, unauthorized sends.
All valid requests.
Provider-side network jitter.
Whether the user clicks.
why: 入口要挡掉请求本身就不可能发送的脏数据。provider 抖动和点击率是发送后问题，不能靠入队前校验解决。
why_en: Validate before enqueueing so workers handle only sendable notifications.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通知发送给平台或用户设备的内容体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A payload is the content body sent to a platform or user device.

termDefinitions.meaning: 实际代发短信、邮件或 push 的外部服务商。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A provider is the external service that actually sends SMS, email, or push messages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从队列取任务并执行发送逻辑的后台进程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A worker is a background process that pulls jobs from a queue and performs the send.

optionExplanations: 格式、必填字段、大小上限和授权在入口就能判断，挡住它们能避免脏任务占用队列和 worker。
合法请求应该进入队列；把它们挡掉就是制造误拒。
provider 网络抖动发生在实际发送阶段，入口校验还没调用它，挡不住。
点击是发送后的用户行为，入口只能校验请求能不能被发送。
optionExplanations_en: Format, required fields, size limits, and authorization can be checked at entry, before dirty jobs occupy workers.
Valid requests should enter the queue; blocking them is a false rejection.
Provider jitter happens during the actual send, before entry validation has even called it.
Clicks are user behavior after delivery; entry validation only checks whether a request is sendable.

scenario: 一次订单提醒优先 push；如果用户没有有效 device token，但有验证过的手机号。
scenario_en: An order alert prefers push; the user has no valid device token but has a verified phone number.
q: 多通道 fallback 怎么做？
q_en: How should multi-channel fallback work?
options: 按业务策略从 push 退到 SMS，并记录原因
同时无脑发所有通道
直接丢弃订单提醒
直接把用户的手机号当成 device token 来用
options_en: Fallback from push to SMS by business policy and record the reason.
Blindly send every channel at once.
Drop the order alert.
Use the phone number as a device token
why: fallback 要按通知重要性和用户设置决定，不能随便轰炸所有通道。记录原因方便之后分析 token 质量。
why_en: Fallback should follow business importance and user settings, not spam every channel blindly.
whenOtherWins: 营销消息通常不应跨通道 fallback，避免打扰用户。

termDefinitions.meaning: 主方案不可用时切到备用方案的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fallback means switching to a backup path when the primary path is unavailable.

tradeoff: 触达可靠性 vs 用户打扰和退订风险
optionExplanations: 按这条通知的重要程度和用户实际情况，从 push 退到已验证过的手机号发 SMS，并记下退回的原因，这样的 fallback 才是有依据、可追溯的。
不管三七二十一同时轰炸所有通道，会让用户在多个渠道同时收到同一条提醒，体验很差，也浪费额外的发送成本。
订单提醒这类重要通知直接丢弃，用户可能完全错过应该收到的重要信息，代价太大。
把手机号直接当 device token 用，两者的格式和用途完全不同，推送网关根本没法用手机号定位设备。
optionExplanations_en: Falling back from push to a verified phone number's SMS, based on how important this notification is and what the user's actual situation looks like, with the reason logged, makes for a fallback that's principled and traceable.
Blindly blasting every channel at once means the user gets the same reminder duplicated across multiple channels — a bad experience and wasted send cost.
Just dropping an important notification like an order reminder risks the user completely missing something they should have received — too costly.
Treating a phone number as if it were a device token confuses two entirely different formats and purposes — a push gateway has no way to locate a device by phone number.

scenario: 产品经理问一条通知现在处于 created、queued、sent、delivered、failed 中哪一步。
scenario_en: A product manager asks whether a notification is created, queued, sent, delivered, or failed.
q: 为什么要建状态机？
q_en: Why build a status state machine?
options: 用显式发送状态机
让所有状态都写在日志文本里手查
为了替代 provider
为了跳过去重
options_en: Use an explicit delivery state machine.
So every state is manually searched in log text.
To replace providers.
To skip dedupe.
why: 状态机让系统知道下一步能不能重试、是否终态、该显示什么。没有状态会让排障全靠猜。
why_en: A state machine makes retry, terminal outcomes, and user-visible status explicit.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是 fire-and-forget 低价值通知，可以只保留最少审计日志。
diagram:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Created
  Created --> Queued
  Queued --> Sent
  Sent --> Delivered
  Sent --> Failed
  Failed --> Queued: retry

termDefinitions.meaning: 用有限状态和状态迁移描述对象生命周期的模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A state machine models an object lifecycle with states and transitions.

optionExplanations: 有一个明确的发送状态机，系统才知道这条通知现在到了哪一步、下一步能不能重试、是不是已经到了终态，产品经理问起来也能立刻查到答案。
让所有状态都散落在日志文本里靠人工去翻，出问题时排查效率极低，也没法直接支撑“现在处于哪一步”这种实时查询。
状态机管的是发送过程本身的状态流转，不负责真正的跨运营商投递，替代不了 provider。
状态机和事件去重是两个不同的机制，状态机不是为了跳过去重而存在的。
optionExplanations_en: Having an explicit send-state machine lets the system know exactly which step a notification is on, whether it can still retry, whether it's reached a terminal state — and lets a PM's question get answered instantly.
Scattering every state across raw log text for someone to manually dig through makes troubleshooting painfully slow and can't directly answer a real-time "what step is it on" question.
A state machine governs the send process's own state transitions — it isn't responsible for actual cross-carrier delivery and can't substitute for the provider.
A state machine and event deduplication are two different mechanisms — the state machine doesn't exist to skip deduplication.

scenario: 用户既能发帖，也能打开首页看好友动态；系统把这两个动作拆成两条主路径。
scenario_en: Users can publish posts and open the home page to read friends' updates; the system splits these into two main flows.
q: 新闻流设计的两条主路径是什么？
q_en: What are the two main flows in a news feed design?
options: 发布写入与 feed 构建/读取
DNS 解析与网页下载
短信发送与 email 发送
支付扣款与退款
options_en: Post publishing and feed building or retrieval.
DNS resolution and page downloading.
SMS sending and email sending.
Payment capture and refund.
why: 发布路径关心写入帖子和分发 post_id；读取路径关心从缓存取 ID 再补齐内容。分开讲能把写扩展和读延迟说清楚。
why_en: Separate publishing from retrieval so write fanout and read hydration can be reasoned about independently.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户首页看到的动态列表，通常由关注对象或好友内容组成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feed is the home-page list of updates from friends or followed entities.

optionExplanations: 对，发帖走的是写入内容和分发 post_id 这条路，刷首页走的是从缓存取 ID 再补齐正文这条路，两条路的瓶颈完全不同，分开讲才能分别说清楚写扩展和读延迟。
DNS 解析和网页下载是爬虫系统的组成部分，跟社交产品的发帖和刷 feed 完全不是一回事。
短信和邮件发送是通知系统的通道，不是新闻流服务本身要处理的两条主路径。
支付扣款和退款属于交易系统的核心流程，跟发帖、刷 feed 这两个动作毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: Right — posting follows the path of writing content and fanning out post_id, while opening the homepage follows the path of pulling IDs from cache and hydrating them, and since the two paths have completely different bottlenecks, splitting them apart is what lets write scaling and read latency each get explained clearly.
DNS resolution and page downloading are parts of a crawler system, entirely unrelated to a social product's posting and feed-reading paths.
SMS and email sending are channels of a notification system, not the two main paths a news feed service itself needs to handle.
Payment charges and refunds belong to a transaction system's core flow, unrelated to posting and reading a feed.

scenario: 10M DAU 的社交产品，大多数用户好友数正常；首页刷新必须快，但少数名人有海量粉丝。
scenario_en: A social app has 10M DAU; most users have normal friend counts, home feed refresh must be fast, but a few celebrities have huge follower counts.
q: fanout 策略怎么选？
q_en: Which fanout strategy fits best?
options: 普通用户写时推，名人读时拉
所有用户都读时全量聚合
所有用户都写时推给全部粉丝
只在客户端拼接好友帖子
options_en: Push normal users, pull celebrities on read.
Aggregate everything on every read for all users.
Push every post to every follower for all users.
Assemble friends' posts only on the client.
why: 大多数用户预计算能让读很快；名人写时推送会制造巨大热 key。混合方案把读延迟和写放大分开处理。
why_en: Use push fanout for normal users to keep reads fast, but pull celebrity posts to avoid huge write amplification.
tradeoff: 读路径延迟 vs 写路径放大
whenOtherWins: 如果用户关系很小且没有名人，纯 fanout on write 更简单。

termDefinitions.meaning: 发帖时把 post_id 预先写入接收者 feed。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fanout on write prewrites a post ID into recipients' feeds when the post is created.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读首页时临时拉取关注对象的近期帖子并合并。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fanout on read pulls and merges recent posts when the feed is requested.

optionExplanations: 普通用户的好友数正常，写时推算好一份能让首页读取很快；名人粉丝数巨大，写时推会瞬间制造海量写操作，改成读时拉能把这份成本挪到真正打开 feed 的粉丝身上。
让所有用户都读时全量聚合，普通用户的首页刷新每次都要现算，跟“刷新必须快”这个要求直接冲突。
让所有用户都写时推给全部粉丝，名人一发帖就要瞬间写几千万份 feed，会制造巨大的写放大和热点压力。
只在客户端拼接好友帖子意味着客户端要自己去查每个好友的最新内容，既慢又没法利用服务端已经算好的结果。
optionExplanations_en: Ordinary users have a normal friend count, so precomputing on write keeps the homepage fast to read; a celebrity's follower count is enormous, and fanning out on write would instantly create a massive write spike, so pulling on read instead shifts that cost onto whichever fans actually open their feed.
Having every user aggregate everything on read means an ordinary user's homepage has to be computed fresh every time, directly conflicting with the requirement that it be fast.
Having every user fan out to all followers on write means one celebrity post instantly triggers tens of millions of feed writes, creating massive write amplification and a hot spot.
Assembling friends' posts purely on the client means the client has to look up each friend's latest content itself — slow, and it can't take advantage of anything the server already precomputed.

scenario: 一个名人发帖会触达几千万粉丝；如果写时推，fanout worker 都围着同一个作者事件跑。
scenario_en: A celebrity post reaches tens of millions of followers; with write fanout, workers all process the same author event.
q: 这个风险叫什么，怎么缓解？
q_en: What is this risk and a mitigation?
options: hotkey；名人帖子改成读时拉或分散处理
判断成 cache miss，于是把所有缓存都删掉
DNS stall；缓存域名
split brain；关闭副本
options_en: Hotkey; pull celebrity posts on read or distribute processing.
Cache miss; delete all caches
DNS stall; cache domains.
Split brain; turn off replicas.
why: 名人事件会把同一份写放大到巨量接收者，形成热点。读时拉能把成本摊到真正打开 feed 的用户身上。
why_en: A celebrity post creates a hotkey because one write fans out massively; pull it on read to spend work only for active readers.
whenOtherWins: 如果粉丝数上限很低，写时推不会形成明显热点。

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个 key 或事件承载远高于平均的读写压力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hotkey is a key or event receiving far more traffic than average.

optionExplanations: 粉丝数太大导致同一个作者事件被放大成海量 fanout 工作，这就是 hotkey，把名人帖子改成读时拉、或者把处理拆散，能把这份被放大的成本摊开而不是集中在一处。
cache miss 是缓存没命中要回源查询的问题，跟名人事件被过度放大导致的写压力是完全不同的现象。
DNS stall 是域名解析卡住的问题，跟这里名人发帖引发的 fanout 热点毫不相关。
split brain 是分布式系统里多个节点各自认为自己是主节点的一致性问题，跟名人写放大不是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: A follower count this large amplifies one author's event into a massive amount of fanout work — that's a hot key, and switching a celebrity's post to pull-on-read or spreading the processing out is what breaks up that concentrated cost instead of letting it pile up in one place.
A cache miss is when a lookup misses and has to fall back to the source — an entirely different phenomenon from write pressure caused by an over-amplified celebrity event.
DNS stall is domain resolution getting stuck — completely unrelated to the fanout hot spot triggered by a celebrity's post here.
Split brain is a distributed-systems consistency problem where multiple nodes each believe they're the primary — not the same thing as celebrity write amplification.

scenario: 每个用户 feed cache 只需要支持最近几百到几千条；完整帖子、作者头像和媒体对象很大。
scenario_en: Each user's feed cache only needs recent hundreds or thousands of entries; full posts, avatars, and media objects are large.
q: feed cache 里存什么？
q_en: What should the feed cache store?
options: 只存 post_id，读取时 hydrate
存放完整用户对象和全部媒体的原始字节内容
只存作者名字字符串
不存任何东西，每次扫库
options_en: Store post IDs and hydrate on read.
Store full user objects and all media raw byte content
Store only author-name strings.
Store nothing and scan the database every time.
why: ID 列表小，适合高命中缓存；读取时再从 user/post cache 补齐展示字段。代价是读路径多几次缓存查询。
why_en: Caching IDs keeps per-user feed entries small, then read-time hydration fills in post and user details.
tradeoff: 缓存体积 vs 读取补齐成本
whenOtherWins: 如果 feed 项极少且字段固定，缓存完整对象能减少一次 hydrate。
diagram:
flowchart LR
  FeedIDs[Feed cache post IDs] --> Service[Newsfeed service]
  Service --> Post[Post cache]
  Service --> User[User cache]
  Service --> JSON[Hydrated JSON]

termDefinitions.meaning: 根据 ID 取回完整对象字段，组装成可返回给客户端的数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hydration fetches full object fields by ID to build the client response.

optionExplanations: 一条 feed 只存几百个 8 字节 ID，同样内存能装下几十倍用户的近期列表。
存完整用户对象和全部媒体字节，会让 feed cache 体积暴涨，本该轻量的近期加速层会被撑得很大很慢。
只存作者名字字符串，连要展示的正文、点赞数这些内容都拿不到，根本不够支撑一条 feed 的展示需求。
不存任何东西、每次扫库，会让每次刷新首页都变成一次完整的数据库查询，完全违背用缓存加速读取的初衷。
optionExplanations_en: A feed is just a few hundred eight-byte IDs, so the same memory holds recent lists for many times more users.
Storing full user objects and every media byte would balloon feed cache size, turning what should be a lightweight recent-acceleration layer into something huge and slow.
Storing only the author's name string leaves out the actual post body and like count needed for display — nowhere near enough to render a single feed item.
Storing nothing and scanning the database on every request turns every homepage refresh into a full database query, defeating the entire point of caching for fast reads.

scenario: 发帖后 fanout 服务要快速找到作者的好友，并考虑好友关系和推荐等图查询。
scenario_en: After a post, the fanout service must quickly find the author's friends and support relationship-style graph queries.
q: 好友关系更适合哪类存储？
q_en: Which storage type fits friend relationships?
options: graph DB 或社交图服务
对象存储，按 key 存 blob
CDN 边缘缓存
只写入渲染模板库
options_en: Use a graph DB or social graph service.
Object storage keyed by blob.
A CDN edge cache.
Only a rendering template store.
why: 好友关系天然是点和边，图服务能围绕邻居查询优化。代价是它通常不负责帖子正文存储。
why_en: Friend relationships are nodes and edges, so a graph service is a natural fit for neighbor lookups.
whenOtherWins: 如果关系很简单且规模小，关系型表加索引也可以先扛住。

termDefinitions.meaning: 用节点和边建模关系的数据库，适合好友、关注和推荐查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A graph database models relationships as nodes and edges, useful for friends, follows, and recommendations.

tradeoff: 关系遍历能力 vs 通用存储和运维成本
optionExplanations: 好友关系本质是点和边构成的图，图数据库或社交图服务能围绕“找某个人的邻居”这类查询做专门优化，正好匹配 fanout 要快速找好友的需求。
对象存储擅长存整块二进制文件，不是为了表达和查询人与人之间关系而设计的结构。
CDN 负责就近分发静态内容，跟查询用户之间的好友关系完全不是一回事。
模板库存的是通知或消息的文案格式，跟好友关系数据毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: Friend relationships are fundamentally a graph of nodes and edges, and a graph database or social-graph service is specifically optimized for "find this person's neighbors" queries, exactly matching what fanout needs to quickly locate friends.
Object storage is good at holding whole binary blobs — it isn't a structure built for expressing or querying relationships between people.
A CDN handles nearby distribution of static content, an entirely different concern from querying friend relationships between users.
A template library stores the wording format for notifications or messages, unrelated to friend-relationship data.

scenario: 作者发帖后，有些好友静音了作者；帖子也可能只对部分好友可见。
scenario_en: After a user posts, some friends may have muted the author, and the post may be visible only to selected friends.
q: fanout 前要先做什么？
q_en: What should happen before fanout?
options: 读取用户设置和可见性规则，过滤接收者
把 post_id 推给所有好友再说
只按好友数量排序
删除 user cache
options_en: Read settings and visibility rules, then filter recipients.
Push the post_id to every friend first.
Sort only by friend count.
Delete the user cache.
why: 分发前过滤能避免把不该看的内容写入对方 feed cache。代价是 fanout 依赖设置缓存的新鲜度。
why_en: Filter recipients before writing feed entries so muted or unauthorized users do not receive the post ID.
whenOtherWins: 如果可见性规则很复杂，也可以先写候选集，读取时再做强校验，但读路径会变重。

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定哪些用户能看到某条内容的权限规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A visibility rule decides which users are allowed to see a piece of content.

optionExplanations: 先读一遍用户的静音设置和帖子的可见性规则，把不该收到的接收者过滤掉，才能避免把不该看的内容写进对方的 feed cache。
把 post_id 不加区分地推给所有好友，会让静音了作者或者本不该看到这条帖子的人也收到，违背了可见性规则。
只按好友数量排序解决的是处理顺序问题，完全不涉及“这条帖子该不该发给这个人”这个可见性判断。
删除 user cache 跟这次发帖该分发给谁毫无关系，也不会实现可见性过滤的效果。
optionExplanations_en: Reading the mute settings and post visibility rules first and filtering out recipients who shouldn't get it is what keeps content the recipient shouldn't see from ever landing in their feed cache.
Fanning out post_id to every friend indiscriminately means someone who muted the author, or who shouldn't see this post at all, still gets it — violating the visibility rule.
Sorting only by friend count decides processing order and has nothing to do with the actual visibility question of whether this post should go to this person.
Deleting the user cache has nothing to do with deciding who this post should be distributed to, and doesn't achieve any visibility filtering at all.

scenario: feed 中有图片和视频；用户遍布全球，媒体对象远大于帖子文本。
scenario_en: The feed contains images and videos; users are global, and media objects are much larger than post text.
q: 媒体文件怎么分发？
q_en: How should media files be served?
options: 存对象存储，URL 走 CDN 边缘
直接放进 feed cache
每次从关系图数据库读
编码到 auth token 里
options_en: Store in object storage and serve through CDN edges.
Put media bytes directly in feed cache.
Read from the graph database each time.
Encode them inside the auth token.
why: 媒体大且读多，CDN 把字节放到离用户近的边缘。feed 服务只返回引用，不承担大文件传输。
why_en: Large read-heavy media should be served from object storage through a CDN, while the feed returns references.
whenOtherWins: 如果只支持纯文本 feed，CDN 不是主路径。

termDefinitions.meaning: Content Delivery Network，把静态内容缓存在靠近用户的边缘节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches static content at edge locations close to users.

tradeoff: 媒体就近分发 vs feed API 轻量化
optionExplanations: 媒体文件又大又是读多场景，存进对象存储、用 CDN 把字节放到离用户更近的边缘，feed 服务只需要返回一个引用地址，不用自己扛大文件传输。
直接放进 feed cache 会让这个本该轻量的近期加速层被大文件撑爆，完全不适合它的设计定位。
每次从关系图数据库读媒体内容，图数据库本来就不是为存储和传输大文件设计的，会很慢也很浪费。
把媒体编码进 auth token 里，token 是用来做身份鉴权的小体积凭证，塞进大文件内容既不合理也不安全。
optionExplanations_en: Media is large and read-heavy, so storing it in object storage and letting a CDN place the bytes near users lets the feed service just return a reference URL without ever carrying the large-file transfer itself.
Putting it straight into feed cache would let a large file blow up what's supposed to be a lightweight recent-acceleration layer — completely mismatched with its purpose.
Reading media content from a graph database every time is slow and wasteful, since a graph database was never designed to store or transfer large files in the first place.
Encoding media into the auth token, which is a small credential meant for identity verification, is neither sensible nor safe as a place to stuff large file content.

scenario: 新闻流读取要组装 feed ID、帖子、作者关系、点赞状态和计数。
scenario_en: News feed reads assemble feed IDs, posts, relationships, action state, and counters.
q: 哪些缓存层常见且有不同职责？
q_en: Which cache layers commonly have distinct responsibilities?
options: News Feed：保存用户 feed 的 post_id
Content：保存帖子正文和热门内容
Action/Counters：保存点赞回复状态和计数
Robots：保存网站抓取规则
options_en: News Feed stores post IDs for a user's feed.
Content stores post bodies and hot content.
Action/Counters store like/reply state and counts.
Robots stores website crawl rules.
why: feed 是多对象组合，分层缓存能让每类数据按自己的访问模式扩展。robots.txt 属于爬虫，不属于新闻流读取。
why_en: A feed is assembled from several object types, so cache layers should match their different access patterns.

termDefinitions.meaning: 计数器，保存点赞数、回复数、关注数等聚合值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A counter stores aggregate counts such as likes, replies, or followers.

optionExplanations: 对，News Feed 缓存层保存的是用户自己那份 feed 的 post_id 列表，是组装首页的骨架。
对，Content 缓存层保存帖子正文和热门内容，是骨架之外要补齐的实际展示内容。
对，Action/Counters 缓存层专门保存点赞、回复这类高频变化的状态和计数，跟正文分开管理。
robots.txt 保存的是网站给爬虫的抓取规则，跟组装一条新闻流需要的这几层缓存完全不在一个系统里。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the News Feed cache layer holds the list of post_id values for a user's own feed, the skeleton used to assemble the homepage.
Right — the Content cache layer holds post bodies and popular content, the actual displayable material that fills in that skeleton.
Right — the Action/Counters cache layer specifically holds high-frequency state like likes and replies, kept separate from the post body.
robots.txt holds the crawl rules a site declares to crawlers — it belongs to an entirely different system from the cache layers needed to assemble a news feed.

scenario: 发帖 API 暴露给登录用户；攻击者可能用脚本高频发垃圾内容。
scenario_en: The post API is exposed to logged-in users; an attacker may script high-rate spam posts.
q: web server 层要先挡什么？
q_en: What should the web-server layer guard first?
options: 认证 auth_token，并对发帖限流
直接信任 content 参数
只加 CDN
让 fanout worker 决定是否登录
options_en: Authenticate auth_token and rate-limit posting.
Trust the content parameter directly.
Only add a CDN.
Let fanout workers decide whether the user is logged in.
why: 入口层先确认是谁，再限制单位时间发帖量。这样垃圾内容不会进入后面的存储和 fanout 管线。
why_en: Authenticate and rate-limit at the entry point so spam does not enter storage and fanout.
whenOtherWins: 内部管理脚本可以走单独高权限入口，但仍应审计和限额。

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端证明登录身份的令牌。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An auth_token is a token the client uses to prove its logged-in identity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 限制某主体在时间窗口内的请求数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rate limit caps requests from an actor within a time window.

optionExplanations: 先确认发帖请求真的来自这个登录用户、再限制单位时间内能发多少条，能在垃圾内容真正进入后端存储和 fanout 管线之前就把它挡住。
直接信任 content 参数，意味着任何人传什么内容服务端都照单全收，完全没有对输入做任何把关。
只加 CDN 优化的是静态内容分发速度，挡不住一个已经通过认证却在高频灌垃圾内容的攻击脚本。
让 fanout worker 才去判断是否登录，这时候垃圾帖子早就已经写进了存储，为时已晚，应该在入口就拦下来。
optionExplanations_en: Confirming the post request genuinely comes from this logged-in user, then capping how many posts they can make per unit time, blocks junk content before it ever reaches downstream storage and the fanout pipeline.
Trusting the content parameter directly means the server accepts whatever anyone sends without any check on the input at all.
Adding only a CDN speeds up static content delivery — it does nothing to stop an authenticated script that's flooding the system with junk content at high frequency.
Letting the fanout worker decide whether the caller was logged in happens far too late — the junk post has already been written to storage by then; it should be caught right at the entry point.

scenario: 发帖请求不能一直等到 5000 个好友的 feed cache 都写完；高峰时 fanout 量会抖动。
scenario_en: The publish request should not wait until feed cache writes for 5,000 friends finish; fanout volume spikes at peak times.
q: post service 和 fanout worker 之间放什么？
q_en: What belongs between the post service and fanout workers?
options: 消息队列，异步分发 post_id
用一个同步 for 循环写完所有好友的 feed
客户端轮询好友列表
DNS resolver
options_en: A message queue for asynchronous post_id fanout.
A synchronous loop writing every friend’s feed
Client polling of the friend list.
A DNS resolver.
why: 队列把发帖延迟和 fanout 工作量解耦，峰值时能缓冲。代价是好友看到新帖可能有轻微延迟。
why_en: A queue decouples publish latency from fanout work and buffers spikes, at the cost of small feed delay.
tradeoff: 发布延迟 vs 分发实时性
whenOtherWins: 如果好友数极少且必须强同步可见，同步写入可以简化一致性。

termDefinitions.meaning: 生产者写入、消费者异步读取的缓冲组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A message queue buffers jobs from producers for asynchronous consumers.

optionExplanations: 用消息队列异步分发 post_id，能让发帖请求不用等 5000 个好友的 feed cache 全部写完才返回，高峰期的抖动也能被队列先缓冲住。
同步 for 循环写所有好友，会让发帖请求一直卡在那里等这几千次写操作全部完成，响应时间会随好友数线性变长。
客户端轮询好友列表把本该由服务端异步完成的分发工作丢给客户端，既低效也不是分发的正确位置。
DNS resolver 负责域名解析，跟发帖服务和 fanout worker 之间该放什么组件完全不是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: Using a message queue to distribute post_id asynchronously lets the post request return without waiting for all 5,000 friends' feed caches to finish writing, and the queue absorbs the burst at peak times too.
A synchronous for-loop writing every friend keeps the post request blocked until all those thousands of writes finish, with response time growing linearly with friend count.
Client-side polling of the friend list dumps what should be server-side asynchronous distribution work onto the client — inefficient and the wrong place for it entirely.
A DNS resolver handles domain resolution, entirely unrelated to what component should sit between the post service and the fanout worker.

scenario: 客户端打开首页，只需要取自己的 feed；排序简化为按时间倒序。
scenario_en: The client opens the home page and only needs its own feed; ordering is simplified to reverse chronological order.
q: feed 读取 API 的核心是什么？
q_en: What is the core feed retrieval API?
options: GET /v1/me/feed，服务端用登录身份取 feed
POST /v1/all/users/delete 批量删所有人
GET /robots.txt
PATCH /provider/sms
options_en: GET /v1/me/feed, with the server using the logged-in identity.
POST /v1/all/users/delete
GET /robots.txt.
PATCH /provider/sms.
why: GET /v1/me/feed 把身份绑定到登录态，而不是让客户端传任意 user_id。这样读路径默认只返回当前用户自己的 feed。
why_en: Use /me/feed with the authenticated identity so clients cannot choose arbitrary user IDs.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 里用于读取资源的请求方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP GET is the request method used to read a resource.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务暴露给客户端或其他服务调用的接口契约。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API is the interface contract a service exposes to clients or other services.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端随请求携带的登录凭证，服务端用它识别当前用户。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An auth token is a login credential sent with a request so the server can identify the current user.

optionExplanations: 这是面向当前登录用户的读接口；服务端从 auth token 取身份，不接受客户端随便传 user_id。
这是删除用户的写接口，权限和副作用都与读取自己的首页相反。
robots.txt 给爬虫看抓取规则，不返回用户 feed。
修改短信 provider 配置和首页读取不在同一业务路径。
optionExplanations_en: This reads the current user's feed; the server gets identity from the auth token, not a client-supplied user_id.
This is a destructive user-delete write path, the opposite of reading your own homepage.
robots.txt is for crawler rules; it does not return a user's feed.
Changing SMS provider config is a different business path from reading the home feed.

scenario: 面试官为了简化需求，明确说 feed 只按发布时间倒序，不做机器学习排序。
scenario_en: The interviewer simplifies the requirement: the feed is only reverse chronological, with no ML ranking.
q: 这会简化哪块设计？
q_en: Which part of the design becomes simpler?
options: 按时间维护 post_id 列表
必须引入一整套复杂的特征平台才行
所有帖子都要重新训练模型
不能使用缓存
options_en: Maintain post IDs in time order.
A complex feature platform is mandatory
Every post must retrain a model.
Caching cannot be used.
why: 时间倒序让排序键很清楚，post_id 或时间戳就能维护列表。复杂 ranking 可以作为扩展，不该抢主线。
why_en: Reverse chronological order keeps the read model simple: maintain a time-ordered list of post IDs.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品要求相关性排序，读取路径要加入 ranking service 和特征缓存。

termDefinitions.meaning: 根据特征和策略给候选内容排序的服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ranking service orders candidate content using features and policy.

tradeoff: 时间倒序简单性 vs 相关性排序能力
optionExplanations: 排序键变得非常明确，只需要按 post_id 或时间戳维护一份有序列表就够了，不用再引入额外的排序逻辑。
面试官明确说不做机器学习排序，这时候还要求引入复杂特征平台，跟这个简化前提正好相反。
按时间倒序跟要不要给已有帖子重新训练模型完全没有关系，重新训练模型是机器学习排序才需要考虑的事。
不能使用缓存和这里的简化毫无关系，时间倒序恰恰是最容易被缓存和快速维护的排序方式，不存在不能用缓存的说法。
optionExplanations_en: The sort key becomes completely unambiguous — maintaining an ordered list by post_id or timestamp is all that's needed, with no extra ranking logic required.
The interviewer explicitly said no ML ranking, so requiring a complex feature platform anyway runs directly against that simplification.
Reverse-chronological order has nothing to do with whether existing posts need retraining a model — that's only a concern for ML ranking.
"Can't use caching" has nothing to do with this simplification — reverse-chronological order is actually the easiest ordering to cache and maintain quickly, so there's no basis for that claim.

scenario: 用户刷新首页；feed cache 里只有 post_id，展示还需要作者、正文和媒体链接。
scenario_en: A user refreshes the home feed; the feed cache contains only post IDs, while rendering needs author, post body, and media URLs.
q: 读取链路的合理顺序是什么？
q_en: What is a reasonable read path order?
steps: 返回 JSON 给客户端渲染
web server 调 newsfeed service
从 feed cache 取 post_id 列表
从 user/post cache 补齐对象
客户端带 auth_token 请求 /me/feed
why: 先鉴权进入 feed 服务，再取轻量 ID 列表，最后 hydrate 成展示对象。这样 cache 小，返回体完整。
why_en: Authenticate the request, fetch lightweight feed IDs, hydrate objects from caches, and return renderable JSON.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  C[Client] --> W[Web server]
  W --> F[Newsfeed service]
  F --> IDs[Feed cache]
  F --> Obj[User and post cache]
  Obj --> JSON[Response JSON]

scenario: 新闻流 Web 层只做鉴权、限流和路由；真实状态在缓存、数据库和队列里。
scenario_en: The news feed web tier only handles auth, rate limiting, and routing; state lives in caches, databases, and queues.
q: web tier 怎么扩展？
q_en: How should the web tier scale?
options: 保持无状态，负载均衡后水平扩容
把每个用户 feed 存本机磁盘
要求客户端固定连同一台机器
只做垂直扩容
options_en: Keep it stateless and scale horizontally behind a load balancer.
Store each user's feed on local disk.
Require clients to stick to one machine.
Only scale vertically.
why: 无状态 web server 可以随时加减实例，失败也容易重试。状态放本机会让扩容和故障恢复都变难。
why_en: A stateless web tier can be added or replaced behind a load balancer without moving user feed state.
tradeoff: 水平扩容简单 vs 本地状态访问快
whenOtherWins: 如果服务维护长连接或本地 session，才需要粘性会话或外部会话存储。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把客户端请求分发到多台后端实例的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A load balancer distributes client requests across backend instances.

optionExplanations: Web 层不保存真实状态，随时可以加减实例，负载均衡器把请求分发出去就行，扩容和故障恢复都很简单。
把每个用户的 feed 存本机磁盘，会让请求必须固定路由到那台特定机器才能拿到数据，完全违背了状态该放在共享存储的原则。
要求客户端固定连同一台机器，本质上是在制造人为的粘性依赖，一旦那台机器故障，这批用户就全部受影响。
只做垂直扩容意味着只能靠升级单台机器的配置来扛流量，撞到硬件上限后就再也扩不动了。
optionExplanations_en: The web tier holds no real state, so instances can be added or removed freely, with the load balancer just distributing requests — scaling and failover both stay simple.
Storing each user's feed on the local machine's disk forces requests to always route to that specific machine to get the data, going against the principle that state should live in shared storage.
Requiring the client to stay pinned to the same machine manufactures artificial stickiness — if that one machine fails, every user pinned to it is affected.
Vertical scaling alone means the only lever is upgrading a single machine's specs, which hits a hard ceiling once hardware limits are reached.

scenario: 每个用户 feed cache 如果无限保存所有历史 post_id，活跃多年后内存会持续膨胀。
scenario_en: If each user's feed cache stores every historical post ID forever, memory grows indefinitely over years.
q: 为什么要设置 feed cache 长度上限？
q_en: Why set a feed cache length limit?
options: 大多数用户只看最新内容，上限能控制内存
有了上限之后就不再需要数据库来兜底
上限能保证没有重复帖子
上限能替代隐私过滤
options_en: Most users read recent content, and a cap controls memory.
With a cap the database is no longer needed as backing store
A cap guarantees no duplicate posts.
A cap replaces privacy filtering.
why: feed cache 是近期加速层，不是永久历史库。控制长度能省内存，老内容可以回源或用分页补查。
why_en: The feed cache should accelerate recent reads, not become permanent history storage.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品要求离线快速翻完整历史，需要额外的持久索引，而不是只靠短 cache。

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求的数据不在缓存里，需要回源读取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache miss means requested data is not in cache and must be fetched from the source.

optionExplanations: 大多数用户只关心最近发生的内容，给 feed cache 设一个长度上限，能防止活跃多年的用户不断累积的历史 post_id 把内存无限撑大。
设了长度上限之后，早期以外的历史内容仍然需要靠数据库或持久索引来查，数据库并不会因此变得不需要。
长度上限只是限制保存多少条最近的 post_id，不涉及去重逻辑，本身保证不了没有重复帖子。
长度上限控制的是内存占用，跟隐私可见性过滤是完全不同的两个机制，替代不了它。
optionExplanations_en: Most users only care about recent content, so capping the feed cache's length keeps memory from growing without bound as a years-active user's history of post_ids keeps piling up.
Beyond that cap, older history still needs the database or a persistent index to be looked up — the database doesn't become unnecessary because of the cap.
The length cap just limits how many recent post_ids are kept — it doesn't involve any deduplication logic, so it can't by itself guarantee there are no duplicate posts.
The length cap controls memory usage, an entirely different mechanism from privacy visibility filtering — it can't substitute for it.

scenario: 用户发帖后，系统需要可靠保存帖子正文、作者、时间和媒体引用。
scenario_en: After a user posts, the system must reliably store text, author, timestamp, and media references.
q: post service 的核心职责是什么？
q_en: What is the core role of the post service?
options: 持久化帖子并更新 post cache
计算 DNS 解析
管理 APNS token
执行好友是否在线的 heartbeat 探测
options_en: Persist posts and update the post cache.
Perform DNS resolution.
Manage APNS tokens.
Run friend online heartbeats
why: post service 是内容写入的权威入口，fanout 只分发 post_id。这样内容存储和 feed 分发职责分清。
why_en: The post service owns content persistence while fanout distributes post IDs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存帖子对象或热门帖子字段的层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A post cache stores post objects or hot post fields.

optionExplanations: 对，post service 负责可靠地把帖子正文、作者、时间和媒体引用真正持久化下来，同时更新 post cache，是内容写入的权威入口。
DNS 解析是域名到 IP 的转换，跟保存一条帖子的内容毫无关系。
管理 APNS token 是推送通知系统里设备路由信息的职责，不属于 post service。
好友在线心跳检测的是连接是否存活，是完全不同系统的职责，跟保存帖子内容不相关。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the post service is responsible for reliably persisting the post body, author, timestamp, and media references, and updating the post cache — the authoritative entry point for content writes.
DNS resolution converts a domain to an IP — unrelated to saving a post's content.
Managing APNS tokens is device-routing responsibility inside a push notification system, not something the post service owns.
Friend online heartbeats check whether a connection is still alive, an entirely different system's responsibility, unrelated to saving post content.

scenario: 用户发帖请求已经通过鉴权；你要把内容写入存储并让好友 feed 尽快看到。
scenario_en: A publish request is authenticated; you need to store the content and make it appear in friends feeds quickly.
q: 发布链路顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the publish path order?
options: 先写 post，再异步 fanout
先通知好友，再决定是否保存帖子
客户端直接写所有好友 cache
只写 CDN
options_en: Persist post, then fan out asynchronously.
Notify friends first, then decide whether to save the post.
Let the client write every friend cache directly.
Write only to CDN.
why: 先持久化内容，后分发 ID，才能保证 feed 里引用的帖子存在。fanout 异步能保护发帖延迟。
why_en: Persist the post before distributing its ID so feed entries never point to missing content.
whenOtherWins: 如果是临时 story 且允许失败丢弃，持久化策略可以更短，但仍要先定义 source of truth。
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Client --> Web[Web server]
  Web --> Post[Post service]
  Post --> DB[(Post DB)]
  Post --> Q[Fanout queue]
  Q --> W[Fanout workers]
  W --> Feed[Feed cache]
optionExplanations: 先把内容真正持久化保存下来，再异步去分发 post_id，才能保证好友 feed 里引用的这个帖子确实是存在的，异步分发也保护了发帖本身的响应速度。
先通知好友再决定要不要保存帖子，会让好友收到一条实际上可能根本没有落库的帖子提醒，顺序完全反了。
客户端直接写所有好友的 cache，把本该由服务端统一管理的分发逻辑绕开了，既不安全也不可控。
只写 CDN 只处理了媒体分发，完全没有解决帖子正文该存在哪里、好友该怎么看到这条帖子的问题。
optionExplanations_en: Persisting the content first, then fanning out post_id asynchronously, guarantees the post referenced in a friend's feed actually exists, and the async fanout also protects the posting response's own speed.
Notifying friends before deciding whether to even save the post risks friends getting a notification for a post that may never actually get persisted — the order here is backwards.
Having the client write directly into every friend's cache bypasses what should be server-owned distribution logic entirely — neither safe nor controllable.
Writing only to the CDN handles only media distribution — it does nothing to address where the post body itself gets stored or how friends come to see it.

scenario: 最初需求是时间倒序；后来产品要求亲密好友、互动概率和内容质量影响顺序。
scenario_en: The initial requirement is reverse chronological; later product wants close friends, engagement probability, and content quality to affect order.
q: 要加哪类组件？
q_en: What component should be added?
options: ranking service 给候选打分
DNS resolver
短信 gateway
crawler 的 robots parser
options_en: Use a ranking service to score candidates.
A DNS resolver.
An SMS gateway.
A crawler's robots parser.
why: 一旦排序不只是时间，就要把候选生成和排序打分拆开。代价是特征缓存、模型延迟和解释复杂度。
why_en: Once ordering is not purely time-based, separate candidate generation from ranking.
tradeoff: 相关性排序 vs 系统复杂度
whenOtherWins: 如果面试范围明确只要时间倒序，ranking service 可以先不画。

termDefinitions.meaning: 先找出可能展示的内容集合，再交给排序层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Candidate generation finds the set of content items that a ranking layer may order.

optionExplanations: 一旦排序要考虑亲密度、互动概率和内容质量这些因素，就需要一个专门给候选帖子打分排序的服务，把候选生成和排序打分这两步拆开来做。
DNS resolver 负责域名解析，跟按互动概率和内容质量给帖子排序完全不是一回事。
短信 gateway 是通知系统里发送短信的通道，跟新闻流的排序需求毫无关系。
robots parser 是爬虫系统里解析抓取规则的组件，跟新闻流该怎么排序完全不搭边。
optionExplanations_en: Once ordering has to factor in closeness, engagement probability, and content quality, a dedicated service for scoring and ranking candidate posts is needed, splitting candidate generation apart from ranking.
A DNS resolver handles domain resolution, entirely unrelated to ranking posts by engagement probability and content quality.
An SMS gateway is a notification system's channel for sending texts, unrelated to a news feed's ranking requirements.
A robots parser is a crawler-system component for parsing crawl rules, unrelated to how a news feed should be ranked.

scenario: 用户下滑 feed，需要稳定加载下一页；新帖子可能同时插入顶部。
scenario_en: A user scrolls the feed and needs a stable next page while new posts may arrive at the top.
q: 分页参数怎么选更稳？
q_en: Which pagination parameter is more stable?
options: cursor 分页，用末条作边界
offset += limit 永远稳定
每次随机取 20 条
让客户端传好友总数
options_en: Use cursor pagination with the last item as boundary.
offset += limit is always stable.
Fetch 20 random posts each time.
Have the client send friend count.
why: feed 会不断插入新内容，offset 容易重复或跳过。cursor 用已见边界继续查，滚动体验更稳。
why_en: A live feed changes under the user, so cursor pagination is more stable than offset.
tradeoff: 分页稳定性 vs 接口状态复杂度
whenOtherWins: 静态后台列表用 offset/limit 更简单。

termDefinitions.meaning: 用上一页边界值继续查询下一页的分页方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cursor pagination uses a boundary value from the previous page to fetch the next page.

optionExplanations: feed 会不断有新帖子插进顶部，用上一页最后一条作为边界继续往下查的 cursor 分页，不会因为顶部插入新内容而重复或跳过条目，滚动体验更稳。
offset += limit 在新内容不断插入顶部的场景下并不稳定，顶部一插入新帖，后面所有 offset 对应的位置都会跟着往后错位。
每次随机取 20 条完全放弃了顺序和连续性，用户下滑时看到的内容会杂乱无章，也没法实现稳定翻页。
让客户端传好友总数既不能标记翻页边界在哪，也没法应对好友关系随时可能变化这个事实。
optionExplanations_en: With new posts constantly being inserted at the top, cursor pagination using the last item on the previous page as the boundary avoids repeating or skipping items as new content lands on top, giving a more stable scroll experience.
offset += limit isn't stable when new content keeps getting inserted at the top — every insertion at the top shifts what every later offset actually points to.
Randomly grabbing 20 items each time abandons order and continuity entirely, leaving the user with a jumbled scroll and no way to achieve stable pagination.
Having the client pass a friend-count total neither marks where the pagination boundary is nor accounts for the fact that friend relationships can change at any time.

scenario: feed cache 只保留最近 1000 条；用户一直向下翻，老 post_id 不在缓存里了。
scenario_en: The feed cache keeps only the latest 1,000 entries; a user scrolls far enough that older post IDs are no longer cached.
q: cache miss 怎么处理？
q_en: How should this cache miss be handled?
options: 回源或重建旧页
直接报 feed 永久丢失
清空用户所有缓存
让客户端猜旧帖子
options_en: Fallback to source storage or rebuild old pages.
Report the feed as permanently lost.
Clear all user caches.
Let the client guess old posts.
why: cache 是加速层，miss 时必须有慢路径。慢路径可以查持久索引或按好友历史重新合并。
why_en: A cache is an acceleration layer, so misses need a slower source-of-truth path.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品只支持有限窗口 feed，超过窗口可以明确返回无更多内容。

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统中最权威、可恢复状态的数据源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The source of truth is the authoritative data source used for recovery.

optionExplanations: 缓存本来就是加速层，命中不了的时候要有慢路径兜底，查持久索引或者按好友历史重新合并出这一页内容，都是可行的回源方式。
直接报 feed 永久丢失是过度悲观的处理，内容其实还在持久存储里，只是没在这份近期缓存里而已。
清空用户所有缓存跟“往下翻到老内容没命中”这个具体场景不对应，会把本来还有效的近期缓存也一起清掉。
让客户端自己猜旧帖子完全没有依据，客户端根本没有能力知道那些超出缓存范围的历史内容具体是什么。
optionExplanations_en: A cache is fundamentally an acceleration layer, so a miss needs a fallback slow path — querying a persistent index or re-merging from friend history are both workable ways to go back to the source.
Reporting the feed as permanently lost is overly pessimistic — the content is still sitting in persistent storage, it just isn't in this recent cache.
Clearing the user's entire cache doesn't match the specific scenario of scrolling into older, uncached content — it would also wipe out perfectly valid recent cache entries.
Letting the client guess at old posts has nothing to go on — the client has no way of knowing what that older, out-of-cache history actually contained.

scenario: 用户刚发帖后立刻刷新自己首页；异步 fanout 可能还没把 post_id 写入她自己的 feed cache。
scenario_en: A user posts and immediately refreshes their own feed; async fanout may not have written the post ID into their feed cache yet.
q: 如何保证写后可读体验？
q_en: How can read-your-writes be preserved?
options: 合并本人新帖或同步写自己 feed
等待所有好友 fanout 完成再返回发帖
告诉用户刷新三分钟后再看
只清空 feed cache
options_en: Merge own new posts or sync-write own feed.
Wait for all friend fanout to finish before returning publish.
Tell users to refresh in three minutes.
Only clear the feed cache.
why: 用户最敏感的是自己刚写的内容能否看到，可以给自己走快路径。好友 feed 仍可异步完成。
why_en: Preserve read-your-writes for the author with a fast path while friend fanout remains asynchronous.
tradeoff: 用户一致性体验 vs 发布延迟
whenOtherWins: 如果产品允许最终一致，简单异步 fanout 也能工作，但体验差一些。

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户写入后，自己的后续读取能看到刚写的数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read-your-writes means a user can read their own recent write immediately.

optionExplanations: 用户最在意的是自己刚发的内容能不能立刻看到，给自己走一条快路径、同步合并或直接写自己的 feed，能满足这个最敏感的体验，好友那边照常异步完成就行。
等所有好友都 fanout 完成才返回发帖成功，会让发帖请求的响应时间跟着好友数一起变长，代价太大。
让用户等三分钟再刷新，直接牺牲了她最关心的“自己刚发的内容能不能马上看到”这个体验。
只清空 feed cache 不会主动把这条新帖子加进去，用户刷新后大概率还是看不到自己刚发的内容。
optionExplanations_en: What a user cares about most is whether their own just-posted content shows up immediately, so giving themselves a fast path — a synchronous merge or direct write to their own feed — satisfies that most sensitive part of the experience, while friends' feeds still finish asynchronously as usual.
Waiting until every friend's fanout finishes before confirming the post succeeded ties the response time to friend count — too costly.
Telling the user to wait three minutes and refresh directly sacrifices the exact experience they care most about: seeing their own just-posted content right away.
Just clearing the feed cache doesn't actively insert the new post — the user is still likely to not see their own content after refreshing.

scenario: 名人帖子不预推给所有粉丝；粉丝打开 feed 时还要看到名人最近内容。
scenario_en: Celebrity posts are not pre-pushed to all followers; a follower should still see recent celebrity posts when opening the feed.
q: 读取时怎么合并名人内容？
q_en: How should celebrity content be merged on read?
options: 拉名人近期帖再合并
完全隐藏名人帖子
把名人所有历史一次性写入 cache
让客户端调用名人数据库
options_en: Pull recent celebrity posts and merge.
Hide celebrity posts entirely.
Write all celebrity history into cache at once.
Let the client call the celebrity database.
why: 名人例外把成本从写时推迟到真正读的人身上。读取服务要多拉一批候选再按时间或排名合并。
why_en: The celebrity exception shifts work to active readers, who pull and merge celebrity candidates on demand.
whenOtherWins: 如果名人粉丝也很少，写时推更简单。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多个有序候选列表合成一个展示列表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Merge combines multiple ordered candidate lists into one display list.

tradeoff: 写时预分发成本 vs 读时合并成本
optionExplanations: 名人的内容没有预先推给所有粉丝，粉丝打开 feed 时读取服务要另外去拉一批名人最近的帖子，再按时间或排名跟已有内容合并展示。
完全隐藏名人帖子会让粉丝再也看不到他们关注的名人内容，跟“还要看到名人最近内容”这个要求正相反。
把名人所有历史一次性写入 cache，等于把写时推的成本换了个时间点做，同样会造成巨大的写放大。
让客户端直接调用名人数据库，等于把本该由服务端统一处理的合并逻辑绕开，给客户端增加了不该有的复杂度和风险。
optionExplanations_en: A celebrity's content was never pre-pushed to every follower, so when a follower opens their feed, the read service has to separately pull the celebrity's recent posts and merge them into the display by time or rank.
Completely hiding celebrity posts means followers never see content from people they follow at all, the opposite of the requirement that they still see recent celebrity content.
Writing a celebrity's entire history into cache all at once just shifts the fan-out-on-write cost to a different moment — it still causes massive write amplification.
Having the client call the celebrity database directly bypasses what should be server-owned merge logic, adding complexity and risk the client shouldn't have to carry.

scenario: 某用户发帖后，好友可能不在 App 内；系统想提示有新内容，但不能阻塞发帖。
scenario_en: A user posts while friends may be outside the app; the system wants to alert them without blocking publishing.
q: 通知触发放在哪里？
q_en: Where should notification triggering happen?
options: 异步事件触发 notification service
发帖 API 同步等待所有 push 全部完成再返回
客户端逐个通知好友
数据库触发器直接打 APNS
options_en: Trigger notification service from async events.
Have the publish API wait for every push
Make the client notify every friend.
Let a database trigger call APNS directly.
why: 通知是副作用，适合跟着异步事件走。否则发帖延迟会被第三方推送服务拖住。
why_en: Notifications are side effects, so trigger them asynchronously rather than blocking the publish request.
whenOtherWins: 如果是少量强事务提醒，也可以同步记录通知意图，但投递仍建议异步。

termDefinitions.meaning: 主写入之外派生出的动作，例如通知、分析或缓存更新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A side effect is a derived action outside the main write, such as notification, analytics, or cache update.

optionExplanations: 通知是发帖之后的一个副作用，让它跟着异步事件走，才不会让发帖请求被第三方推送服务的响应时间拖住。
让发帖 API 同步等所有 push 完成，意味着这次发帖的响应时间要看第三方推送服务的脸色，完全违背了发帖该快速返回的目标。
让客户端逐个通知好友，把本该由服务端统一处理的推送逻辑丢给了客户端，既不现实也不安全。
数据库触发器直接打 APNS，会让数据库承担起它本不该管的外部网络调用职责，还很难做重试和限流。
optionExplanations_en: Notification is a side effect of posting, and letting it follow an async event means the post request never gets held up by how long a third-party push service takes to respond.
