Having the post API wait synchronously for every push to finish makes the post response's speed hostage to the third-party push service — directly against the goal of a fast-returning post.
Having the client notify friends one by one dumps what should be server-owned push logic onto the client — neither realistic nor safe.
A database trigger calling APNS directly saddles the database with an external network call it was never meant to own, and makes retry and rate limiting difficult.

scenario: fanout 每次都要查作者好友列表；图数据库扛不住热门用户频繁发帖。
scenario_en: Fanout must fetch the author friend list each time; the graph database cannot handle frequent posts from hot users.
q: 好友列表读取怎么优化？
q_en: How can friend-list reads be optimized?
options: 缓存好友 ID 列表，并在关系变更时失效
每次全表扫描关系表
把好友 ID 列表直接塞进帖子的正文里
关闭 fanout
options_en: Cache friend ID lists and invalidate them on relationship changes.
Scan the relationship table every time.
Embed the friend ID list in the post body
Disable fanout.
why: 好友列表读多写少，缓存能减少图服务压力。关系变更时要失效，否则会推给旧好友或漏新好友。
why_en: Friend lists are read-heavy, so cache them but invalidate on relationship changes.
whenOtherWins: 如果隐私规则很复杂，缓存只能存候选好友，最终可见性还要单独判断。

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户之间好友、关注、屏蔽等关系组成的图。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A social graph is the network of friendships, follows, blocks, and similar relationships.

tradeoff: 图服务压力 vs 好友关系新鲜度
optionExplanations: 好友列表读多写少，缓存好友 ID 列表能大幅减轻图服务的查询压力，只要在关系变更时主动让缓存失效，就不会推给已经不是好友的人或漏掉新加的好友。
每次都全表扫描关系表，正是热门用户频繁发帖时会把图数据库压垮的做法，跟想解决的问题方向相反。
把好友列表放在帖子正文里，会让每条帖子都携带一份可能很大且很快过时的好友列表，既浪费空间也不准确。
关闭 fanout 直接放弃了内容分发这个核心功能，不是解决查询压力问题该有的办法。
optionExplanations_en: Friend lists are read far more than written, so caching the friend ID list takes a lot of load off the graph service, and invalidating it on relationship changes keeps it from pushing to people who unfriended or missing newly added friends.
Full-table scanning the relationship table every time is exactly what overwhelms the graph database when a popular user posts frequently — the opposite direction from solving the problem.
Putting the friend list into the post body itself means every post carries a potentially large and quickly stale friend list — wasteful and inaccurate.
Turning off fanout gives up on core content distribution entirely — not a real answer to a query-pressure problem.

scenario: fanout worker 写 feed cache 后崩溃，队列重投同一 post_id；可能重复出现在好友 feed。
scenario_en: A fanout worker crashes after writing feed cache, and the queue redelivers the same post_id; it may appear twice in a friend feed.
q: feed 写入要怎么防重复？
q_en: How should feed writes avoid duplicates?
options: 用 (user_id, post_id) 幂等写
每一次写入都用一个随机生成的新 post_id
关闭队列重试
让客户端手动删除重复
options_en: Use idempotent (user_id, post_id) writes.
Write a randomly generated new post_id every time
Disable queue retries.
Ask the client to delete duplicates manually.
why: 异步 worker 必须假设任务会重复执行，写入键要能天然去重。否则可靠重试会换来重复 feed。
why_en: Async workers must tolerate duplicate execution, so feed entries need idempotent keys.
whenOtherWins: 如果底层 cache 只支持列表 append，就要在读取或写入前做去重。

termDefinitions.meaning: 重复执行多次仍只产生一次有效结果的写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotent write has the same final effect even if repeated.

optionExplanations: 用 (user_id, post_id) 这个组合作为幂等写入键，即使队列因为 worker 崩溃重投同一个任务，重复写入也会落到同一个位置，不会在好友 feed 里出现两次。
每次写入都用随机 post_id，会让同一条帖子被重复写入时被当成两条不同的记录，反而制造了真正的重复。
关闭队列重试意味着 worker 崩溃后这次分发就直接丢失了，用不重试换来不重复的代价过大。
让客户端手动删除重复，把本该由服务端保证的幂等性丢给了用户自己去发现和处理，既不现实也很差体验。
optionExplanations_en: Using (user_id, post_id) as the idempotent write key means even if the queue redelivers the same task after a worker crash, the duplicate write lands on the same slot instead of showing up twice in a friend's feed.
Writing with a random post_id every time makes the same post look like two different records when it's rewritten — actually creating the duplicate instead of preventing it.
Turning off queue retries means a fanout is simply lost the moment a worker crashes — too high a price to pay just to avoid duplicates.
Having the client manually delete duplicates dumps what should be server-guaranteed idempotency onto the user to discover and fix themselves — unrealistic and a poor experience.

scenario: feed cache 需要按时间倒序取最近 N 个 post_id，还要快速追加新 post_id。
scenario_en: The feed cache needs the latest N post IDs in reverse time order and fast appends for new posts.
q: 用什么结构表达更自然？
q_en: Which structure is natural?
options: list 或 sorted set
把整个 feed 拼成一个全局字符串
图片 CDN 目录
DNS 记录
options_en: A list or sorted set.
Concatenate the whole feed into one global string.
An image CDN directory.
A DNS record.
why: 用户 feed 是 per-user 有序集合，追加和截断都围绕这个 key。sorted set 还能按分数范围分页。
why_en: A feed is a per-user ordered collection, so lists or sorted sets support append, trim, and pagination.
whenOtherWins: 如果 feed 完全实时计算，不维护 per-user cache，就不需要这个结构。

termDefinitions.meaning: 带分数的集合，可按分数排序和范围查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sorted set stores members with scores and supports ordered range queries.

tradeoff: 追加/分页效率 vs 数据结构复杂度
optionExplanations: list 或 sorted set 天然按顺序组织元素，追加新 post_id 和按时间倒序取最近 N 个都能高效完成，围绕这一个 key 就能搞定。
单个全局字符串没法表达“每个用户各自一份、按时间排序”的结构，追加和截取都会变得非常笨拙。
图片 CDN 目录管的是媒体文件的组织方式，跟维护每个用户自己的 post_id 有序列表完全不是一回事。
DNS 记录是域名解析用的条目，跟需要频繁追加和按时间查询的 feed 列表毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: A list or sorted set naturally keeps elements ordered, making both appending a new post_id and pulling the most recent N in reverse-chronological order efficient, all around a single key.
A single global string can't express "one ordered structure per user" at all — both appending and slicing would become extremely awkward.
An image CDN directory organizes media files, an entirely different concern from maintaining each user's own ordered list of post_ids.
A DNS record is an entry used for name resolution, unrelated to a feed list that needs frequent appends and time-based queries.

scenario: post cache 中保存媒体 URL，但图片和视频字节在 CDN；feed service 返回时要怎么组装？
scenario_en: The post cache stores media URLs while image and video bytes live in the CDN; the feed service must assemble a response.
q: 返回体里应放什么？
q_en: What should the response contain?
options: 返回帖子字段和 CDN URL
把视频二进制塞进 JSON
只返回 CDN 节点 IP
删除媒体字段
options_en: Return post fields and CDN URLs.
Put video binary inside JSON.
Return only CDN node IPs.
Remove media fields.
why: feed JSON 应轻量，客户端再用 URL 拉媒体。内联大文件会拖慢 API，也绕开 CDN 缓存。
why_en: Feed JSON should return media references, letting clients fetch bytes from the CDN.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端可用来下载图片或视频的地址。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A media URL is an address the client can use to fetch an image or video.

optionExplanations: 把帖子字段和指向 CDN 的媒体 URL 一起返回，客户端拿到 URL 后再单独去 CDN 拉媒体，feed 接口本身保持轻量。
把视频二进制直接塞进 JSON 响应体，会让这个本该轻量的接口变得极其臃肿缓慢，也完全绕开了 CDN 本该发挥的缓存作用。
只返回 CDN 节点 IP 对客户端没有实际意义，客户端需要的是能直接请求媒体的完整 URL，不是底层节点地址。
删除媒体字段会让客户端完全拿不到图片和视频，这条 feed item 就没法正常展示媒体内容了。
optionExplanations_en: Returning post fields together with the CDN media URL keeps the feed response light, letting the client separately fetch media from the CDN using that URL.

Stuffing raw video bytes directly into the JSON response makes what should be a lightweight endpoint extremely bloated and slow, and completely bypasses the caching benefit the CDN is there to provide.
Returning only the CDN node's IP is useless to the client, which actually needs a complete URL it can request media from directly, not a low-level node address.
Dropping the media field entirely leaves the client with no way to get the image or video, so this feed item can no longer display its media at all.

scenario: 作者删除帖子；该 post_id 可能已经被写进很多好友的 feed cache。
scenario_en: An author deletes a post; its post_id may already exist in many friends feed caches.
q: 删除怎么处理更稳？
q_en: How should deletion be handled?
options: 标 deleted，读时过滤，异步清理
只删作者本地页面
要求所有好友立即同步删除完成后才返回
让 CDN 决定权限
options_en: Mark deleted, filter on read, clean async.
Delete only the author’s local page.
Wait for every friend cache deletion before returning.
Let the CDN decide permissions.
why: 读时过滤能快速生效，不必同步扫所有 feed cache。异步清理再回收空间，代价是读取要检查状态。
why_en: Mark-and-filter makes deletion visible quickly while asynchronous cleanup removes stale feed entries later.
whenOtherWins: 如果法规要求强删除，清理任务和媒体删除要有更严格 SLA。

termDefinitions.meaning: 删除标记，表示对象已删除但记录暂时保留。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tombstone is a deletion marker kept after an object is removed.

optionExplanations: 先把帖子标记成已删除，读取时把这类内容过滤掉，能立刻在展示层面生效，不用同步去扫每一个已经写入这条 post_id 的好友 feed cache，之后再慢慢异步清理回收空间。
只删作者本地页面，其他好友 feed cache 里的这条帖子依然存在且照常可见，没有真正完成删除。
要求所有好友都立即同步删除完成才返回，等于要在这次删除请求里扫遍并等待所有相关 feed cache 全部处理完，会让删除操作变得极慢。
让 CDN 决定权限，CDN 负责的是就近分发媒体字节，不具备判断一条帖子是否该被删除、对谁可见这类业务逻辑的能力。
optionExplanations_en: Marking the post deleted and filtering it out on read takes effect immediately at the display layer, without having to synchronously sweep through every friend's feed cache that already has this post_id — cleanup and space reclamation can happen asynchronously afterward.
Deleting only the author's own local page leaves the post still present and visible in every friend's feed cache — the deletion never actually took effect elsewhere.
Requiring every friend's feed cache to finish syncing the deletion before returning means scanning and waiting on every related cache within this one request, making deletion extremely slow.

Letting the CDN decide permissions misunderstands its job — a CDN handles nearby distribution of media bytes and has no capacity to judge business logic like whether a post should be deleted or who it's visible to.

scenario: 用户跨地区访问 feed；单机房故障时仍希望能读到最近内容，允许短暂旧数据。
scenario_en: Users access feed across regions; during one data-center failure they should still read recent content, with brief staleness allowed.
q: 多机房 feed 读怎么设计？
q_en: How should multi-region feed reads be designed?
options: 跨区复制，读本地副本
所有读都强制跨洲回主库
不做复制，故障时全站不可用
把 feed 放进用户浏览器永久缓存
options_en: Replicate across regions and read local replicas.
Force every read across continents to the primary database.
Do no replication and go down on failure.
Keep the feed permanently in the browser cache.
why: feed 读多且可容忍短暂旧数据，本地副本能降延迟和提高可用性。代价是跨区一致性要解释清楚。
why_en: For read-heavy feeds, local replicas reduce latency and improve availability at the cost of short staleness.
tradeoff: 本地低延迟可用性 vs 强一致
whenOtherWins: 如果是金融余额 feed，可能必须读主库或做强一致协议。

termDefinitions.meaning: 主数据的一份副本，用于读扩展或容灾。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A replica is a copy of data used for read scaling or failover.

optionExplanations: feed 读多、也能容忍短暂的旧数据，跨区域复制、让用户读本地副本，能在降低延迟的同时，让单机房故障时其他区域仍然可以正常读取。
让所有读都强制跨洲回主库，会让每一次刷新首页都背上一次跨洲往返延迟，用户体验会明显变差。
不做复制、故障时全站不可用，意味着一个机房出问题就会波及所有用户，跟“仍希望能读到最近内容”的要求正相反。
把 feed 放进浏览器永久缓存，既没法让内容保持更新，也不是真正意义上跨机房容灾该走的路径。
optionExplanations_en: Reads are frequent and tolerant of brief staleness, so replicating across regions and reading from the local copy both lowers latency and keeps other regions readable when a single datacenter goes down.
Forcing every read back across continents to the primary saddles every homepage refresh with a cross-continent round trip, noticeably hurting the experience.
Skipping replication and going fully unavailable during an outage means one datacenter's failure affects every user — the opposite of the requirement to still read recent content.
Putting the feed into the browser's permanent cache neither keeps content current nor is a real path toward cross-datacenter disaster tolerance.

scenario: 每个 feed item 要展示点赞数和回复数；这些数变化频繁，读请求也很多。
scenario_en: Each feed item shows like and reply counts; these counts change often and are read heavily.
q: counter 怎么存更合适？
q_en: How should counters be stored?
options: 独立 counter cache
每次展示都 count 全表
把计数写进媒体文件名
让客户端自己累计
options_en: Use a dedicated counter cache.
Count the full table on every render.
Put counts in media filenames.
Let clients compute them locally.
why: 计数是高频小对象，独立缓存能扛读写。代价是要处理计数短暂不准和回写失败。
why_en: Counters are hot small objects, so a dedicated counter cache handles read/write pressure.
whenOtherWins: 如果写量很低，数据库聚合加缓存可能先够。

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门缓存点赞数、评论数等聚合计数的层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A counter cache stores aggregate counts such as likes and comments.

tradeoff: 计数读写速度 vs 精确一致和恢复成本
optionExplanations: 点赞数、回复数变化频繁又要支撑大量读请求，独立的 counter 缓存能专门扛住这种高频小对象的读写，跟正文内容分开管理。
每次展示都对全表做一次计数聚合查询，在读请求量很大的情况下会给数据库带来沉重且完全没必要的负担。
把计数写进媒体文件名既没有更新计数的正常途径，也会让文件名本身变得不稳定，是完全不合理的做法。
让客户端自己累计计数，不同客户端各自算出来的数字很容易对不上，也没法反映其他人的真实点赞和回复。
optionExplanations_en: Like and reply counts change constantly and get hit by heavy read traffic, so a dedicated counter cache is built to absorb this kind of high-frequency small-object read/write, kept separate from the post body.
Running a full aggregation count query on every display would put a heavy and entirely unnecessary load on the database given how much read traffic this sees.
Encoding the count into a media filename gives no normal way to update it and makes the filename itself unstable — an entirely unreasonable approach.
Letting the client accumulate its own count easily drifts out of sync between different clients and can't reflect other people's actual likes and replies.

scenario: 系统上线后，用户抱怨刷新慢；你要知道慢在取 ID、hydrate、ranking 还是媒体加载。
scenario_en: After launch, users complain feed refresh is slow; you need to know whether the delay is ID fetch, hydration, ranking, or media loading.
q: 应该怎么埋点？
q_en: How should latency be instrumented?
options: 按阶段记录延迟和命中率
只记录总请求数
只看发帖 QPS
只看 CDN 账单
options_en: Record latency and hit rate by stage.
Record only total request count.
Look only at publish QPS.
Look only at the CDN bill.
why: feed 是多阶段组合，总延迟不拆开就找不到瓶颈。分位数能暴露尾延迟。
why_en: A feed read has multiple stages, so per-stage percentiles and hit rates reveal the real bottleneck.

termDefinitions.meaning: 95th percentile，95% 请求不超过该延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p95 is the 95th percentile latency: 95% of requests are no slower.

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求命中缓存的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache hit rate is the fraction of requests served from cache.

optionExplanations: 按取 ID、hydrate、ranking、媒体加载这几个阶段分别记录延迟和缓存命中率，才能定位到底是哪一步在拖慢刷新，总延迟拆开才有意义。
只记录总请求数看不出延迟到底花在哪一步，没法回答“慢在取 ID、hydrate 还是媒体加载”这个具体问题。
只看发帖 QPS 关注的是写路径的流量，跟用户抱怨的刷新慢这个读路径体验问题完全不是一回事。
只看 CDN 账单反映的是成本，不是延迟具体卡在哪个环节，回答不了排查慢在哪里这个问题。
optionExplanations_en: Recording latency and hit rate separately for each stage — fetching IDs, hydrating, ranking, and loading media — is what actually locates which step is slowing the refresh; breaking total latency apart is the whole point.
Recording only total request count shows nothing about where the latency actually goes, and can't answer the specific question of whether it's ID fetching, hydration, or media loading that's slow.
Watching only post QPS focuses on write-path traffic, an entirely different concern from the read-path experience users are complaining is slow.
Watching only the CDN bill reflects cost, not where along the pipeline the latency is actually stuck — it can't answer the question of where the slowdown is.

scenario: 有人建议所有 feed 都读时聚合，因为写路径最简单；另一个人建议所有都写时推。
scenario_en: One engineer suggests read-time aggregation for every feed because writes are simple; another suggests write fanout for everyone.
q: 这两个方案的核心取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the core tradeoff?
options: 读延迟和写放大之间取舍
DNS 延迟和 robots 规则之间取舍
短信成本和邮件模板之间取舍
图片大小和视频编码之间取舍
options_en: Read latency versus write amplification.
DNS latency versus robots rules.
SMS cost versus email templates.
Image size versus video encoding.
why: 读时聚合省写但打开首页慢；写时推读快但发帖成本随粉丝数增长。混合方案就是围绕这条轴做例外处理。
why_en: Feed fanout is mainly a tradeoff between read latency and write amplification.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次逻辑写入引发多次物理写入的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write amplification means one logical write causes many physical writes.

tradeoff: 读时成本 vs 写时放大
optionExplanations: 读时聚合把成本推迟到打开首页的那一刻，写便宜但读慢；写时推提前把结果算好，读快但发帖成本随粉丝数一起放大，两个方案争的正是这条轴。
DNS 延迟和 robots 规则都是爬虫系统里的概念，跟新闻流该在读时聚合还是写时推毫不相关。
短信成本和邮件模板是通知系统的关注点，跟这里讨论的 feed 构建方式完全是另一个话题。
图片大小和视频编码是媒体处理层面的问题，跟读时聚合还是写时推这个 feed 架构层面的取舍不在一个维度上。
optionExplanations_en: Read-time aggregation defers the cost to the moment the homepage opens, cheap to write but slow to read; write-time fanout precomputes the result ahead of time, fast to read but with posting cost scaling with follower count — this exact axis is what the two proposals are fighting over.
DNS latency and robots rules are crawler-system concepts, unrelated to whether a news feed aggregates on read or fans out on write.
SMS cost and email templates are notification-system concerns, an entirely different topic from the feed-construction tradeoff being discussed here.
Image size and video encoding are media-processing concerns, on a different dimension entirely from the read-versus-write architectural tradeoff being discussed.

scenario: 聊天接收方需要服务器主动推新消息；连接要长期存在，消息要低延迟到达。
scenario_en: The chat recipient needs the server to push new messages over a long-lived connection with low latency.
q: 主通信协议选什么？
q_en: Which main communication protocol fits?
options: WebSocket
短轮询 polling
每天批量 email
只用离线文件同步
options_en: WebSocket.
Short polling.
Daily batch email.
Offline file sync only.
why: WebSocket 是客户端发起但后续双向持久，适合服务器主动推消息。代价是 chat server 要管理大量长连接状态。
why_en: WebSocket gives a bidirectional persistent connection, which fits server-pushed chat messages while making connection management stateful.
tradeoff: 实时双向推送 vs 长连接状态成本
whenOtherWins: 如果只是低频通知且实时性弱，轮询或 push notification 可以更简单。

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种从 HTTP 握手升级来的双向持久连接协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a bidirectional persistent protocol upgraded from an HTTP handshake.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端定时问服务器有没有新数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Polling means the client repeatedly asks the server for new data.

codeSample:
GET /chat HTTP/1.1
Host: chat.example.com
Upgrade: websocket
Connection: Upgrade
Sec-WebSocket-Key: <nonce>
optionExplanations: 连接建立后能双向长期保持，服务器随时能主动往下推新消息，正好匹配聊天要求的低延迟主动推送，代价是服务器要长期管理大量连接状态。
短轮询要客户端不断主动发请求来问有没有新消息，天然带来延迟和大量无效请求，不适合低延迟场景。
每天批量 email 的延迟是以天为单位的，跟聊天要求的低延迟到达完全不在一个量级上。
离线文件同步没有实时推送能力，用户不打开客户端主动同步就完全看不到新消息。
optionExplanations_en: Once established, the connection stays open in both directions, letting the server push new messages any time, matching the low-latency, server-initiated push chat needs — the cost is the server having to manage a huge amount of long-lived connection state.
Short polling requires the client to keep actively asking whether anything's new, inherently adding latency and a mountain of wasted requests — a poor fit for low latency.
Batching email once a day has latency measured in days, nowhere near the same order of magnitude as the low latency chat requires.
Offline file sync has no real-time push capability at all — without the client actively opening and syncing, new messages simply never show up.

scenario: 你用 long polling 做聊天；负载均衡可能把发送方请求和接收方挂起连接分到不同服务器。
scenario_en: You use long polling for chat; load balancing may send the sender request and receiver's hanging request to different servers.
q: long polling 的主要麻烦是什么？
q_en: What is a main problem with long polling?
options: 服务器难知道客户端断开，且连接所在服务器不一定有新消息
它不能发任何 HTTP 请求
它只能用于图片下载
它天然就能保证 exactly once 的投递语义
options_en: The server may not know disconnects, and the right connection may be on another server.
It cannot send HTTP requests at all.
It only works for image downloads.
It naturally guarantees exactly-once delivery semantics
why: long polling 能模拟推送，但连接分布和断线检测都麻烦。WebSocket 仍要管状态，但语义更贴近实时双向通道。
why_en: Long polling can simulate push, but connection placement and disconnect detection make it awkward for real-time chat.
tradeoff: 兼容 HTTP 请求模型 vs 实时连接语义
whenOtherWins: 如果环境不允许 WebSocket，long polling 仍是可用降级方案。

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端发起请求后服务器暂不返回，直到有新数据或超时。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Long polling holds a client request open until data is available or a timeout occurs.

optionExplanations: 接收方挂起的连接停在某台服务器上，发送方的消息却可能打到另一台机器，服务器也很难及时判断客户端到底是不是真的断开了，这些都是 long polling 天生要面对的麻烦。
long polling 本质上还是走 HTTP 请求，完全可以发普通请求，说它不能发任何 HTTP 请求不成立。
它是一种通用的服务端推送模拟手段，不限定只能用来下载图片。
投递语义要靠消息 ID 去重和 ACK 保证，跟请求挂起多久没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: A receiver's pending connection sits parked on one server while a sender's message might land on an entirely different machine, and the server also struggles to promptly tell whether a client has truly disconnected — both are inherent troubles with long polling.
Long polling is fundamentally still an HTTP request underneath and can send ordinary requests just fine — claiming it can't send any HTTP request doesn't hold.
It is a general way to emulate server push, not something limited to image downloads.
Delivery semantics come from message IDs, dedupe, and acks — not from how long a request hangs.

scenario: 每个在线客户端都和某台 chat server 保持 WebSocket；连接期间通常不频繁迁移。
scenario_en: Each online client keeps a WebSocket to one chat server and normally does not move during the connection.
q: chat service 为什么是 stateful？
q_en: Why is the chat service stateful?
options: 服务器持有长连接和在线会话映射
它只处理登录表单
它完全没有任何内存里的连接状态
它只存静态图片
options_en: It holds long-lived connections and online session mappings.
It only handles login forms.
It has no in-memory connection state at all
It only stores static images.
why: 连接本身就是状态，服务要知道用户在哪台机器上在线。失败恢复要靠 service discovery 让客户端重连新 server。
why_en: The chat server is stateful because live connections and user-to-server mappings live on it.
whenOtherWins: 登录、资料修改这类普通请求仍适合无状态 API server。

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务实例保存会影响后续请求的会话或连接状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A stateful service keeps session or connection state that affects later requests.

tradeoff: 长连接路由能力 vs 无状态扩容简单性
optionExplanations: 每个在线用户的长连接和当前登录在哪台机器上的映射，都实实在在地保存在服务进程里，这份内存状态正是它有状态的原因。
登录表单属于普通的一次性请求，处理它不需要维护长期存在的连接和会话映射，跟聊天服务的有状态性质不是一回事。
服务器要持续持有 WebSocket 连接对象和用户在线会话映射，说它没有任何内存状态不成立。
它承载的核心是消息和连接状态，不是静态图片，把它说成只存静态图片完全说错了服务的职责。
optionExplanations_en: Every online user's live connection and which machine they're currently logged into are both genuinely held in the service process's memory — that in-memory state is exactly why it's stateful.
Handling a login form is an ordinary one-off request that needs no long-lived connection or session mapping — unrelated to why a chat service is stateful.
The server has to continuously hold onto the WebSocket connection object and the online session mapping — claiming it has no in-memory state at all doesn't hold.
Its core payload is messages and connection state, not static images — describing it as only storing static images completely mischaracterizes what the service does.

scenario: 用户登录后，需要选择一台延迟低、容量还够的 chat server 来建立 WebSocket。
scenario_en: After login, a user needs a low-latency chat server with enough capacity for a WebSocket connection.
q: 谁来推荐 chat server？
q_en: Who should recommend the chat server?
options: service discovery
让客户端自己随机猜一个可用的 IP
消息数据库返回 HTML
短信供应商分配连接
options_en: Service discovery.
The client randomly guesses an IP
The message database returns HTML.
The SMS provider assigns the connection.
why: service discovery 维护可用 chat server 和负载信息，能避免新连接压到满载机器。代价是它本身要高可用。
why_en: Service discovery tracks available chat servers and load so new clients connect to a suitable instance.
tradeoff: 连接均衡 vs 发现服务复杂度
whenOtherWins: 小规模 demo 可以先用静态配置或负载均衡直连。

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录服务实例位置和健康状态，并帮客户端或网关找到可用实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Service discovery records service instance locations and health so clients or gateways can find one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常见的协调服务，可用于服务注册、发现和配置管理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZooKeeper is a coordination service often used for registration, discovery, and configuration.

optionExplanations: 握手时多一次查询，换来连接均匀落在健康机器上；这张登记表本身要多副本，不能变成新的单点。
让客户端随机猜一个 IP，完全没有依据判断这台机器延迟高不高、容量够不够，很容易连到过载的服务器。
消息数据库负责存储消息数据，不负责返回 HTML 页面，也不承担挑选合适 chat server 这件事。
短信供应商是通知系统里的一个通道，跟聊天连接该分配到哪台服务器完全不相关。
optionExplanations_en: One extra lookup at handshake spreads connections across healthy servers; that registry itself needs replicas so it does not become a new single point.
Having the client randomly guess an IP gives no basis at all for judging that machine's latency or remaining capacity — it easily lands on an overloaded server.
The message database is responsible for storing message data, not returning HTML pages, and it plays no role in picking a suitable chat server either.
An SMS provider is a channel inside a notification system, entirely unrelated to which server a chat connection should be assigned to.

scenario: 聊天历史要永久保存；最近消息读得最多，但也要支持搜索、跳到某条消息等随机访问。
scenario_en: Chat history is stored forever; recent messages are read most, but search and jump-to-message require random access.
q: 消息历史适合哪类存储？
q_en: What storage fits message history?
options: KV / wide-column store
单机本地文件
只放在 Redis 内存里而且完全不落盘持久化
CDN 边缘缓存作为主库
options_en: A KV or wide-column store.
A single local file.
Only Redis in memory with no persistence at all
A CDN edge cache as the primary store.
why: 消息量巨大且按会话/消息 ID 访问，KV 或 wide-column 更容易横向扩展。关系库可存用户资料，但长尾历史索引会越来越重。
why_en: Chat messages are huge and accessed by conversation and message ID, so a scalable KV or wide-column store fits better.
tradeoff: 水平扩展低延迟 vs 复杂关系查询
whenOtherWins: 如果只是企业内小聊天且需要复杂事务，关系库也能先满足。

termDefinitions.meaning: Key-Value store，按 key 读写 value 的存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A KV store reads and writes values by key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按分区键组织多行数据的分布式存储，常用于大规模时间序列或消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A wide-column store organizes rows by partition keys and is often used for large message-like data.

optionExplanations: 消息量巨大、又要按会话或消息 ID 这类 key 做随机访问，KV 或宽列存储天生适合这种按 key 查询、水平扩展的场景，能撑住持续增长的历史数据。
单机本地文件既没有容错能力，也没法在多机之间共享和横向扩展，撑不住永久保存的海量聊天记录。
只放 Redis 且不落盘意味着进程一重启或崩溃，所有聊天历史就彻底丢了，跟“永久保存”这个要求直接冲突。
CDN 边缘缓存是为分发静态内容设计的加速层，不是能长期承载海量写入和随机访问的主存储。
optionExplanations_en: With a massive message volume accessed by keys like conversation or message ID, a KV or wide-column store is naturally suited to this key-based, horizontally scalable access pattern and can absorb ever-growing history.
A single machine's local files have neither fault tolerance nor the ability to be shared and scaled across multiple machines — nowhere near enough for permanently storing a huge chat history.
Keeping everything only in Redis with no persistence means a process restart or crash wipes out the entire chat history — directly conflicting with the "permanently stored" requirement.
CDN edge caching is an acceleration layer designed for static content distribution, not a primary store built to carry massive sustained writes and random access.

scenario: 聊天消息要能按发送顺序展示；created_at 可能相同，NoSQL 也不一定有全局自增。
scenario_en: Chat messages must be shown in send order; created_at may collide, and NoSQL may not provide global auto-increment.
q: message_id 要满足什么？
q_en: What must message_id provide?
options: 唯一且大体按时间递增
只要是随机字符串即可
必须由客户端自由填写
可以在同一会话内重复
options_en: Unique and roughly time-sortable.
A random string is enough.
Clients must choose it freely.
It may repeat within one conversation.
why: 排序靠 message_id 比靠时间戳更稳，至少要在会话内唯一且可排序。可以用 Snowflake，也可以用会话内本地序列。
why_en: Message IDs should be unique and time-sortable, at least within the conversation, to drive display order.
whenOtherWins: 如果只需要最终一致的无序评论流，随机 UUID 也可能够用。

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种 64-bit 分布式 ID 方案，通常包含时间、机器和序列字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Snowflake is a 64-bit distributed ID scheme usually combining time, machine, and sequence fields.

termDefinitions.meaning: Universally Unique Identifier，常用随机或半随机唯一标识。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A UUID is a Universally Unique Identifier, often random or semi-random.

tradeoff: 排序稳定性 vs ID 生成复杂度
optionExplanations: created_at 时间戳可能撞车，只有唯一且大体按时间递增的 message_id 才能在这种情况下仍然给出一个可靠的展示顺序。
只要求是随机字符串完全没有排序含义，随机字符串之间没有大小关系，没法用来决定消息先后展示的顺序。
让客户端自由填写 message_id，客户端完全可能填出重复或乱序的值，服务端没法保证这个字段真正可靠。
允许同一会话内重复，意味着两条不同的消息可能共用同一个 ID，排序和定位单条消息都会变得混乱。
optionExplanations_en: created_at timestamps can collide, so only a message_id that's both unique and roughly time-increasing can still deliver a reliable display order even when that happens.
Requiring only a random string carries no ordering meaning at all — random strings have no inherent size relationship usable for deciding which message displays first.
Letting the client freely fill in message_id leaves plenty of room for duplicate or out-of-order values, since the server can't guarantee this field is actually reliable.
Allowing repeats within the same conversation means two different messages could share the same ID, making both ordering and locating a specific message a mess.

scenario: User A 和 User B 分别连在不同 chat server；A 发一条消息给 B。
scenario_en: User A and User B are connected to different chat servers; A sends a message to B.
q: 1 对 1 消息链路顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the one-on-one message flow?
steps: 根据 B 在线状态分支：在线路由到 B 的 server，离线触发 push
A 的 chat server 获取 message_id
写入消息同步队列并持久化
B 在线时，B 的 server 通过 WebSocket 推给 B
B 上线后按游标从存储补拉缺口
why: 先编号和持久化，再根据在线状态走实时推送或离线通知。这样断线时消息还在存储里，可被重放。
why_en: Assign and persist the message first, then deliver over WebSocket if online or send a push notification if offline.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A[User A] --> S1[Chat server 1]
  S1 --> ID[ID generator]
  S1 --> Store[(Message store)]
  S1 --> Q[Sync queue]
  Q --> S2[Chat server 2]
  S2 --> B[User B]
  Q --> PN[Push if offline]

termDefinitions.meaning: App 不在前台时，由平台通知用户有新消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A push notification alerts the user about a new message when the app is not active.

scenario: 同一账号同时登录手机和电脑；每个设备读到的最新消息位置可能不同。
scenario_en: The same account is logged in on phone and laptop; each device may have a different latest-read message position.
q: 多设备同步靠什么状态？
q_en: What state supports multi-device sync?
options: 每设备保存 cur_max_message_id
让所有设备都共享服务端上的同一个内存指针变量
只给最近一次登录的设备发消息
按设备屏幕大小排序
options_en: Keep cur_max_message_id per device.
All devices share one server-side in-memory pointer variable
Send messages only to the most recently logged-in device.
Order by device screen size.
why: 每台设备都有自己的已读进度，所以游标要按设备保存。设备重连时只拉 message_id 大于本地游标的消息。
why_en: Store a cursor per device, then fetch only messages newer than that device's last synced ID.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品强制单设备在线，全局游标可以简化。

termDefinitions.meaning: 某设备已经同步到的最大消息 ID，用作增量拉取游标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: cur_max_message_id is the largest message ID a device has synced, used as an incremental cursor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分页或同步时记录当前位置的标记。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cursor marks the current position for pagination or synchronization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消息的唯一编号，可用来排序和做增量同步边界。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A message_id is a unique message identifier used for ordering and incremental sync.

tradeoff: 设备独立进度 vs 同步状态存储成本
optionExplanations: 每台设备保存自己的 cur_max_message_id，重连时只补拉更大的 message_id，既不漏也少重复。
共享内存指针会互相覆盖进度，服务重启还会丢状态。
只给最新设备发消息会让手机或电脑其中一端漏消息。
屏幕大小不是同步游标，不能表示设备读到了哪条消息。
optionExplanations_en: Each device keeps its own cur_max_message_id, so reconnect only pulls larger message IDs.
One shared memory pointer overwrites device progress and disappears on restart.
Sending only to the latest device makes the phone or laptop miss messages.
Screen size is not a sync cursor and says nothing about the last read message.

scenario: 群聊最多 100 人；希望每个接收者只查自己的 inbox 就能拿到新消息。
scenario_en: Group chat has at most 100 members; each recipient should fetch new messages from their own inbox.
q: 小群消息怎么分发？
q_en: How should small-group messages be distributed?
options: 复制引用到成员 inbox
只写给发送者自己
每次读全群历史并客户端过滤
把群消息发成 SMS
options_en: Copy references into member inboxes.
Write only to the sender.
Read full group history and filter on the client every time.
Send group messages as SMS.
why: 100 人以内复制引用成本可控，换来每个客户端只读自己的队列。大群会把写放大到不可接受。
why_en: For groups capped at 100, per-recipient inbox copies keep reads simple with acceptable write amplification.
tradeoff: 读同步简单 vs 写入放大
whenOtherWins: 如果群有十万成员，应按频道存一份，用户进入时按 channel 拉取。

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向某个接收者的消息收件箱，用来同步新消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A message sync queue is a recipient-specific inbox for synchronizing new messages.

optionExplanations: 100 人以内的规模下，把消息引用复制进每个成员各自的 inbox 成本还可控，换来的是每个客户端只需要查自己的队列就能拿到新消息，不用去理解整个群的结构。
只写给发送者自己完全没有把消息分发给其他成员，群里的其他人根本收不到这条消息。
每次读全群历史再靠客户端过滤，会让每个客户端都要处理远超自己实际需要的数据量，效率很差。
把群消息发成 SMS 混淆了聊天系统内部的消息分发机制和外部通知通道，是完全不同的两回事。
optionExplanations_en: At a scale under 100 people, copying a message reference into each member's own inbox stays affordable, and in exchange each client only needs to check its own queue to get new messages, without needing to understand the group's structure at all.
Writing only to the sender's own inbox never distributes the message to any other member — nobody else in the group receives it at all.
Reading the entire group's history and filtering client-side forces every client to process far more data than it actually needs — very inefficient.
Sending group messages as SMS conflates a chat system's internal message-distribution mechanism with an entirely different external notification channel.

scenario: 移动网络会短暂断开又恢复；如果每次断开立刻标离线，好友会看到状态频繁闪烁。
scenario_en: Mobile networks may briefly disconnect and reconnect; marking offline immediately would make presence flicker.
q: 在线状态怎么判定更稳？
q_en: How should online status be judged more stably?
options: heartbeat 超时后再置离线
断开事件一到就立刻把用户永久置为离线
只看用户头像是否加载
每秒给所有好友发短信
options_en: Mark offline after heartbeat timeout.
Immediately mark permanently offline on disconnect
Check whether the avatar loads.
Text all friends every second.
why: heartbeat 给短暂网络抖动一个缓冲窗口。代价是离线显示会慢一点，并且 presence server 要处理心跳流量。
why_en: Heartbeats smooth over brief network drops by delaying offline status until the timeout expires.
tradeoff: 状态稳定性 vs 离线检测延迟
whenOtherWins: 如果是交易连接，断线可能要立刻撤销会话，而不是等 presence 超时。

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端周期性发送的小事件，用来证明连接仍然活着。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heartbeat is a small periodic event proving the client is still alive.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户在线、离线或最近活跃状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Presence is a user's online, offline, or last-active state.

optionExplanations: 给短暂断开留出一个心跳超时的缓冲窗口，等确认真的连不上了再标离线，就不会让一次网络抖动变成好友眼前反复闪烁的状态。
断开事件一来就立即永久离线，会把移动网络常见的短暂抖动直接放大成频繁的状态闪烁，体验很差。
只看用户头像是否加载完全反映不出这个人现在到底在不在线，头像加载和在线状态是两回事。
每秒给所有好友发短信来同步状态，成本极高也完全不现实，短信不是用来做高频状态同步的通道。
optionExplanations_en: Giving a brief disconnect a heartbeat-timeout buffer before actually marking someone offline keeps a momentary network blip from turning into the status flickering repeatedly in front of friends.
Marking someone permanently offline the instant a disconnect event arrives amplifies the common brief mobile-network blip straight into frequent status flickering — a poor experience.
Looking only at whether a user's avatar has loaded says nothing about whether that person is actually online right now — avatar loading and online status are unrelated.
Sending every friend a text message every second to sync status is prohibitively expensive and unrealistic — SMS isn't a channel meant for high-frequency status sync.

scenario: 好友列表规模较小；User A 上下线时，B/C/D 都希望实时看到绿点变化。
scenario_en: Friend lists are small; when User A goes online or offline, B/C/D want real-time green-dot updates.
q: presence 变化怎么推？
q_en: How should presence changes be pushed?
options: Pub/Sub 按好友关系频道发布状态变化
每个客户端每分钟全量扫库
把状态写进消息正文
只靠 push notification
options_en: Publish status changes through Pub/Sub channels per friend relationship.
Have every client scan the database every minute.
Write status into message bodies.
Use only push notifications.
why: 小关系网里 Pub/Sub 能把变化实时送到订阅者。代价是好友数很大时事件数会爆炸。
why_en: Pub/Sub works well for small friend sets because subscribers receive status changes in real time.
tradeoff: 实时状态推送 vs 事件扇出成本
whenOtherWins: 如果群有十万成员，进入页面时按需拉在线状态更省。

termDefinitions.meaning: Publish/Subscribe，发布者发事件，订阅者按频道接收。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/Sub means Publish/Subscribe: publishers send events and subscribers receive them by channel.

optionExplanations: 好友圈子不大的情况下，按好友关系开一个 Pub/Sub 频道，A 一上下线就能把这次状态变化实时送到 B、C、D 这些订阅者手上。
让每个客户端每分钟自己去全量扫库查所有好友的状态，既有明显延迟又给数据库带来不必要的周期性压力。
把状态直接写进消息正文，混淆了聊天消息内容和用户在线状态这两种完全不同性质的数据。
只靠 push notification 来通知在线状态变化，会让绿点变化变成一次次系统通知，既不实时也很打扰。
optionExplanations_en: With a small enough friend circle, opening a Pub/Sub channel keyed to the friend relationship lets A going online or offline get pushed to B, C, and D as subscribers in real time.
Having every client scan the database for all its friends' status once a minute has obvious lag and puts unnecessary periodic pressure on the database.
Writing the status directly into a message's body conflates two completely different kinds of data: chat content and online presence.
Relying only on push notifications for presence changes turns every green-dot flicker into a system notification — neither timely nor pleasant.

scenario: 一个群有 100000 人；任意成员上下线都广播给全群，会产生 100000 条状态事件。
scenario_en: A group has 100,000 members; broadcasting every presence change to the whole group creates 100,000 status events.
q: 大群 presence 怎么降成本？
q_en: How do you reduce large-group presence cost?
options: 用户进入群或刷新列表时按需拉在线状态
继续对每次变化全量 fanout
禁用 WebSocket 连接
把所有人永久标在线
options_en: Fetch online status on demand when a user enters the group or refreshes.
Keep full fanout for every change.
Disable WebSocket connections.
Mark everyone online forever.
why: 大群里实时全量推送的事件数太大，按需拉取把成本转到真正查看列表的时候。代价是状态不是毫秒级实时。
why_en: For huge groups, fetch presence on demand because broadcasting every change is too expensive.
whenOtherWins: 小群或核心好友列表仍适合实时 Pub/Sub。

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个事件复制并发送给多个接收者的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fanout is copying and sending one event to many recipients.

optionExplanations: 十万人的规模下，只在用户真正打开群或刷新列表时才去拉一次在线状态，能把成本转移到真正需要看这份数据的那一刻，而不是每次变化都广播给所有人。
继续对每次上下线都做全量 fanout，会让一次状态变化产生十万条事件，这正是这个场景下要避免的爆炸式成本。
禁用 WebSocket 连接会连消息本身的实时收发都一起丢掉，是完全不成比例的过度反应。
把所有人永久标在线跟真实状态完全脱节，用户看到的会是一份完全不准确的在线信息。
optionExplanations_en: At a scale of 100,000, pulling online status only when a user actually opens the group or refreshes the list shifts the cost to the moment it's actually needed, instead of broadcasting to everyone on every single change.
Continuing to fully fan out every online/offline change generates 100,000 events per change — exactly the kind of exploding cost this scenario needs to avoid.
Disabling WebSocket connections would also throw out real-time message delivery itself, a wildly disproportionate overreaction.
Marking everyone permanently online completely disconnects from reality, leaving users looking at entirely inaccurate presence information.

scenario: 粗估 100 万并发连接，每条连接在服务器上占 10 KB 内存；这只是量级判断。
scenario_en: Roughly estimate 1 million concurrent connections, with each connection using 10 KB of server memory; this is an order-of-magnitude check.
q: 这个估算告诉你什么？
q_en: What does this estimate tell you?
text: 连接内存约 {{1,000,000 * 10 KB = 10 GB}}；单机也许装得下内存，但不能因此做单点设计。
text_en: Connection memory is about {{1,000,000 * 10 KB = 10 GB}}; one machine may fit the memory, but it would still be a single point of failure.
why: 这个数字说明内存不是唯一瓶颈，连接数、故障域和发布维护同样重要。面试里要从单机起步，但马上拆成多台 chat server。
why_en: The estimate shows memory alone is not the whole problem; connection count and failure domains still force multiple chat servers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一时刻保持打开的网络连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A concurrent connection is a network connection kept open at the same time as others.

termDefinitions.meaning: Single Point of Failure，单点故障；一个组件挂掉会拖垮整条能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SPOF means Single Point of Failure, where one failed component breaks the whole capability.

scenario: 群聊读取通常按 channel_id 拉某个群的最近消息；消息 ID 用来在群内排序。
scenario_en: Group chat reads usually fetch recent messages by channel_id; message ID orders messages within the group.
q: 群消息表主键怎么选？
q_en: How should the group message primary key be shaped?
options: channel_id + message_id
只用 created_at 时间戳来做主键
只用发送者昵称
随机按文本长度分区
options_en: channel_id plus message_id.
Use only the created_at timestamp
Use only the sender nickname.
Partition randomly by text length.
why: 查询总是围绕某个群，所以 channel_id 应把同群消息放一起；message_id 再保证群内顺序。代价是超大热群需要进一步分片。
why_en: Group reads are by channel, so partition by channel_id and order within it by message_id.
whenOtherWins: 如果群特别大且单 channel 分区过热，可以按时间桶或子分区拆开。

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定数据落到哪个分区的 key，也决定常见查询是否高效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A partition key decides where data is stored and whether common queries are efficient.

termDefinitions.meaning: 群聊或频道的唯一标识。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A channel_id uniquely identifies a group chat or channel.

tradeoff: 按群顺序读取 vs 跨群全局排序
optionExplanations: 查询几乎总是围绕某个群展开，channel_id 把同一个群的消息聚在一起保证读取局部性，message_id 再负责群内的先后顺序，两者合起来正好匹配这种查询模式。
只用 created_at 既可能因为并发写入产生冲突，也没法表达“这条消息属于哪个群”这个查询最需要的边界。
只用发送者昵称既不能唯一定位一条消息，也完全不能表达消息该属于哪个会话，昵称跟会话边界毫无关系。
按消息长度随机分区会让同一个群的消息散落到不同分片里，每次读群消息都要跨多个分片聚合，完全违背查询局部性。
optionExplanations_en: Queries almost always revolve around a specific group, so channel_id keeps that group's messages together for read locality, while message_id handles the within-group ordering — together they match exactly this access pattern.
Using only created_at risks collisions under concurrent writes, and it also can't express which group a message belongs to, the exact boundary this query needs most.
Using only the sender's nickname can neither uniquely locate a single message nor express which conversation it belongs to — a nickname has nothing to do with conversation boundaries.
Randomly partitioning by message length scatters one group's messages across different shards, forcing every group read to aggregate across shards — completely defeating query locality.

scenario: 聊天 App 除实时消息外，还有登录、注册、用户资料、设置修改等普通请求。
scenario_en: Besides real-time messages, the chat app has login, signup, profile, and settings requests.
q: 这些普通功能用什么协议更合适？
q_en: What protocol is better for these regular features?
options: HTTP request/response
把登录注册资料更新也强行全部走 WebSocket
短信协议
数据库复制协议
options_en: Use HTTP request/response.
Force everything through WebSocket
SMS protocol.
Database replication protocol.
why: 登录、注册、资料更新是一次请求一次响应，不需要为每个用户占长连接。HTTP 更容易做无状态负载均衡；WebSocket 留给实时消息和 presence。
why_en: Use HTTP for one-shot CRUD requests and keep WebSocket for real-time messaging and presence.
tradeoff: 简单无状态请求 vs 实时双向连接
whenOtherWins: 如果客户端已经有稳定 WebSocket，也可复用它发少量控制消息，但主 API 不必强依赖。

termDefinitions.meaning: Create, Read, Update, Delete，常见资料类增删改查操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CRUD means Create, Read, Update, Delete.

termDefinitions.meaning: Hypertext Transfer Protocol，Web 常用请求/响应协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the common request-response protocol of the web.

termDefinitions.meaning: 浏览器或 App 与服务端保持的一条双向长连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WebSocket is a long-lived bidirectional connection between a client and a server.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户是否在线、正在输入或可接收实时消息的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Presence is state such as whether a user is online, typing, or reachable in real time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 手机运营商短信通道，常用于离线通知或验证码。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SMS is the carrier text-message channel often used for offline alerts or verification codes.

optionExplanations: 登录、注册、改资料是一次性请求，HTTP 方便无状态负载均衡，把长连接留给实时消息。
强行走 WebSocket 会让简单请求背上连接保持、断线重连和路由状态成本。
SMS 是外部通知通道，适合提醒或验证码，不适合承载 App 内部 API。
数据库复制协议只在数据库节点之间同步数据，客户端业务请求不会走它。
optionExplanations_en: Login, signup, and profile edits are one-shot requests, so HTTP keeps load balancing stateless.
Forcing WebSocket adds connection, reconnect, and routing-state cost to simple requests.
SMS is an external notification channel, useful for alerts or codes, not internal app APIs.
Database replication syncs database nodes; client business requests do not use it.

scenario: 接收者离线时没有 WebSocket 连接；但她重新上线后必须看到历史消息。
scenario_en: The recipient is offline and has no WebSocket connection, but must see history after coming back online.
q: 离线消息怎么处理？
q_en: How should offline messages be handled?
options: 先持久化消息，离线时发 push，上线后从存储同步
直接丢弃并只发绿点变化
只存在发送者手机里
等接收者真正在线之后才生成 message_id
options_en: Persist the message, send push while offline, and sync from storage when back online.
Drop it and only send presence changes.
Keep it only on the sender's phone.
Generate message_id only after the recipient is online
why: 聊天的可靠性来自服务器持久化，不来自接收者当前在线。push 只是提醒，真正补消息靠上线后的同步。
why_en: Persisted storage is the source of truth; push is only an alert, and online sync retrieves the actual messages.
whenOtherWins: 如果是阅后即焚且产品允许离线丢弃，才会改变持久化策略。

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统里被认为最权威、可恢复真实状态的数据源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The source of truth is the authoritative data store for recovering real state.

optionExplanations: 先把消息真正持久化保存下来，接收者离线时用 push 提醒一下，等她重新上线，服务端再从存储把这段时间的消息同步过去，可靠性靠的是持久化而不是当时有没有在线。
直接丢弃消息只发绿点变化，等于把真正的内容全部扔掉，接收者上线后压根看不到之前发生的对话。
只存在发送者手机里意味着一旦发送者的设备出问题，这条消息就彻底没了，接收方压根就没有一份服务端保存的记录可以同步。
等接收者在线才生成 message_id，会让发送者这边已经确认发出去的消息在服务端一直没有正式落定，逻辑完全反了。
optionExplanations_en: Persisting the message first, sending a push nudge while the receiver is offline, and then syncing everything from storage once they come back online means reliability comes from persistence, not from whoever happened to be online at the time.
Simply discarding the message and sending only a status update throws away the actual content entirely — the receiver comes back online to find no trace of what happened.
Storing it only on the sender's phone means the message is gone entirely if that device has any issue, leaving the receiver with no server-side record to sync from at all.
Waiting until the receiver comes online to generate the message_id leaves what the sender already believes was successfully sent never formally settled server-side — the logic here is backwards.

scenario: 某台 chat server 掉线，上面有大量 WebSocket 连接；消息存储和 service discovery 仍可用。
scenario_en: A chat server goes down with many WebSocket connections; message storage and service discovery remain available.
q: 客户端恢复路径是什么？
q_en: What is the recovery path?
options: 重连新 server，再按 cursor 补拉
干等原来那台机器被人工手动修好，不允许重连
清空所有历史消息
把用户永久标离线
options_en: Reconnect to a new server, then sync by cursor.
Wait for the original machine to be fixed by hand, with no reconnect
Clear all message history.
Mark users offline forever.
why: 长连接会断，但消息已持久化，重连后可以补拉。代价是客户端要实现重连退避和重复消息去重。
why_en: When a chat server fails, clients reconnect elsewhere and use message cursors to fill any delivery gap.
whenOtherWins: 如果消息没有持久化，重连也无法恢复缺口，所以存储必须先设计好。

termDefinitions.meaning: 重连失败时逐步拉长等待时间，避免所有客户端同时打爆服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Reconnect backoff gradually increases retry delay so clients do not overload servers.

optionExplanations: 消息本来就已经持久化在存储里，客户端重连到一台新的 server 后，按自己上次同步到的 cursor 继续往下拉，就能补齐这段断线期间错过的消息。
要求客户端等原来那台机器手动修好才能重连，完全没必要，反而把本可以立刻恢复的服务变成了长时间不可用。
清空所有历史消息是极端且毫无必要的做法，一台机器掉线跟整个聊天历史该不该保留没有任何关系。
把用户永久标离线跟这台机器只是掉线、消息和发现服务仍然可用这个前提矛盾，用户完全应该能重连回来。
optionExplanations_en: The messages are already persisted in storage, so once the client reconnects to a new server, continuing to pull from wherever its own last-synced cursor left off fills in exactly what was missed during the outage.
Requiring the client to wait for that original machine to be manually fixed before reconnecting is completely unnecessary, turning what could be an instant recovery into extended downtime.
Wiping out the entire chat history is an extreme and needless overreaction — one machine going offline has nothing to do with whether history should be kept.

Marking the user permanently offline contradicts the premise that only this one machine went down while message storage and service discovery are still working fine — the user should absolutely be able to reconnect.

scenario: 核心文本聊天已经能跑；面试最后还有时间，可以补充扩展话题。
scenario_en: The core text chat works; near the end of the interview, you can add extension topics.
q: 哪些是合理的后续扩展？
q_en: Which are reasonable follow-up extensions?
options: 媒体文件：对象存储、压缩和缩略图
端到端加密：密钥管理和设备同步
客户端缓存：减少历史消息重复传输
把所有消息改成公开网页让 crawler 抓
options_en: Media files: object storage, compression, and thumbnails.
End-to-end encryption: key management and device sync.
Client caching: reduce repeated history transfer.
Turn all messages into public web pages for crawlers.
why: 这些扩展都围绕聊天的真实瓶颈：大文件、隐私和加载速度。公开给 crawler 抓违背私密聊天的基本边界。
why_en: Good extensions address real chat concerns: large media, privacy, and load time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 端到端加密让只有发送者和接收者设备能读明文，服务器看不到内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: End-to-end encryption means only sender and recipient devices can read plaintext.

optionExplanations: 对，媒体文件涉及大对象存储、压缩和缩略图生成，是聊天系统很自然会遇到的真实瓶颈之一。
对，端到端加密涉及密钥管理和多设备同步，是隐私要求更高的聊天场景常见的合理扩展。
对，客户端缓存能减少重复拉取历史消息，直接改善加载速度，是很实际的优化方向。
私密聊天的基本前提就是内容只在参与者之间可见，把消息内容公开成网页让爬虫抓取，直接违反了这个最基本的隐私边界。
optionExplanations_en: Right — media files bring large-object storage, compression, and thumbnail generation, a real bottleneck a chat system naturally runs into.
Right — end-to-end encryption brings key management and multi-device sync, a reasonable extension for chat scenarios with higher privacy requirements.
Right — client-side caching cuts down on re-fetching history and directly improves load speed, a very practical optimization direction.

The basic premise of private chat is that content stays visible only to the participants — turning messages into a public webpage for crawlers to index directly violates that most basic privacy boundary.

scenario: 企业代理环境偶尔挡住 WebSocket；产品仍希望聊天可用，只是体验可以降级。
scenario_en: Some enterprise proxies block WebSocket; the product still wants chat to work, with degraded experience.
q: 降级方案怎么说？
q_en: How should the fallback be described?
options: 长连接主，长轮询备
永远只用短轮询
失败后改成邮件聊天
关闭接收消息
options_en: Persistent connection primary, long polling backup.
Always use short polling only.
Switch to email chat after failure.
Disable receiving messages.
why: WebSocket 更适合实时双向，但降级能提高可用性。long polling 成本更高，所以不应是首选主路径。
why_en: Use WebSocket for the normal real-time path and long polling as a compatibility fallback.
whenOtherWins: 如果目标环境完全不支持长连接，短轮询可能是最后兜底。

termDefinitions.meaning: 主方案不可用时切换到备用方案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fallback is switching to a backup path when the primary path is unavailable.

tradeoff: 实时体验 vs 兼容性降级成本
optionExplanations: 平时用长连接享受实时双向的体验，遇到代理挡住 WebSocket 的环境就自动切到长轮询，这样既保住了大多数场景的体验，又给受限环境留了一条能用的路。
永远只用短轮询会让绝大多数正常网络环境下的用户白白承受本可以避免的延迟和大量无效请求。
失败后改成邮件聊天，延迟是以天甚至小时计的，跟聊天场景要求的实时性完全对不上，等于放弃了聊天体验。
关闭接收消息意味着代理受限的用户直接完全用不了聊天功能，跟“产品仍希望聊天可用”这个目标正相反。
optionExplanations_en: Using a long connection by default for the real-time bidirectional experience, and automatically falling back to long polling in environments where a proxy blocks WebSocket, keeps most scenarios' experience intact while still giving restricted environments a working path.
Using only short polling forever makes the vast majority of users on normal networks needlessly suffer avoidable latency and a mountain of wasted requests.
Falling back to email chat has latency measured in hours or days, nowhere near the real-time requirement chat needs — effectively abandoning the chat experience entirely.
Turning off message receiving entirely leaves proxy-restricted users completely unable to use chat at all, the opposite of the goal that chat should still be usable.

scenario: chat server 上维护 user_id 到 connection_id 的映射；发送消息时要找到接收者在哪台机器。
scenario_en: A chat server maintains user_id to connection_id mappings; message delivery must locate the recipient machine.
q: 这份状态应该怎么管理？
q_en: How should this state be managed?
options: server 持连接并登记路由
把这份连接状态只保存在客户端本地
写进每条消息正文
完全不维护
options_en: Server holds connections and registers routing.
Keep it only on the client
Write it into every message body.
Do not maintain it.
why: 连接对象只能由持有 socket 的 server 直接写；全局路由只需要知道用户在哪。服务挂掉后登记要过期或被清理。
why_en: Only the server holding the socket can write to it, while routing needs to know where that user is connected.
whenOtherWins: 如果所有用户都离线，路由状态不需要存在，消息只写存储和 push。

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器内部标识某条长连接的 ID。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A connection_id identifies a live connection inside a server.

tradeoff: 连接本地写入能力 vs 全局路由登记成本
optionExplanations: 只有真正握着这条 socket 的那台服务器才能直接写连接对象，所以由持有连接的 server 自己维护并登记路由信息，其他服务再通过这份登记去找到用户在哪。
只存在客户端本地意味着服务端完全不知道这个用户当前连在哪台机器上，发消息时根本没法找到接收者所在的 server。
写进每条消息正文会让路由信息和消息内容混在一起，既冗余又没有必要，路由该是独立维护的元数据。
完全不维护路由信息，发消息时就没有办法知道该往哪台机器投递，这条消息根本送不到接收者手上。
optionExplanations_en: Only the server that actually holds the socket can directly write to that connection object, so the server holding it maintains and registers the routing entry itself, and other services look it up through that registry to find where the user is.
Keeping it only on the client means the server has no idea which machine this user is currently connected to, with no way to locate the recipient's server when sending a message.
Writing it into every message's body mixes routing information with message content unnecessarily — routing should be independently maintained metadata.
Maintaining no routing information at all leaves no way to know which machine to deliver to when sending a message — it simply can't reach the recipient.

scenario: 一对一聊天按 conversation 读取最近消息；双方都要看到同一条有序历史。
scenario_en: One-on-one chat reads recent messages by conversation; both users should see the same ordered history.
q: 1 对 1 消息表怎么建 key？
q_en: How should the one-on-one message table be keyed?
options: 会话ID + 消息ID
只按发送者姓名分区
只按 created_at 做唯一主键
按消息长度分区
options_en: Conversation ID plus message ID.
Partition only by sender name.
Use created_at alone as the unique primary key.
Partition by message length.
why: 查询边界是会话，排序边界是 message_id。created_at 可能冲突，发送者姓名也不能表示会话。
why_en: Conversation reads should partition by conversation and order by message ID.
whenOtherWins: 如果存储模型是每个用户 inbox 副本，也仍要保留会话和排序字段。

termDefinitions.meaning: 一段一对一或群聊会话的唯一标识。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A conversation_id uniquely identifies a one-on-one or group conversation.

tradeoff: 会话查询局部性 vs 跨会话查询灵活性
optionExplanations: 查询边界是一段会话，排序边界是消息，用会话 ID 加消息 ID 做联合 key，正好让双方都能按同一份有序历史读到一致的内容。
只按发送者姓名分区完全没有表达“这是哪一段对话”，同一个人可能同时参与很多段不同的会话。
只按 created_at 做唯一主键，时间戳可能冲突，也没法回答“这条消息属于哪段会话”这个查询最先要问的问题。
按消息长度分区跟这条消息属于哪段会话、该排在第几条完全不相关，是一个无意义的分区维度。
optionExplanations_en: The query boundary is a conversation and the ordering boundary is a message, so a composite key of conversation ID plus message ID is exactly what lets both sides read the same ordered history consistently.
Partitioning only by sender name says nothing about which conversation this is — the same person can be part of many different conversations at once.
Using only created_at as the unique primary key risks timestamp collisions, and it also can't answer which conversation a message belongs to, the very first question this query needs answered.
Partitioning by message length has nothing to do with which conversation a message belongs to or where it should sort — a meaningless partitioning dimension here.

scenario: 群内只要求同一个 channel 的消息有序，不要求全平台所有消息共享一个序列。
scenario_en: Messages only need ordering within the same channel, not one sequence across the whole platform.
q: 本地序列号为什么可行？
q_en: Why can local sequence numbers work?
options: channel 内有序即可
所有数据库都只能全局自增
本地序列天然跨群唯一
客户端不需要排序
options_en: Ordering only needs to hold inside a channel.
Every database only supports global auto-increment.
Local sequences are naturally unique across groups.
Clients do not need ordering.
why: 聊天展示按会话看，局部有序就够。局部序列比全局 ID 服务简单，但跨会话比较时间要另有字段。
why_en: Chat display is scoped to a conversation, so local ordering can be enough and simpler than global IDs.
whenOtherWins: 如果需要全局审计流或跨会话严格排序，Snowflake 这类全局 ID 更合适。

termDefinitions.meaning: 只在某个会话或分区内递增的序列号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A local sequence increments only within one conversation or partition.

tradeoff: 局部有序简单性 vs 全局排序能力
optionExplanations: 需求只是同一个 channel 内的消息要有序，不要求跨群共享一个全局序列，那么在群内本地维护一个递增序列号就已经足够满足这个要求，也比维护全局唯一 ID 服务简单得多。
不是所有数据库都只能靠全局自增来生成 ID，很多场景本来就用局部或分布式的方式生成序列号。
本地序列号只在它所属的这个 channel 内有意义，跨群比较时序号完全可能重复，不能说它天然跨群唯一。
客户端展示消息时仍然需要按顺序呈现，说客户端不需要排序不符合聊天界面的基本需求。
optionExplanations_en: The requirement is only that messages within one channel stay ordered, not that every group share one global sequence, so a locally maintained incrementing counter within the group is already enough, and much simpler than running a global unique-ID service.
Not every database can only generate IDs through global auto-increment — plenty of scenarios generate sequence numbers locally or in a distributed way instead.
A local sequence number only means something within its own channel — the same number can easily repeat across different groups, so it isn't naturally unique across groups.
A client still needs to display messages in order, so claiming the client doesn't need sorting doesn't match a chat UI's basic requirement.

scenario: 用户手机读完消息，电脑稍后打开；产品希望两个设备都能显示正确未读数。
scenario_en: A user reads messages on the phone, then opens the laptop; the product wants correct unread counts on both devices.
q: ACK 状态应该怎么建模？
q_en: How should ACK state be modeled?
options: 服务端保存 read cursor
只存在手机内存
把每次 ACK 直接写进消息的正文文本里
不记录已读位置
options_en: Store read cursors on the server.
Keep it only in phone memory.
Write ACKs into message text
Do not record read position.
why: 未读数来自服务端知道用户读到哪。设备级 cursor 支持每台设备独立进度，用户级 cursor 支持跨设备统一已读。
why_en: Unread counts require server-side read cursors, either per device or unified per user depending on product semantics.
tradeoff: 设备独立进度 vs 跨设备统一已读
whenOtherWins: 如果产品明确每台设备独立未读，就按 device_id 保存 cursor。

termDefinitions.meaning: Acknowledgement，客户端确认已收到或已读某条消息的信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ACK means Acknowledgement, a signal that a client received or read a message.

termDefinitions.meaning: 表示用户或设备已经读到哪条消息的位置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read cursor marks the latest message a user or device has read.

optionExplanations: 服务端保存每台设备各自的已读位置，手机读完更新自己的 cursor，电脑打开时读到这个更新过的 cursor，就能算出跨设备统一的未读数。
只存在手机内存意味着这份进度对电脑端完全不可见，电脑没法知道手机已经读到哪了，算不出正确的未读数。
把 ACK 写进消息文本混淆了消息内容和已读状态这两种完全不同的数据，也没法支撑跨设备的已读同步。
不记录已读位置，系统压根不知道用户读到哪了，两个设备的未读数都无从算起。
optionExplanations_en: The server saves each device's own read position — the phone finishing reading updates its own cursor, and the desktop opening later reads that updated cursor, letting it compute an accurate unread count consistent across devices.
Keeping it only in the phone's memory makes that progress completely invisible to the desktop, which has no way to know how far the phone has read and can't compute the correct unread count.
Writing the ACK into the message text conflates message content with read state, two entirely different kinds of data, and can't support cross-device read sync either.
Not recording the read position at all leaves the system with no idea where the user left off, so neither device's unread count can be computed.

scenario: 用户有很多会话；首页要显示每个会话的未读数，不能每次都扫描所有消息。
scenario_en: A user has many conversations; the inbox must show unread counts per conversation without scanning all messages each time.
q: 未读数怎么维护？
q_en: How should unread counts be maintained?
options: 用 read cursor 或计数缓存
每次都对全表 count 一遍未读消息
让客户端猜一个数字
把未读数写进用户名
options_en: Use read cursors or cached counts.
Count unread messages from the full table every time
Let the client guess a number.
Write unread count into the username.
why: 未读数是高频派生数据，应该用 cursor 或计数缓存快速算。全表扫描会随历史增长变慢。
why_en: Unread counts should come from cursors or cached counters, not full history scans.
whenOtherWins: 如果会话极少且历史很短，实时 count 可以先满足。

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户在某会话中最后读到的消息 ID。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: last_read_message_id is the latest message ID a user has read in a conversation.

optionExplanations: 用 read cursor 或者一个专门维护的计数缓存，能把未读数变成一次快速查询，而不用每次都重新扫一遍消息。
每次都对全表做一次 count 未读消息，随着历史消息越积越多，这个查询会越来越慢，扛不住首页高频展示的需求。
让客户端自己猜一个数字完全没有依据，客户端并不掌握服务端权威的消息已读状态。
把未读数写进用户名把两种完全不相关的数据混在一起，既没有意义也没法正常更新。
optionExplanations_en: A read cursor or a dedicated counter cache turns fetching the unread count into a fast lookup, instead of rescanning messages every single time.
Running a full-table count of unread messages every time gets slower and slower as history piles up, unable to survive a homepage that displays this frequently.
Having the client guess a number has nothing to base itself on — the client doesn't hold the server's authoritative read state.
Writing the unread count into the username mashes two entirely unrelated pieces of data together — pointless and impossible to update normally.

scenario: 接收者离线；消息已经写入存储，但没有实时连接可以推送。
scenario_en: The recipient is offline; the message is stored, but there is no live connection for real-time delivery.
q: push notification 应该承载什么？
q_en: What should the push notification carry?
options: 轻量提醒和会话 ID，不作为消息唯一存储
把五年内的完整聊天历史全部内容都塞进去
服务端数据库密码
所有群成员在线状态
options_en: A lightweight alert and conversation ID, not the only copy of the message.
The complete five-year chat history
The server database password.
Every group member’s presence state.
why: push 是提醒通道，可能被系统折叠或用户关闭；真正消息必须在服务端存储里。payload 也要避免泄露过多内容。
why_en: Push is an alert path, not the source of truth for chat messages.
whenOtherWins: 如果用户开启隐私预览，可以在 push 中放少量摘要，但仍不能替代存储。

termDefinitions.meaning: 推送通知携带的数据内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Payload is the data carried by a push notification.

tradeoff: 提醒可达性 vs 消息隐私和权威存储
optionExplanations: push 只是一个轻量提醒，附带会话 ID 让用户点开对应会话，真正的消息内容还是要从服务端存储里拿，因为 push 通道可能被系统折叠或用户直接关闭。
把五年完整聊天历史塞进一条 push，既不现实也完全违背了 push 只是提醒的定位，push 通道从来不是用来承载完整历史的。
服务端数据库密码属于绝密凭证，绝不应该出现在任何面向终端用户的 push payload 里。
把所有群成员的在线状态塞进一条离线消息提醒，跟这条提醒本身要传达的内容毫无关系，也偏离了 push 该承载的信息。
optionExplanations_en: A push is just a lightweight nudge carrying the conversation ID so the user can tap into it, while the actual message content still has to come from server storage, since the push channel itself can be collapsed by the OS or turned off by the user.
Cramming five years of full chat history into a single push is neither realistic nor consistent with what a push is meant to be — the push channel was never built to carry entire histories.
A server database password is a highly sensitive credential that should never appear in any user-facing push payload.

Stuffing every group member's online status into one offline-message notification has nothing to do with what that notification is actually meant to convey, and strays far from what a push should carry.

scenario: presence server 要记录 online/offline 和 last_active_at；读写很频繁，状态可短暂丢失后重建。
scenario_en: Presence servers record online/offline and last_active_at; reads and writes are frequent, and state can be rebuilt after brief loss.
q: presence 状态适合哪里？
q_en: Where does presence state fit?
options: 低延迟 KV + TTL
长期冷对象存储
只写入消息正文
每次从关系库复杂 join
options_en: Use low-latency KV plus TTL.
Long-term cold object storage.
Only message bodies.
Complex relational joins every time.
why: presence 是热状态，不是永久历史。KV 加 TTL 能让断开的连接自动过期，读写也快。
why_en: Presence is hot ephemeral state, so KV with TTL fits frequent updates and automatic expiry.
whenOtherWins: 审计最后在线时间可以异步落持久库，但在线判断不该依赖慢查询。

termDefinitions.meaning: Time To Live，记录在过期前有效的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is the time a record remains valid before expiring.

tradeoff: 热状态低延迟 vs 持久历史能力
optionExplanations: presence 是一份会频繁读写、也能承受短暂丢失后重建的热状态，低延迟 KV 配合 TTL 让断开的连接自动过期，读写速度也能跟上这种高频场景。
presence 不是永久历史，把它放进为长期冷数据设计的对象存储，会让本该毫秒级响应的在线判断变得又贵又慢。
presence 是需要频繁更新的独立状态，把它写进消息正文既没有正常更新的入口，也会污染消息内容本身。
presence 变化频率极高，每次都走关系库的复杂 join 查询，延迟和数据库压力都会远超这个场景能承受的范围。
optionExplanations_en: Presence is hot state that's read and written frequently and can tolerate being briefly lost and rebuilt, so a low-latency KV store with TTL lets disconnected sessions lapse automatically while still keeping up with this high-frequency traffic.
Presence isn't permanent history — putting it in object storage designed for long-term cold data would make what should be a millisecond-level online check both expensive and slow.
Presence is independent state that updates constantly; writing it into message bodies gives it no normal update path and pollutes the actual message content.
Presence changes extremely often, so running a complex relational join on every check would push latency and database load far beyond what this scenario can tolerate.

scenario: 客户端每 5 秒发一次 heartbeat，服务端 30 秒没收到才判离线。
scenario_en: The client sends a heartbeat every 5 seconds, and the server marks offline after 30 seconds without one.
q: 这个数字约束什么？
q_en: What does this number constrain?
options: 每连接心跳写入量和离线检测延迟
限制单条消息正文所能达到的最大长度
群成员上限
存储保留年限
options_en: Heartbeat write volume and offline detection delay per connection.
The maximum body length of a single message
Group member limit.
Storage retention years.
why: 5 秒间隔决定 presence 写 QPS，30 秒阈值决定绿点最多晚多久变灰。这是体验和服务器压力的折中。
why_en: The heartbeat interval drives presence write QPS, while the timeout bounds offline detection delay.
whenOtherWins: 如果连接资源很贵，可以拉长间隔；如果状态必须更实时，可以缩短但要扩 presence 层。

termDefinitions.meaning: 相邻两次心跳之间的时间间隔。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Heartbeat interval is the time between two heartbeat events.

optionExplanations: 5 秒的心跳间隔直接决定了 presence 服务器要扛多大的写入 QPS，30 秒的判定阈值决定了绿点最晚要多久才会真的变灰，这两个数字合在一起就是体验和服务器压力之间的折中。
消息正文最大长度是内容层面的限制，跟心跳间隔、离线判定阈值这两个连接管理相关的参数完全不是一回事。
群成员上限是群这个业务概念的容量限制，跟心跳频率和离线判定延迟没有直接关系。
存储保留年限决定的是数据能留多久，跟心跳这种连接层面的实时信号完全不在一个维度上。
optionExplanations_en: A 5-second heartbeat interval directly decides how much write QPS the presence server has to sustain, and the 30-second threshold decides how long the green dot can lag before actually turning gray — together they're the tradeoff between experience and server load.
Maximum message body length is a content-layer constraint, entirely unrelated to these two connection-management parameters of heartbeat interval and offline threshold.
Group member cap is a capacity limit on the group business concept, with no direct relationship to heartbeat frequency or offline-detection delay.
Data retention period decides how long data gets kept, on a completely different dimension from a connection-layer real-time signal like heartbeats.

scenario: 当前需求小群最多 100 人；后来产品想支持 10 万人直播群。
scenario_en: The current requirement caps groups at 100 members; later product wants 100,000-member live groups.
q: 消息分发方案要怎么变？
q_en: How should message distribution change?
options: 小群 inbox，大群 channel log
在超大群里也继续给每一个成员都复制一份消息
小群必须用全球广播
所有群都只能 SMS
options_en: Small groups use inboxes; large groups use channel logs.
Keep copying each message to every member even in huge groups
Small groups must use global broadcast.
All groups must use SMS only.
why: 100 人复制引用可控，10 万人复制会把每条消息放大成 10 万次写。大群更适合频道日志模型。
why_en: Per-recipient copies work for small groups, but huge groups need a channel log to avoid massive write amplification.
whenOtherWins: 如果大群只有极少数在线读者，按需读取优势更明显。

termDefinitions.meaning: 按频道保存的一份有序消息日志。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A channel log is one ordered message log stored per channel.

tradeoff: 小群读简单 vs 大群写放大
optionExplanations: 100 人以内继续用复制到每个人 inbox 的模型成本可控，但涨到 10 万人后，同样的复制思路会把一条消息放大成 10 万次写，这时候改成频道日志、大家按需读取才是出路。
大群继续给每个人复制一份消息，正是要避免的做法，10 万人复制会把写入压力放大到不可接受的程度。
小群没有必要强制用面向海量接收者设计的全球广播机制，那是为完全不同规模准备的方案，杀鸡用牛刀。
把所有群消息都通过 SMS 发送，跟聊天系统内部该怎么组织存储和分发完全是不同层面的问题，也不现实。
optionExplanations_en: Sticking with the copy-to-each-inbox model stays affordable under 100 people, but at 100,000 the same copying approach amplifies one message into 100,000 writes — switching to a channel log that people read on demand is the way out.
Continuing to copy a message to every member in a large group is exactly what needs avoiding — at 100,000 members that amplifies write pressure to an unacceptable level.
A small group has no need to be forced into a broadcast mechanism built for massive receiver counts — that's a solution meant for an entirely different scale, overkill here.
Sending every group message via SMS is a completely different concern from how a chat system should organize its internal storage and distribution, and isn't realistic either.

scenario: 文本消息允许最多 100000 字符；超大消息会影响队列、存储和 WebSocket 帧。
scenario_en: Text messages allow up to 100,000 characters; very large messages affect queues, storage, and WebSocket frames.
q: 入口应怎么处理大小限制？
q_en: How should the entry point handle size limits?
options: 发送前校验大小，超限拒绝或改附件路径
让任意大小直接进 WebSocket
只在接收端崩溃后报错
把大消息拆成无序碎片
options_en: Validate size before send and reject or move to an attachment path.
Send any size directly through WebSocket.
Error only after the receiver crashes.
Split into unordered fragments.
why: 大小限制要在入口挡住，避免大对象拖垮实时通道。若支持超长内容，应走附件/对象存储路径。
why_en: Validate message size at the entry so huge payloads do not overload the real-time path.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品需要文件或长文，设计专门上传和引用机制。

termDefinitions.meaning: WebSocket 连接上传输的一段消息数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WebSocket frame is a unit of message data sent over a WebSocket connection.

optionExplanations: 在消息真正进入队列之前先校验大小，超过 100000 字符就拒绝或者引导走附件路径，能避免一个超大对象拖垮队列、存储和 WebSocket 帧这些原本按普通消息设计的通道。
让任意大小的消息直接进 WebSocket，一旦真出现超大内容，会直接冲击这条本该轻量、低延迟的实时通道。
只在接收端崩溃后才报错，意味着这个超大消息已经一路走完了发送、存储、分发的全部流程才暴露问题，代价太大也太晚。
把大消息拆成无序碎片既没有解决大小限制的问题，无序的碎片到了接收端也没法正确重新拼装成原始内容。
optionExplanations_en: Validating size before a message ever enters the queue, rejecting or redirecting anything over 100,000 characters to an attachment path, keeps one oversized object from overwhelming channels — the queue, storage, and WebSocket frames — that were sized for ordinary messages.
Letting messages of any size straight into WebSocket means an oversized payload directly slams into what should be a lightweight, low-latency real-time channel the moment it appears.

Only erroring out after the receiving end crashes means the oversized message already made it all the way through sending, storage, and distribution before the problem surfaced — too costly and too late.
Splitting a large message into unordered fragments doesn't solve the size limit at all, and unordered fragments can't be correctly reassembled back into the original content on the receiving end.

scenario: A 和 B 几乎同时向同一群发消息；两个 chat server 的本地时钟有轻微偏差。
scenario_en: A and B send messages to the same group almost simultaneously; the two chat servers have slightly skewed clocks.
q: 排序不要只靠什么？
q_en: What should ordering not rely on alone?
options: created_at 时间戳
单调 message_id 或 channel sequence
同一 channel 的序列号
存储层排序键
options_en: created_at timestamps.
Monotonic message IDs or channel sequences.
A sequence number within the channel.
The storage sort key.
why: 服务器时钟可能冲突或倒退，created_at 只适合展示辅助。消息顺序应靠单调 ID 或会话内序列。
why_en: Server clocks can skew, so display order should not depend only on created_at timestamps.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是粗略排序历史日志，created_at 可能够用；聊天对话通常需要更稳。

termDefinitions.meaning: 不同机器时钟之间的偏差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Clock skew is the difference between clocks on different machines.

optionExplanations: 两台 chat server 的本地时钟本身就可能有轻微偏差，只靠 created_at 时间戳排序，A 和 B 几乎同时发的消息完全可能被排出错误的先后顺序。
单调递增的 message_id 或 channel 内的序列号不依赖本地时钟，能给出真正可靠的先后关系，是排序该真正依靠的东西。
同一个 channel 内的序列号正是应该依赖的排序依据，不在需要避免的范围内。
存储层排序键如果本身就基于单调 ID 或序列号，同样是可靠的排序依据，问题出在依赖时钟本身，不是存储层排序键这个概念。
optionExplanations_en: Two chat servers' local clocks can already have a slight drift, so relying only on created_at timestamps for order risks getting A and B's near-simultaneous messages sorted in the wrong sequence.

A monotonically increasing message_id or a within-channel sequence number doesn't depend on the local clock at all, giving a genuinely reliable ordering — exactly what sorting should actually rely on.
A sequence number within the same channel is exactly the kind of ordering basis that should be relied on, not something to avoid.

A storage-layer sort key, if it's itself built on a monotonic ID or sequence number, is just as reliable a basis — the actual problem is depending on the clock, not the concept of a storage-layer sort key.

scenario: 发送方想看到 sent/delivered/read 状态；接收方可能多设备在线。
scenario_en: The sender wants sent, delivered, and read states; the receiver may be online on multiple devices.
q: 这些状态怎么推进？
q_en: How should these states advance?
options: 落库算已发，ACK 算已送/已读
客户端发出即 read
push 发出就代表所有设备已读
不需要任何 ACK
options_en: Persisted means sent; ACK means delivered or read.
Mark read as soon as the sender sends.
A push send means every device read it.
No ACKs are needed.
why: sent 表示服务器接收并保存，delivered/read 必须来自接收端确认。多设备时还要定义任一设备还是全部设备算 delivered。
why_en: Sent can be server-side, but delivered and read require receiver acknowledgements with clear multi-device semantics.
tradeoff: 状态准确性 vs ACK 流量
whenOtherWins: 如果产品不展示回执，就可以只保留服务器持久化状态。

termDefinitions.meaning: 接收设备确认消息已送达的信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A delivery ACK is a signal that the receiving device got the message.

optionExplanations: 消息落库就代表服务器确实收到并保存了、算 sent，真正的 delivered 和 read 必须等接收端主动确认，多设备场景下还要明确定义是任一设备确认就算，还是要求全部设备都确认。
客户端刚一发出就直接算 read，完全跳过了服务器接收确认和接收端真正打开阅读这两个必要环节，状态会严重失真。
push 只是提醒通道，push 发出去了不代表用户在任何一台设备上真正打开并读到了这条消息，把它当成已读是错的。
不需要任何 ACK 意味着发送方永远不知道消息到底有没有真正送达和被读到，直接放弃了这几个状态该有的意义。
optionExplanations_en: A message landing in storage means the server actually received and saved it — that counts as sent; genuine delivered and read states have to come from the receiving end's own confirmation, and with multiple devices, it needs to be defined whether any one device confirming counts, or all of them must.
Marking it read the instant the client sends it skips both the server's receipt confirmation and the receiving end actually opening and reading it — badly misrepresenting the true state.
Push is just a notification channel — a push going out doesn't mean the user actually opened and read the message on any device; treating it as read is wrong.
Requiring no ACK at all means the sender never knows whether the message was actually delivered or read — it throws away the entire point of having these states.

scenario: service discovery 仍把新用户分配到一台 CPU 很高、连接数接近上限的 chat server。
scenario_en: Service discovery keeps assigning new users to a chat server with high CPU and near-max connections.
q: 发现服务要依赖哪些信号？
q_en: What signals should discovery use?
options: 健康检查、连接数、CPU/内存和地理位置
只看用户头像图片的分辨率高低和文件大小
短信供应商当前的每条报价
消息文本使用的语言种类
options_en: Health checks, connection count, CPU/memory, and geography.
Only the resolution and file size of user avatars
The current per-message price from SMS providers.
The language of the message text.
why: chat server 的瓶颈常是连接和资源，不只是进程活着。选择时还要考虑用户距离以降低延迟。
why_en: Discovery should route by health, capacity, and location rather than merely whether a process exists.

termDefinitions.meaning: 周期性检测服务实例是否可用的探测。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A health check periodically tests whether a service instance is usable.

optionExplanations: chat server 的真正瓶颈是连接数和 CPU/内存这些资源，再加上用户地理位置以降低延迟，把这些信号综合起来才能真正避免新用户被分到一台已经吃紧的机器上。
用户头像大小是内容层面的属性，跟一台 chat server 是否还有余量承接新连接毫无关系。
短信供应商报价是通知系统里的成本信息，跟挑选一台合适的 chat server 完全不搭边。
消息文本语言是内容层面的信息，不反映一台 chat server 当前的资源和连接压力。
optionExplanations_en: A chat server's real bottlenecks are connection count and CPU/memory, plus factoring in user geography to keep latency down — combining these signals is what actually keeps a new user from landing on an already-strained machine.
Avatar file size is a content-layer attribute, unrelated to whether a chat server still has headroom to accept new connections.
SMS provider pricing is cost information belonging to a notification system, entirely unrelated to picking a suitable chat server.
Message text language is content-layer information, unrelated to a chat server's current resource and connection pressure.

scenario: 聊天历史要永久保存，但最近消息最热，老消息主要用于搜索或偶尔回看。
scenario_en: Chat history is stored forever, but recent messages are hottest while old messages are mainly searched or occasionally revisited.
q: 冷热存储怎么分层？
q_en: How should hot and cold storage be tiered?
options: 近期热存储，老历史冷存储
把所有历史消息永远都放在内存里
老消息立即删除
只存最近一条消息
options_en: Hot storage for recent messages; cold storage for history.
Keep all history in memory forever
Delete old messages immediately.
Store only the latest message.
why: 访问分布强烈偏近期，冷热分层能控制成本。永久保存仍要求老数据可查，只是延迟可以高一点。
why_en: Because chat reads skew recent, tier hot messages separately from colder durable history.
tradeoff: 成本控制 vs 老历史访问延迟
whenOtherWins: 如果法规要求所有历史同等低延迟，冷层也要提高性能和成本预算。

termDefinitions.meaning: 最近或频繁访问的数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hot data is recent or frequently accessed data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 很少访问但仍需保存的数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cold data is rarely accessed but still retained.

optionExplanations: 近期消息访问最热，放在热存储保证低延迟；老消息主要用于偶尔搜索或回看，放进成本更低的冷存储，这样的分层能在保证永久保存的同时控制整体成本。
把所有历史永远放内存，成本会随时间无限增长，聊天历史动辄多年累积下来这个开销根本扛不住。
老消息立即删除跟“永久保存”这个前提直接矛盾，用户回看很久以前的对话会直接找不到。
只存最近一条消息意味着历史记录几乎不存在，用户没法翻看任何更早的聊天内容，完全不满足永久保存的要求。
optionExplanations_en: Recent messages get accessed the most and stay in hot storage for low latency, while older messages, mostly used for occasional search or lookback, move into cheaper cold storage — that tiering keeps things permanently retained while controlling overall cost.
Keeping all history in memory forever means cost grows without bound over time, and years of accumulated chat history simply can't sustain that expense.
Deleting old messages immediately directly contradicts the premise of permanent retention, leaving users unable to find conversations from long ago at all.
Storing only the most recent single message leaves almost no history at all — users can't scroll back through any earlier conversation, failing the permanent-retention requirement entirely.

scenario: 手机离线 2 小时后重连；期间收到 200 条消息。
scenario_en: A phone reconnects after two hours offline and received 200 messages during that time.
q: 补同步请求应带什么？
q_en: What should the catch-up request include?
options: 设备上次同步的 cursor/message_id
只带上设备当前的剩余电量百分比作为唯一的同步条件
最近一次 push 文案
好友头像 URL
options_en: The device’s last synced cursor or message_id.
Send only the current remaining battery percentage as the sole sync condition
The latest push copy.
Friend avatar URL.
why: 服务端用 cursor 查大于该位置的消息，返回缺口。没有 cursor 就只能粗暴全量拉取。
why_en: The server uses the cursor to fetch messages after the device’s last synced position.

termDefinitions.meaning: 设备离线或断连期间缺失的消息范围。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sync gap is the range of messages missed while a device was offline or disconnected.

optionExplanations: 服务端只要拿到设备上次同步到的 cursor 或 message_id，就能精确查出比这个位置更新的所有消息，把这 2 小时的缺口一次性补齐。
设备电量百分比跟服务端该从哪个位置开始补发消息毫无关系，用它当唯一条件根本查不出该补哪些消息。
最近一次 push 文案只是一条提醒的展示内容，不携带任何用来定位同步起点的信息。
好友头像 URL 跟这次要补拉的消息范围完全不相关，不能用来告诉服务端该从哪里开始同步。
optionExplanations_en: Once the server has the device's last-synced cursor or message_id, it can precisely query everything newer than that position, filling in the 2-hour gap in one shot.
Device battery percentage has nothing to do with where the server should resume sending from — using it as the sole condition gives no way to figure out which messages are missing.
The text of the most recent push notification is just display content for one alert — it carries no information for locating a sync starting point.
A friend's avatar URL is entirely unrelated to the range of messages that need catching up, and can't tell the server where to resume syncing from.

scenario: WebSocket 是长连接；如果握手时不校验身份，攻击者可以冒充用户占用连接。
scenario_en: WebSocket is long-lived; without authentication during handshake, an attacker can impersonate users and occupy connections.
q: WebSocket 连接建立时要做什么？
q_en: What should happen during WebSocket setup?
options: 握手校验 token 并绑定 user_id
连接后再让客户端随便声明 user_id
只检查 User-Agent
完全匿名连接所有功能
options_en: Validate token and bind user_id in handshake.
Let the client claim any user_id after connecting.
Check only User-Agent.
Allow all functionality anonymously.
why: 长连接后续消息都复用这次身份，所以握手校验很关键。token 过期也要有续期或断开策略。
why_en: Authenticate during the WebSocket handshake because later messages reuse that connection identity.
whenOtherWins: 公开聊天室可以允许匿名读，但发消息仍应有身份或风控。

termDefinitions.meaning: 证明客户端登录身份的令牌。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An auth token proves the client’s logged-in identity.

optionExplanations: 握手阶段就校验 token 并把这次连接绑定到确定的 user_id，之后这条连接上的所有消息都复用这个已确认身份，是防止有人冒充别人占用连接的关键一步。
连接建立后才让客户端随便声明自己是谁，攻击者完全可以在握手通过后随意冒充任意用户的身份继续使用这条连接。
User-Agent 只是客户端类型的自我声明，任何人都能随意伪造，不能作为身份校验的依据。
完全匿名连接所有功能意味着任何人都能不带身份地建立长连接并使用聊天的全部能力，安全风险极高。
optionExplanations_en: Validating the token and binding the connection to a definite user_id right at the handshake, so every subsequent message on that connection reuses this confirmed identity, is the key step preventing anyone from impersonating someone else on it.
Letting the client freely declare who it is only after the connection is established gives an attacker free rein to claim any identity once past the handshake.
